  old-french    6768/13572 (49.9%)

OE and ON should have rich form data — Anglo-Saxon dialect spelling variation is well-attested (tūn/tun/ton/toun etc.) and ON has gender/number/case-table forms. The wiktextract OE slice has 88% sounds coverage (per wyrd-xmk3 sampling); forms coverage is likely similarly rich.

Acceptance:
- mine-wiktextract-forms --apply runs on OE and ON slices
- etymon_text_match rows for OE / ON jump (target: OE ≥ 50% coverage matching middle-english)
- bundle's _variants pool surfaces these via the wyrd-1cjg variant-mining path
- Dashboard E row for OE / ON rises meaningfully

title: Thread sense-category → tag extraction through full wiktextract ingest
description:
The full ingest-wiktionary path (wiktextract_ingester._process_entry) extracts etymology, descent, pronunciation, original_script, transliteration — but NOT tags. The corpus-miner path (wiktextract_corpus_miner._write_one + _select_canonical_sense + _map_categories_to_tags) does extract tags from sense categories, but only touches etymons whose surface matches a place-name fragment.

Consequence: the wyrd-dxu2 modern-english slice ingest (PR #164) created ~1.4M new modern-english etymon rows, all of them tag-less. Dashboard now shows modern-english at C 2/15 (13.3%) reference-tag hits despite the slice having rich categories. Modern-english is 29.2% of bundle words — biggest single language — so this tag gap suppresses generation quality for the most-used language.

Fix path:
1. Promote _map_categories_to_tags to a shared module (or import it into wiktextract_ingester from wiktextract_corpus_miner)
2. In wiktextract_ingester._process_entry, after the etymon upsert, iterate senses and:
   - Apply _map_categories_to_tags to each sense's categories
   - db.add_tag(etymon_id, tag) for each mapped tag (INSERT OR IGNORE so re-runs are idempotent)
3. Add a 'tags_added' counter to the per-run summary
4. Re-run ingest-wiktionary --apply on the English slice (and ideally all other ingested slices for consistency)

Acceptance:
- modern-english tag coverage in DB jumps from 0.0% to a meaningful % (target: 30%+ on lemmas with senses+categories)
- Bundle's C row for modern-english jumps from 2/15 to 12+/15 reference-tag hits
- Per-run summary surfaces 'tags_added' counter
- Existing corpus-miner path's _write_one still adds tags (no double-counting; INSERT OR IGNORE handles it)
- 2232+ tests still pass
- Re-exported bundle's modifier_tags + per-language modifier_tags fields reflect the new tag coverage

Trade-off: full ingest writes tags on 1.4M English etymons; many of those have no senses (just etymology-template placeholders). Those rows would still be tag-less but the entries WITH senses would all get tagged. That's the right behavior.

title: Backfill IPA via ingest-wiktionary on existing European wiktextract slices
description:
The corpus-miner path (mine-wiktextract-corpus) only touches etymons whose surface matches an unaccounted place-name fragment — ~1% of OE etymons (4858 of 73871 after the wyrd-69s5 backfill in PR #159). The wiktextract slices already on disk (OE, ON, OF, ME, welsh, irish, scottish-gaelic, old-irish, middle-irish, breton, cornish, manx, proto-celtic) contain IPA in their sounds arrays for many entries the corpus miner never touches.

The FULL ingest path (wyrd kenning lexicon ingest-wiktionary <slice>) walks every entry in the slice via wiktextract_ingester._process_entry — which already extracts and writes pronunciation_ipa via _extract_pronunciation since wyrd-ha9q. It also handles etymology templates and descent edges.

Running ingest-wiktionary on the existing slices should:
1. Backfill IPA on existing etymons via COALESCE on upsert
2. Create new etymons for entries the corpus miner skipped
3. Add etymon_descent edges

Acceptance:
- Run ingest-wiktionary --apply on at least the OE + ON + OF slices
- Verify per-language IPA coverage jumps significantly in the lexicon table:
    target: OE from 1.0% to 50%+
    target: ON from 0.1% to meaningful %
    target: OF from 0.9% to meaningful %
- Re-export bundle so renderings.ipa surfaces the new IPA
- Dashboard rerun shows the lifts in Section H

Operational cost estimate:
- OE slice ~73K entries × ~50ms = ~1 hour per slice
- ON / OF similar
- All ~12 slices: several hours total, but can be incremental

Risk: full ingest does MORE than backfill IPA — it also writes descent edges. That may create new cluster connections that affect family rollup behavior elsewhere (e.g. the wyrd-vn09 grandfather audit). Worth doing dry-runs first to size the impact.

Separate from wyrd-dxu2 which is specifically about ACQUIRING a new modern-english wiktextract slice (since one isn't on disk).

title: IPA / pronunciation: 0% coverage on every shipped language; bundle ships empty renderings
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-09: user expected pronunciation data in generator output, found 'renderings: {}' on every component. Investigation shows the lexicon DB has zero IPA for every European / ancient language we ship:

    old-english:      0/73,871   0.0%
    middle-english:   0/54,250   0.0%
    irish:            0/34,204   0.0%
    welsh:            0/27,040   0.0%
    modern-english:   0/21,175   0.0%
    scottish-gaelic:  0/17,403   0.0%
    old-norse:        0/14,696   0.0%
    latin:            0/14,694   0.0%
    proto-germanic:   0/13,408   0.0%
    old-french:       (similar)

The 5% global IPA coverage is concentrated in non-European langs we don't ship (Arabic 23.6%, Persian 59.3%, Hebrew 19.5%). 

The data path is fully wired — etymon.pronunciation_ipa column exists, load_meanings parses it, NewName.components() emits a 'renderings' slot with an 'ipa' subslot, the SPA reads it. The pipe is empty all the way back to the source.

Causes to investigate (in priority order):

1. wiktextract ingest skipping the 'sounds' field on European-language entries. The mining path probably drops it. Fix: thread IPA through mine-wiktextract-corpus / mine-wiktextract-forms upserts.

2. Modern English Wiktionary has IPA on most entries — should give us 90%+ for modern-english. Lower-hanging fruit.

3. Old English / Latin / Old Norse on Wiktionary often DO have reconstructed IPA or at least 'pronunciation' notes — extracting these takes more parsing care but is doable.

4. SPA-side rendering: even with empty renderings, the panel should show 'pronunciation: not attested' or similar so the user knows it's a data gap, not a UI bug. Currently the empty {} is invisible.

Acceptance:
- Modern-english: at least 50% IPA coverage.
- Old-english: at least 20% (Wiktionary reconstructed IPA exists for a meaningful fraction).
- Spot-check 10 generated names from a re-emitted bundle: most components carry non-empty 'ipa' for modern-english parts.
- SPA: when renderings.ipa is absent, the pronunciation panel renders 'no IPA' rather than nothing.

title: Generator: drop citations from description() text — they're already in components for the SPA
description:
Bug surfaced 2026-05-09: NewName.description() inlines citation lists into the human-readable explanation text, producing dense walls like:

    -don- ( To do, perform (an activity) or CL contraction of do + an or EN dwellings...; cited by mawer_1920_northumberland_durham, wiktionary-empirical) -hole- ( hole or EN Dale, Hollow, Vale, Valley...; cited by ekwall_1922_lancashire, mawer_1920_northumberland_durham, mawer_stenton_1927_worcestershire (+4 more)) ...

The SPA already renders citations in a structured expandable component (the components() output carries 'citations' per part). The description() text should be the COMPACT human-readable summary — gloss block only, no citations.

Fix: strip the '; cited by ...' tail from NewName.description() output.

Sketch (proportions.py around line 762-780):
    # current:
    if citations:
        cite_block = f'; cited by {_format_citations_for_description(citations)}'
    else:
        cite_block = ''
    results.append(f'{head} ({gloss_block}{cite_block})')

    # fix:
    results.append(f'{head} ({gloss_block})')
    # citations stay in components() for the SPA's expandable box.

Acceptance:
- Sample 'wyrd kenning generate english --count 5' output's description lines no longer contain 'cited by'.
- components() output is unchanged (still carries citations per part).
- Existing tests pinning description format updated for the simpler shape.
- The CLI's own description text becomes scannable in the terminal.
notes:
ALSO: each etymon entry should be on its own line. Current
description() joins with ' ' (space) producing a wall of text.
Switch to '\n' so each '-foo- (gloss block)' is on its own
visible line in the CLI / SPA explanation panel.

Fix is one-line in NewName.description (proportions.py around
line 780):
    return " ".join(results)   # current
    return "\n".join(results)  # fixed

Acceptance addendum:
- 'wyrd kenning generate english --count 5' output: each part
  on its own line.
- The structured components() output is unchanged (it's a
  per-part list already; the join is purely for the human-readable
  text channel).

title: Generator: prevent same usage from being picked for adjacent slots within a name
description:
Bug surfaced 2026-05-09 in generated output post-wyrd-eni4 bundle: names like 'port port', 'les les Betton Kergan', 'Lowmall Lowy' have the SAME morpheme picked twice in adjacent slots (within a word, or across words). Independent per-slot sampling allows duplicates and the larger bundle has heavily-skewed buckets that surface dupes more often.

Root cause: proportions.NameGenerator._select_no_tag / _select_tags pick each slot independently via meaning_gen.select(...). No tracking of prior-slot usage. With the new bundle, certain buckets (especially location='inner' under the existing too-permissive semantics — see related ticket on inner) are dominated by a few high-frequency entries, so adjacent picks dupe.

Fix: track the prior slot's usage and re-roll if the new pick equals it. Cap re-rolls (e.g., 3 attempts) so tiny buckets don't infinite-loop.

Sketch:
    prev_usage = None
    for w in struct:
        for key in w:
            for attempt in range(3):
                picked = meaning_gen.select(...)
                if picked != prev_usage or picked is None:
                    break
            keys.append(picked)
            prev_usage = picked

Apply consistently across _select_no_tag, _select_tags. Determinism: re-rolls share the same RNG so seed-stability holds; the sequence of RNG calls changes vs prior, which is a one-time bit-shift acceptable for a quality fix.

Acceptance:
- New unit test: structure [(K,), (K,)] with a 1-element bucket — generator either re-rolls cap times then accepts the dupe, or returns one None. Document the chosen behaviour.
- Sample generation output: 100+ names per culture, no adjacent-identical-usage patterns.
- Tag-cooccurrence stats unaffected (proportions are corpus-derived; this fix is generator-only).

title: Dashboard: add bundle-level decomposition/attestation metric alongside DB-level
description:
The current language-quality dashboard (lexicon language-report) measures DB-level state — every etymon mined including unpromoted. This is useful as a curation signal ("50K rows of mining residue to consolidate") but misleading as a runtime-quality signal: the bundle is post-promotion, so what actually ships is a small well-attested subset.

Concrete confusion seen 2026-05-09 (post-wyrd-eni4 epic): user looked at dashboard, saw "many morphemes with almost no observations", then looked at actual generated output and found morphemes with 14-15 scholarly citations (-stone-, -curry). The dashboard alarm didn't match the empirical experience because they measure different layers.

Fix: add a parallel bundle-level metric alongside the DB-level one. Per-language report should include:

* DB level (current): total etymons, witnesses distribution, % below threshold
* Bundle level (NEW): subjects in bundle, citation distribution per subject, % rando-port-grandfathered, % wiktionary-empirical, % scholar-witnessed

The bundle-level metric is what tells you 'is your runtime output well-attested'. The DB-level metric tells you 'how much mining residue you have to clean up'. Both useful, currently conflated.

Implementation sketch:
- After lexicon export-meanings runs, compute bundle-level stats by walking subjects + citations
- Emit them in the JSON dashboard output under a 'bundle' key alongside 'lexicon'
- Markdown rendering: separate columns 'bundle subjects', 'bundle scholar-attested rate', 'rando-port grandfather %' alongside the existing DB columns

Acceptance:
- language-report --json has both 'lexicon' (existing) and 'bundle' (new) sections per language
- markdown view distinguishes the two
- a re-run after a bundle re-emit reflects the new bundle-level numbers (not stale)

title: Upgrade bundle era_reflexes schema to carry source tag (unblock Tier 4 in SPA)
description:
Surfaced by general-review BLOCKING finding on PR #146 (wyrd-98cs). Tier 4 (phonology-rule) era reflexes are currently filtered OUT of the bundle export at _fetch_root_era_reflexes because the bundle's era_reflexes field is shaped {lang: [form, ...]} — set semantics, no source tag. If we let Tier 4 reflexes through today they'd reach KenningRewind / SPA indistinguishable from human-vetted Tier 1 cluster mates.

To unlock the projected ~22pp time-travel coverage lift on the bundle / SPA, upgrade the schema:

Bundle field shape:
- Old: era_reflexes: {target_language: [form, ...]}
- New: era_reflexes: {target_language: [{form, source}, ...]}

Loader-side (meaning.py:load_meanings + Meaning.era_reflex_for):
- Detect shape (string entries = legacy, dict entries = new).
- Internal storage carries (form, source) tuples.
- era_reflex_for(target) keeps returning list[str] (back-compat).
- Add era_reflex_for_with_sources(target) → list[(form, source)] for source-aware consumers.

Export-side (lexicon.py:_fetch_root_era_reflexes + _emit_era_reflexes):
- Drop the Tier 4 filter at line 5895.
- Stamp full {form, source} dicts onto the bundle's era_reflexes field.
- Merge across linked families: dedupe on (form, source); when same form has multiple sources, keep the higher-quality source ('cluster' > 'descent' > 'period-form' > 'phonology-rule:v1').

Consumer-side (Phase 2 follow-on, OK to defer):
- KenningRewind / KenningEraMap surface source visually (e.g. italic for inferred forms; tooltip explaining 'derived via phonology rule').
- SPA component reads source field if present, falls back to plain form display otherwise.

Test plan:
- Loader handles legacy list-of-strings input correctly (back-compat).
- Loader handles new list-of-dicts input correctly.
- Bundle export emits new shape when Tier 4 fires.
- KenningRewind continues to render correctly with both shapes.

Audit context (wyrd-98cs review): blocks the user's headline 'real town names move forward and backward in time' question reaching the SPA. CLI path already works via direct etymon_era_reflexes calls; this ticket bridges to the bundle/SPA path.

title: Surface lexicon etymon_tag data into the bundle for languages without dedicated siblings
description:
Audit follow-up from wyrd-wzwa dashboard (2026-05-08): the bundle export drops semantic-tag data for languages without dedicated bundle siblings. Concrete: middle-english has 182 etymons with tags hitting 13/15 reference tag classes (architecture, topography, plant, animal, tree, water, etc.), but 0/15 of those reach the runtime bundle because there's no 'middle_english' sibling field. Same shape for modern-english (5 tagged etymons, 3/15 hit, 0/15 in bundle), early-modern-english, norman-french, old-irish, scottish-gaelic. Whatever bundle subject each of these etymons could attach to either doesn't exist (no rollup target) or strips the tag at export boundary.

Two implementation paths to scope (pick one in design):

Path A — schema additions: extend bundle subject shape to carry per-language tagged-etymon data. Add middle_english / modern_english / etc. siblings whose presence triggers the same subject-tag visibility logic that old_english enjoys today. Larger schema change but architecturally clean.

Path B — promotion-threshold relaxation for tagged etymons: if an etymon carries a tag in etymon_tag AND has a citation, surface it in the bundle as a tagged contribution to the relevant subject regardless of witness count. Smaller bundle export change. Risk: noise from low-quality tags polluting the runtime tag-cooccurrence statistics.

Acceptance:
- After fix + bundle re-emit (gated on wyrd-j43l), the language-quality dashboard's bundle_tag_hit_rate for middle-english reaches at least 13/15 (matches the lexicon-side reading).
- modern-english, old-irish, scottish-gaelic show non-zero bundle_tag_hit_rate.
- No regression on bundle subject count (the existing 1879 subjects stay).
- Tag co-occurrence proportions don't get poisoned by sparse-witness tag data — measure via test that compares pre/post tag_cooccurrence row counts and flags 10x+ growth.

This is part of the cleanup epic wyrd-eni4 (gated on the bundle dict-shape migration wyrd-c1vq + bundle re-emit wyrd-j43l).

title: Per-culture rebuild-proportions BETWEEN bundle re-export and Lambda deploy
description:
When meanings.json is re-exported (wyrd-j43l), the per-culture proportions JSONs (english_proportions.json, scottish_proportions.json, welsh_proportions.json, irish_proportions.json, breton_proportions.json) are derived from the bundle + place-names corpus. They MUST be regenerated to reflect the new morpheme inventory + tag distributions, otherwise the runtime samples from a stale empirical distribution.

Approach (per COVERAGE.md procedure):
```
for c in english scottish welsh irish breton; do
  .venv/bin/wyrd kenning rebuild-proportions "$c" \
    "wyrd/generators/kenning/data/${c}_place_names.json"
done
```
Each run regenerates {culture}_proportions.json + emits a 'culture=… perfect=… total=…' progress line on stderr that should be appended to COVERAGE.md as a new snapshot.

This ticket covers:
1. Run rebuild-proportions for all 5 cultures.
2. Append the new snapshot to COVERAGE.md (date + commit + table).
3. Verify tag_marginal + tag_cooccurrence are populated in each output (they're consumed by --cohesion).
4. Quick spot-check: post-rebuild perfect-rates should be ≥ pre-rebuild rates (more morphemes in the bundle → more decompositions land).
5. Single PR commit bundling all 5 proportions + the COVERAGE.md snapshot.

Gated on wyrd-j43l (bundle re-emit must land first; this is the proportions-side follow-up).

Audit context: wyrd-wl35. Part of epic wyrd-eni4.
notes:
Rolled into PR #208 (wyrd-j43l deploy refresh) merged at 2026-05-15T15:13:16Z.

All 5 cultures' proportions JSONs rebuilt against the new bundle + place_names corpus + --db ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db (canonical decomposition path):

| culture  | perfect | total  | rate    |
|----------|--------:|-------:|--------:|
| english  |   12383 | 17876  | 69.3%   |
| scottish |    1452 |  2321  | 62.6%   |
| welsh    |    1265 |  1916  | 66.0%   |
| irish    |   16417 | 34041  | 48.2%   |
| breton   |     183 |  1208  | 15.1%   |

Perfect-rates flat vs prior (wyrd-69s5) — the epic enriched existing morpheme subjects rather than adding new subjects. tag_marginal + tag_cooccurrence verified populated for all 5 cultures. COVERAGE.md snapshot added.

Sequence: ran BETWEEN bundle re-export and Lambda deploy as the ticket required.

title: Fantasy creature pipeline: runtime surface (KenningFantasy generator + SPA + CLI)
description:
The wyrd-ami fantasy creature pipeline is paper-only at the runtime layer: 1,308 fantasy_morpheme rows mined, 244 with full etymon_id linkage and descent chains (Angel→OE, Archon→ancient-Greek, Daemon→Latin), but no Generator class / SPA UI / public CLI consumes the data. Authoring works; the tap is closed.

Per D30's design intent: 'no new generator class needed — same temporal-axis machinery just works'. Architecturally correct, but the user has no way to invoke the flow. Three minimal moves to surface it:

1. Add KenningFantasy Generator class (or --mode=creature flag on existing Kenning). Reads fantasy_morpheme + etymon descent. Composes with KenningRewind for era-rendered creature names.
2. Bundle export path for fantasy_morpheme rows (subjects keyed by creature input_name, etymon_id linkage retained).
3. Public CLI: 'wyrd kenning render-creature Harpy' or similar.
4. SPA dropdown entry exposed via the manifest.

Audit context (wyrd-wl35): one of the highest-impact half-shipped surfaces in the project. Runtime layer is absent; backend is complete.

title: Bundle migration: array-shape → dict-shape to unblock joiners + canonical_decompositions
description:
meanings.json is currently array-shaped (legacy). Two shipped features are unreachable because of this:

1. wyrd-q0g6 joiners pool: Phase 1 schema + Phase 1.5 insertion code wired in proportions.py, but bundle export never populates the dict 'joiners' key. joiner_density knob is silent no-op.

2. wyrd-h8k1 canonical decompositions: Phase 3b shipped (PR #140) and KenningExplain projects canonical_decompositions when bundle is dict-shape, but load_canonical_decompositions returns {} on array-shape input.

The dict-shape pattern is the right forward-compat: emit dict-shape only when new fields have data, keep list-shape otherwise. Each loader (load_joiners, load_canonical_decompositions) defensively returns empty for list-shape input.

Approach:
1. Update lexicon.py:export_meanings to emit dict-shape {subjects: [...], joiners: {...}, canonical_decompositions: {...}} when joiners pool or canonical decompositions are present.
2. The runtime loaders already handle dict-shape (per the wyrd-h8k1 PR #140 work).
3. Bundle re-emit (wyrd-j43l) surfaces the change to SPA + Lambda.

Audit context (wyrd-wl35): two shipped features blocked on this migration. Re-using the dict-shape forward-compat pattern (memory: bundle-dict-shape-forward-compat).

title: Wire phonology_rules into etymon_era_reflexes as Tier-4 fallback
description:
The phonology rules library (wyrd/generators/kenning/phonology_rules.py) ships 4 complete sound-change cells (OE→ME, ME→EModE, EModE→ModE, OW→ModW) via PRs #131/#135/#141/#143 but is dead code — apply_rules() is never called outside the test suite. Integrating it as a Tier-4 fallback after period-form projection in etymon_era_reflexes() could close most of the current 61.3% time-travel coverage gap on bundle etymons WITHOUT any new mining. Highest-leverage idle capability surfaced by the 2026-05-08 end-to-end audit (wyrd-wl35).

Approach:
1. In lexicon.py:etymon_era_reflexes, after Tier 3 (period-form projection) returns empty, fall through to Tier 4: take the etymon's modern_canonical, route through apply_rules(form, language, from_era, to_era, mode='inverse') to surface ancestral forms; for forward-walking, route through mode='forward' to surface descendants.
2. Tag the result with source='phonology-rule:v1' so consumers can distinguish projection-from-real-attestation vs projection-from-rule.
3. Add quality dimension: phonology-rule-derived forms are weaker evidence than cognate-cluster mates; KenningRewind explainer should mark them differently.
4. Bundle re-emit needed (wyrd-j43l) to surface the new coverage to SPA.

Audit context (wyrd-wl35): 2026-05-08 audit found 38.7% of bundle etymons have era data today (Tier 1 cognate 27.2% + Tier 2 descent 10.9% + Tier 3 period-form 0.6%). Phonology-rule integration could plausibly raise this toward ~80-90% on the four cells covered (OE/ME/EModE/ModE chain + OW/ModW).

title: wyrd-n9x5 Phase 2.2: EModE → ModE sound-change cell
description: Fourth cell in the sound-change rules library (parent wyrd-4i6 / wyrd-n9x5). Roughly 5 hand-curated rules covering EModE → ModE place-name orthographic shifts. Most place-name orthography stabilized by EModE; the surfacing transitions are dominated by final-e drop on EModE-attested suffixes (-stocke, -brooke, -grene, -poole, -ditche) yielding their ModE forms. Parallel structure to Phase 2.1 (PR #135) and Phase 2.3 (PR #141): hand-curated rule set, per-rule exemplar tests, has_rules / dispatch / inverse / probability-sum tests, ME→EModE→ModE chain composition test.
notes: Phase 2.2 implementation complete. PR #143 ready for merge: CI green (1m27s), Gemini review no feedback, all 4 internal review agents (complexity / test-coverage / clarity / general) verdict ship. 5 rules, 16 new tests (108 in phonology suite, 2104 full suite). Awaiting user merge authorization (squash-merge gated by permission rule).

title: wyrd-08m Phase 3b: KenningExplain canonical surfacing via bundle projection
description:
Phase 3a (PR #136) wired the canonical pick into rebuild-proportions and the unaccounted miner. KenningExplain (Lambda / SPA path) was deliberately excluded because the Lambda has no DB access — the canonical decomposition lives only in the lexicon DB.

To surface canonical in KenningExplain (the user-facing decomposer), one of these has to happen:

(a) Project canonical_signature (and optionally canonical_source) into the bundle's per-name structure at export-meanings time, so the Lambda can read it without a DB. Cost: bundle size grows by 40 hex chars + a small label per toponym × ~7000 toponyms = ~300KB.

(b) Add a canonical-aware decomposition function that runs in the bundle context — but this requires the bundle to carry enough scholar/etymology data to compute canonical at runtime, which it does not.

Option (a) is the right call. Implementation:
1. Update lexicon export-meanings to emit a 'canonical' block per toponym carrying decomposition_signature + canonical_source for any toponym with a canonical pick.
2. Update KenningExplain.generate_all to honour the canonical block when present: sort the candidates dict so the canonical-signature reading appears first (or marked visually); show alternates as 'also possible'.
3. Tests: bundle export emits canonical for toponyms with a pick; KenningExplain marks canonical when bundle carries it; falls back to current heuristic-by-unaccounted-count sort when bundle lacks canonical.

Acceptance: KenningExplain output for a toponym with a canonical pick highlights the canonical reading and orders alternates beneath it.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #140. Bundle projects canonical_decompositions; KenningExplain marks + front-loads canonical reading; GenerationResult + envelope carry canonical/canonical_source fields.

title: wyrd-08m Phase 3: wire canonical pick into rebuild-proportions / unaccounted / explainer
description:
Phase 3 of wyrd-08m (parent ticket): consumer integration that turns the Phase 1 schema + Phase 2 refactor (wyrd-zpi9) into actual user-facing value.

Today the matcher's reduce=True heuristic still feeds:
- rebuild-proportions: counts morpheme frequencies via the heuristic pick → false-hits inflate frequencies, false-gaps under-count.
- unaccounted miner: surfaces fragments via the heuristic pick → false-gaps appear as 'corpus gaps' that authoring effort would target.
- KenningExplain: shows decomposition via the heuristic pick.

Phase 3 wires the canonical decomposition (toponym_decomposition.is_canonical=1) into all three:
1. rebuild-proportions reads the canonical pick when available; falls back to the heuristic when canonical is unset (e.g. multi-zero-tied not yet tiebreaker'd).
2. unaccounted miner reads the canonical pick — fragments that appear ONLY in the canonical decomposition's unaccounted_fragments are real gaps.
3. KenningExplain surfaces canonical visually (e.g. a marker) but shows alternates too — operators see the canonical pick + the disagreement context.

Acceptance criteria (from the parent wyrd-08m ticket):
- Coverage and gap reports use canonical-only counts.
- Re-running rebuild-proportions after a 'decompose --apply' run produces stable counts (no churn from arbitrary tiebreaks).

Dependencies:
- Requires Phase 1 + Phase 2 + the eventual rule (c) tiebreaker (Phase 4) for full coverage. Phase 3 can ship with rule (c) deferred; canonical-set just won't cover multi-zero ties until then.
notes: Phase 3a shipped via PR #136 (d86336b): rebuild-proportions + unaccounted miner --db wiring. KenningExplain canonical surfacing carved out to wyrd-h8k1 (needs bundle-side projection — Lambda has no DB access). Follow-ups: wyrd-8m87 (region plumbing), wyrd-0see (shared _decompose_corpus helper refactor).
close_reason: Phase 3a shipped via PR #136; explainer carved to wyrd-h8k1. Parent wyrd-08m remains open for rule (c) tiebreaker.

title: wyrd-4i6 Phase 2: ME→EModE→ModE cells + sporadic-weight rules
description:
Phase 2 of wyrd-4i6 (parent ticket): extend the sound-change rules library beyond the OE→ME cell shipped in Phase 1 (PR #131).

Cells to add:
- (english, middle-english, early-modern-english): roughly the Great Vowel Shift block (Sweet 1888 covers; ~20-30 rules).
- (english, early-modern-english, modern-english): post-GVS settling, final-e loss, modern orthography.
- (welsh, old-welsh, modern-welsh): ~20 rules per Morris-Jones 1913 / Lewis & Pedersen.

Plus refinements deferred from Phase 1:
- Sporadic-weight rules (weight<1.0) for transitions that aren't universal. Phase 1 framework supports them; Phase 2 mining surfaces the actual frequency data.
- Environment constraints (regex-based 'before front vowel', 'word-initial', 'in stressed syllable'). Phase 1 used literal patterns; ME→EModE has more context-dependent rules where this matters.
- Phase 1 limitation pinned in test docstring: short y → i fires on suffix-introduced y (e.g. -ley → -lei). Add a terminal-suffix protection mechanism so once -ley appears it stops further char-level rewrites.
- Attestation-weighted priors for inverse-mode 50/50 split. Phase 1 splits uniformly; Phase 2 mining could surface 'when ME has X, OE was Y 73% of the time' priors.

Acceptance criteria from parent ticket:
- 30+ rules for OE→ME→ModE forward chain.
- Inverse application of OE→ModE chain on 20 known test toponyms produces the attested OE form within top-3 candidates for >70% of cases.
- A test confirms apply_rules('Bridgewater', 'old-english', 'modern-english', mode='inverse') includes 'brycgwæter' or close variant in the candidate set.

Phase 1 (PR #131) shipped: framework + OE→ME cell + 28 rules + 55 tests. Phase 2 chains the cells together so 'modern-english' can route through ME via composition.
notes: Phase 2.3 (OW→ModW Welsh cell) shipped via PR #141. Phase 2.1 (ME→EModE) shipped via PR #135. Phase 2.2 (EModE→ModE) and Phase 2.4 (sporadic-weight rules + env constraints + restoration of dropped Phase 2.1 rules) remain. Phase 2.2 lower-priority (most place-name orthography stable by EModE).

title: wyrd-q0g6 Phase 1.5: generator-side joiner insertion (compose-time)
description:
Generator hook deferred from PR #130 (wyrd-q0g6 Phase 1):

Phase 1 shipped the matcher-side hook (Joiner sentinel + matcher-time consumption). The complementary GENERATOR-side hook lets compose-time output insert one joiner between adjacent picked morphemes, probability-gated like manorial_affix.

Concrete surface:
- New input_schema knob: `--joiner-density` (0..1, default 0).
- In Kenning.generate / NameGenerator structure walk: between adjacent picked morphemes whose families share a populated joiner pool, with probability=joiner_density, pick one joiner (weighted by attestation) and insert it between the morpheme surfaces. Emit a component for the joiner with location='joiner' so KenningExplain can round-trip it.

Caveats / scope:

title: wyrd-q0g6 Phase 2: audit 149 short subjects + populate joiners pool

title: wyrd-08m Phase 2: split pick_canonical_decomposition + add cross-product cap
description:
Phase 2 follow-ups deferred from PR #126 (wyrd-08m Phase 1):

1. **Refactor pick_canonical_decomposition**: ~80-line function fails the and/or test (loads rows + rebuilds slot candidates + runs rule (a) + runs rule (b)). Extract:
   - _build_slot_candidates_per_row(rows, word_db) -> list of slot lists
   - _try_rule_scholar(...) -> matching rows (or None)
   - _try_rule_unique_zero(...) -> matching row id (or None)
   Will become more important in Phase 2 when rule (c) tiebreaker lands and the function would otherwise grow another ~30 lines.

2. **Cross-product memory cap in compute_decompositions**: _cross_product_decompositions materializes the full Cartesian product before persisting. For multi-word toponyms with many per-word options the product can explode. Before the operator runs decompose --apply against the production 1.4M-row corpus, add either:
   - A per-toponym cap (e.g. 256 combos max; emit a warning + sample the rest)
   - OR streaming yield instead of materialize + persist incrementally

3. **Optional: log on _scholar_form_sequences silent drops**: today an etymon with an unmapped language code or NULL canonical_form is silently dropped from the scholar sequence. A one-line warning would surface the failure mode the next time it bites.

Phase 2 also wires the canonical pick into rebuild-proportions, the unaccounted miner, and the explainer (per the wyrd-08m parent ticket).
notes: SHIPPED via PR #132 (squash-merged 2026-05-08). Refactor + cap + log. Critical bug caught + fixed in review: original early-termination of cross-product loop emitted prefix-only combos. New per-word capping ensures all combos full-length. 49 tests, 1908 full-suite passing. title: toponym_attestation projection: derive per-etymon period forms
description:
Deferred from PR #114 (wyrd-rni Phase 3.1). The era-reflex picker covers 24% of OE toponym etymons via cognate-cluster + 4% via direct descent fallback (PR #110); ~72% remaining have neither cognate_id nor descent edges. Demo-name fallback rate is ~58% of morpheme×era slots.

Closing the gap via projection:
- toponym_attestation already carries 1,476 dated historical spellings keyed to 669 toponyms (PR #108 mining output).
- toponym_etymology_element gives per-toponym element ordering with surface_in_modern.
- For each toponym_attestation row, project the historical form's segments back onto the canonical breakdown's elements via prefix/suffix anchoring (last morpheme aligned to historical-form suffix).
- Aggregate across toponyms: each etymon gets a list of (historical_form, year, source) entries representing its surface at attested points in time.

Schema option A: new etymon_period_form table (etymon_id, form, date_year, source_doc).
Schema option B: extend etymon_variant with attested_year column.

Picker integration: extend etymon_era_reflexes with a Tier 4 fallback that consults projected period forms when cognate-cluster and descent both miss. Sort by year ascending; pick the form whose date_year falls in the target era cell's range.

Quality gates:
- Last-morpheme suffix-anchoring is high-precision (Hadenham → -ham, Bradford → -ford).
- First-morpheme prefix-anchoring is medium-precision.
- Middle-morpheme alignment is low-precision; skip for v1.

Empirical baseline: 1,476 attestations × ~2 segmentable morphemes ≈ ~3000 projected period-form rows. Coverage of the 1,507 isolated OE etymons probably reaches ~30-50% (the productive toponym suffixes show up everywhere).

Parent epic: wyrd-lm5m
Related: wyrd-4i6 (phonological-rule fallback — orthogonal path; rules are forward-derived, projection is backward-derived from attestations)

title: EraReflexProvider abstraction + bundle plumbing for SPA-side rewind
description:
Deferred from PR #114 (wyrd-rni Phase 3.1). The CLI rewinder works against a LexiconDB handle directly; the SPA needs an EraReflexProvider protocol abstraction so the same primitive can run on bundled data.

Why this is needed:
- wyrd/generators/kenning/rewind.py:rewind_name() takes a LexiconDB and runs raw SQL in two places (anchor lookup + era-reflex query).
- The Lambda runs on bundled data (importlib.resources). The lexicon DB is 673MB — won't fit in a Lambda layer.
- For SPA integration, era-reflex data must ship as part of the bundle.

Scope:
1. Define an EraReflexProvider protocol with two methods:
   - resolve_anchor(meaning: Meaning, sources_pref: tuple[str, ...]) -> Anchor | None
   - era_reflexes(anchor: Anchor, family: str, cell: str) -> list[EraReflex]
2. Implement LexiconDBProvider (current behavior, wraps lexicon.etymon_era_reflexes) — used by CLI.
3. Implement BundleProvider that reads era-reflex data from per-Meaning sibling fields on the bundle. Requires:
   - Bundle export: emit <lang>_era_reflexes per word entry with etymon_id + cluster_lang_form pairs
   - Runtime: parse the sibling into Meaning.era_reflexes; expose Meaning.era_reflex_for(family, cell) accessor
4. Refactor rewind_name to take an EraReflexProvider instead of LexiconDB; CLI passes LexiconDBProvider, SPA passes BundleProvider.
5. Register a Generator subclass (e.g. KenningRewind) using BundleProvider so the SPA's /api/generators endpoint surfaces the rewinder.

Best designed once wyrd-381 has shipped — both demos consume the same era-reflex shape, so the protocol's contract becomes evident once we have two callers.

Parent epic: wyrd-lm5m

title: wyrd-lr4 Phase 4d — manual stratum hand-correction CLI
description:
Phase 4d (the last Phase 4 follow-on per the umbrella). The classifier family (Welsh / French / OE / ON via Phase 4a-c) covers the bulk-classification path; Phase 4d is the operator escape hatch for high-stakes etymons the heuristic misclassifies.

## Design

New 'lexicon set-stratum' CLI subcommand:

  wyrd kenning lexicon set-stratum --etymon-id 12345 --stratum latin-loan
  wyrd kenning lexicon set-stratum --canonical-form caer --language welsh --stratum latin-loan
  wyrd kenning lexicon set-stratum --etymon-id 12345 --clear

Inputs (mutually-exclusive identification):
- --etymon-id INT — direct row identifier
- --canonical-form + --language — pair lookup; must resolve to exactly one row

Stratum specification:
- --stratum STR — must be in ALL_STRATA (union of WELSH/FRENCH/OE/ON tuples) for typo protection
- --clear — sets stratum to NULL (--stratum and --clear are mutually exclusive)

Output to stderr:
- 'etymon N <canonical_form, language>: <old_stratum> → <new_stratum>' so the operator can verify

## Validation

- Exactly one of {--etymon-id, --canonical-form+--language} required
- --stratum and --clear mutually exclusive (one required)
- Stratum value validated against ALL_STRATA frozenset (catches typos)
- Cross-family strata (e.g. setting 'native-welsh' on a french etymon) are NOT blocked — operator's responsibility; these may legitimately surface during edge-case correction
- Canonical-form ambiguity (multiple matches across languages with the same form) → error listing candidates
- Missing etymon → error

## Out of scope

- Bulk corrections file (operator can script multiple --etymon-id calls)
- Audit trail / log of changes (stderr line is the audit trail)
- wyrd-j3gy validator + SPA culture gating (separate ticket)

## Tests

~12 tests:
- set by id (happy path)
- set by canonical-form + language (happy path)
- both id and form+lang → error
- neither → error
- form-only without language → error
- canonical-form ambiguity → error with candidates
- etymon doesn't exist → error
- unknown stratum → error
- --clear sets to NULL
- --clear + --stratum mutex → error
- previous-stratum reported in stderr line
- --apply path for full DB stratum write doesn't blow this away (idempotency check)

Estimated 250-300 lines.

Includes warn-and-proceed for merged-cluster losers. 22 new strata tests cover happy paths, all error paths, --clear semantics, end-to-end idempotency, cross-family writes, merged-row warning. title: wyrd-lr4 Phase 3 — generator --stratum filter consumes the loaded data
description:
Phase 3 of wyrd-lr4 (within-language stratum tagging).

Phase 1 (PR #105) shipped the schema/classifier/CLI. Phase 2 (PR #107) plumbs stratum through the bundle export so Meaning.stratum_for(lang_field, form) returns the tag at runtime. Phase 3 wires the generator filter so users can actually use it.

Plan, mirroring the established --era filter pattern (D5-2 / wyrd-lyp):

1. Meaning.in_stratum(stratum: str | None) -> bool — analogous to attested_in_era_range. Returns True when stratum is None (no filter), when self.stratum is empty (treated as 'always include' — same convention as era for 'no data → pass'), or when any of self.stratum.values() contains the requested tag for any form.

2. MeaningGenerator.keep_keys_for_stratum(stratum) -> frozenset[str] | None — mirrors keep_keys_for_era. Cache by stratum tag. Returns None when stratum is None or when the keep-set covers the full meaning_db (full-coverage fast path, same bit-stable invariant as era).

3. Proportions.select gains a stratum: str | None = None param. Compose era_range + stratum keep_keys: if both are non-None, frozenset intersection; if one is None, use the other. Threaded down to Generator.select via the keep_keys arg unchanged.

4. CLI: add --stratum to wyrd kenning generate (cli.py near --era around line 262). Validate against the loaded vocabulary at runtime so a typo fails loud.

5. Kenning.generate (or whatever orchestrator sits between cli.py and Proportions.select) needs the param threaded through.

6. Tests:
   - Meaning.in_stratum: present (in lang's stratum dict) / missing-from-lang / missing-from-form / empty-stratum-data passthrough / None-filter passthrough.
   - keep_keys_for_stratum: returns None on None input; returns None on full-coverage; returns subset on partial; cache hit.
   - Proportions.select: stratum-only filter; era + stratum intersection; stratum=None bit-stable with no-arg.
   - CLI: --stratum welsh:native-welsh actually narrows the bundle pool (smoke test against rebuild-proportions or a fixture).

Granularity caveat (same as era): filtering happens at the USAGE level, not the SENSE level. A usage with two senses (one in-stratum, one out) stays in the pool; the downstream pick at NameGenerator._pick_surface picks meanings[0]. Documented for era; carry forward verbatim.

Out of scope for Phase 3:
- Per-form filtering within a Meaning (would need NameGenerator._render_substitutions reworked).
- French / Old English / Old Norse classifiers (Phase 4).
- Manual hand-correction CLI for misclassified etymons.
