title: wyrd-ami: capture IPA pronunciation + derive English-shaped renderings for non-Latin etymons
description:
Per user 2026-05-06: when an etymon comes from a non-Latin-script language (Hebrew, Arabic, Egyptian, Sanskrit, etc.), the canonical_form alone is insufficient for English town-name generation. We need both the academic transliteration AND an English-phonotactic rendering so generated names are pronounceable to native English speakers.

Two-phase implementation:

## Phase 1: Capture IPA at ingest time (cheap)

Wiktextract entries already contain a 'sounds' array with IPA strings, e.g.:
  {'sounds': [{'ipa': '/d͡ʒɪnː/', 'tags': ['Modern Standard Arabic']}, ...]}

The current wiktextract_ingester.py discards this. Plumb it into the etymon table.

Schema change:
- Add etymon.pronunciation_ipa TEXT (nullable). Optionally also a pronunciation_dialect TEXT to distinguish multiple IPA variants when present (Modern Standard Arabic vs. Egyptian Arabic, Old vs. Middle Egyptian, etc.).
- Migration: nullable so existing rows don't need backfill.

Ingester change:
- wiktextract_ingester.py picks the most authoritative IPA from the sounds array (first one with no dialect tag, falling back to the first overall).
- Empirical mining helpers (lexicon mine-wiktextract-corpus) plumb the same.

## Phase 2: English-shaped derivation (the harder part)

For each non-Latin-language etymon with IPA, derive an English-spelled rendering using English phonotactic rules. Roughly:

1. Map IPA phonemes to closest English phonemes:
   - Arabic ʿayin /ʕ/ → silent or 'a'
   - Arabic ḍād /dˤ/ → 'd'
   - Hebrew ḥet /ħ/ → 'h' or 'kh'
   - Egyptian aleph /ʔ/ → silent
   - Sanskrit retroflex ṭ /ʈ/ → 't'
   - etc.

2. Map English phonemes to English spellings using mainstream conventions:
   - /ʤ/ → 'j' (initial), 'g' (before e/i)
   - /k/ → 'c' (before a/o/u), 'k' (before e/i, finally)
   - Long vowels → magic-e or doubled-vowel patterns
   - /ʃ/ → 'sh'
   - etc.

3. Output the English-shaped form alongside the canonical academic transliteration.

Examples from PR #83's wave-2 entries:
  Arabic jinn /ʤɪnː/         → 'Jinn' (English-shaped) + 'jinn' (academic) — same in this case
  Arabic ʿifrīt /ʕifriːt/    → 'Ifrit' (English-shaped, ʿayin silenced) + 'ʿifrīt' (academic)
  Egyptian inpw /ɪnpw/       → 'Anpu' or 'Anep' (English-shaped, vowels guessed) + 'inpw' (academic)
  Hebrew gōlem /ɡoːlɛm/       → 'Golem' (English-shaped) + 'gōlem' (academic)
  Sanskrit rakṣasa /rɐkʂɐsɐ/ → 'Rakshasa' (English-shaped retroflex→s) + 'rakṣasa' (academic)

Generation pipeline integration:
- Realistic-mode names: prefer the English-shaped form (modern register).
- Archaic/scholarly mode: use the academic transliteration.
- Could expose both as a generation option ('register=english_modern' vs 'register=scholarly').

## Caveats

- IPA → English-phoneme → English-spelling has many-to-many mappings; needs heuristic + confidence rating. Some etymons probably need a hand-curated override.
- For Egyptian especially (no native vowels in hieroglyphs), Wiktionary's IPA may be conjectural. Mark these with lower confidence.
- For Sanskrit / Arabic / Hebrew, the established English forms (rakshasa, jinn, golem) should win over rule-derived forms. Could load a small known-form lookup table that overrides the rule output for canonical creature names.
- Already-Latin-script languages (Latin, Greek, OE, etc.) probably don't need this — Latin → English orthography is well-known and the canonical_form is usually fine. Scope this to non-Latin-script source languages.

## Scope clarification

NOT included in this ticket:
- Phonotactic-aware joining for compound town names (different concern; town-generation has its own pipeline).
- Full TTS synthesis (out of scope; we only need the spelling).

User-facing impact: town names like 'Anpu Hollow', 'Jinn Reach', 'Rakshasa Crossing' read natively to English readers, while the underlying etymological provenance is still preserved in the academic transliteration field.
notes: Phase 2b started 2026-05-07: english_shaped derivation rules + CLI backfill, on branch wyrd-ami/english-shaped-derivation. Generator + SPA integration deferred to later PRs.

title: wyrd-ami: re-ingest wiktextract for Semitic / Egyptian / Indo-Iranian language slices
description:
Part of EPIC wyrd-ialp (wave-2 language etymon corpus expansion). FIRST to implement per user 2026-05-06.

The wiktextract_ingester (wyrd/generators/kenning/wiktextract_ingester.py) already supports any language code — codes pass through as-is. The bottleneck is operational: the slices we actually RAN it against were targeted at British Isles place-name ancestry (Germanic, Celtic, Romance, Greek/Latin). The wave-2 dumps were never ingested at scale.

What to do:

1. Download the relevant wiktextract slices from kaikki.org. Each language has a per-language extract:
   - Hebrew: kaikki.org/dictionary/Hebrew/kaikki.org-dictionary-Hebrew.jsonl (or similar)
   - Arabic: kaikki.org/dictionary/Arabic/...
   - Persian: kaikki.org/dictionary/Persian/...
   - Akkadian: kaikki.org/dictionary/Akkadian/...
   - Egyptian (Ancient Egyptian): kaikki.org/dictionary/Egyptian/...
   - Aramaic: kaikki.org/dictionary/Aramaic/...
   - Middle Persian / Pahlavi: kaikki.org/dictionary/Middle_Persian/...
   - (Sanskrit already has 12,456 — verify it doesn't need re-ingestion.)

2. Run lexicon mine-wiktextract or whichever ingester is current against each dump. Verify _WIKTIONARY_LANG_CODE_MAP correctly canonicalizes the codes (he, ar, fa, akk, egy, arc, pal — should all pass through correctly per the existing 'unmapped passes through' contract).

3. Re-mine the pfsrd2 corpus (with --skip-resolved disabled or via approach_version bump) and verify previously attested_but_not_in_corpus entries (Jann, Kanya, Anpw, etc.) now resolve usable via descent_walking_lookup.

Expected impact: should rescue most of the ~140 attested_but_not_in_corpus rows from the 2026-05-06 mine. Each language probably grows from ~few-hundred to ~10k+ entries (matching the IE language coverage).

Caveats:
- Wiktionary's coverage of these languages is uneven. Hebrew likely good (lots of biblical scholarship), Egyptian probably weakest (small Wiktionary editor pool).
- Some lemmas may need transliteration normalization. The ingester should handle this transparently but verify e.g. that 'jinn' in Latin script and 'جن' in Arabic script both land correctly.
- No new ALLOWED_LANGUAGES code change needed — PR #83 already approved these.

Trust level: HIGH — same authoritative data source as the rest of our corpus.
notes: PR #94 opened. Wave-2 wiktextract ingest yielded etymon counts of ar 709->64698, fa 752->20242, he 425->15220, egy 131->4343, arc 227->2696, akk 217->1614, pal 384->1005. Rescue mine of 210 attested_but_not_in_corpus rows recovered 26 (12.4%) -> fantasy_morpheme usable 218->244. Remaining 143 are anchor-form mismatches (Phase 2 wyrd-ha9q target). Added 16 precursor/postcursor codes per user 2026-05-06 sign-off.

title: EPIC: wave-2 language etymon corpus expansion
description:
Goal: bring our etymon table coverage for the wave-2 languages (Hebrew, Arabic, Persian, Sanskrit, Akkadian, Egyptian, Aramaic, Pahlavi/Middle Persian) up to a level where wyrd-ami's descent_walking_lookup pre-filter actually resolves morphemes in those languages, instead of falling through to the LLM and bouncing on attested_but_not_in_corpus.

Empirical baseline 2026-05-06 (post-PR #83 wave-2 approval):
  Well-covered (5,000+ entries each):
    old-english 73,871 / ancient-greek 64,637 / middle-english 54,232 /
    modern-english 19,128 / old-norse 14,694 / latin 14,208 /
    proto-germanic 13,406 / sa (Sanskrit) 12,456 (the outlier!) /
    proto-indo-european 12,003 / old-french 10,898

  Sparse (under 1,000 — bottleneck for wave-2):
    fa (Persian) 752 / ar (Arabic) 709 / he (Hebrew) 425 /
    pal (Middle Persian) 384 / arc (Aramaic) 227 /
    akk (Akkadian) 217 / egy (Egyptian) 131

The wiktextract ingester (wiktextract_ingester.py) supports these
languages — codes pass through as-is — but the slices we've actually
RUN it against were targeted at British Isles place-names (Germanic /
Celtic / Romance / Greek/Latin). The Semitic / Egyptian / Indo-Iranian
dumps were never ingested at scale.

Implementation order per user 2026-05-06 (cheapest first, lowest-trust
last):

1. **wyrd-3wt (re-ingest wiktextract)** — same data source, broader
   slice coverage. Authoritative trust level.
2. **wyrd-h7e (dedicated dictionary parsers)** — Klein's Hebrew,
   Lane's Arabic, Faulkner's Egyptian, Hans Wehr Modern Arabic, etc.
   Higher fidelity but per-source parser cost.
3. **wyrd-hgg7 (LLM-driven backfill)** — convert existing
   attested_but_not_in_corpus rows into etymons using the LLM finding
   and citation. Lowest trust — final sweep of what 1+2 missed.

User-facing impact: until at least wyrd-3wt lands, wave-2-language
creature names (Djinni, Ifrit, Marid, Kanya, Rakshasa-variants, Anpw,
Lammasu, Tiamat) will mostly bar as attested_but_not_in_corpus
instead of resolving usable. The PR #83 language approvals are
necessary but not sufficient.

title: wyrd-ami: backfill etymon corpus from attested_but_not_in_corpus rows
description:
Pattern surfaced 2026-05-06 during the v2 pfsrd2 re-mine: many entries in the new variant tier resolve to a real attested historical form in an APPROVED language, but our wiktextract-derived etymon corpus doesn't have a row for that (form, language) pair. They get bar_reason='attested_but_not_in_corpus' rather than 'outside_language_family'.

Examples from the 2026-05-06 mine (250/395 in):
- Jann → Arabic (citation: Wiktionary). 'ar' is approved, just not in our corpus.
- Kanya → Sanskrit (citation: Monier-Williams Sanskrit-English Dictionary). 'sa' is approved.
- Triceratops, Velociraptor, Tyrannosaurus → Ancient Greek (citation: LSJ). 'ancient-greek' is approved.
- Many more (143+ already in this category mid-mine).

Why: This is a different problem than 'language not approved' (PR #83 fixed that wave). These are 'language approved + LLM knows the etymon + our wiktextract dump just doesn't have this specific lemma'. The fantasy_morpheme row already records:
- unapproved_form (the historical form the LLM identified)
- citation (the source the LLM cited)
- attested_in (the language code, after PR #83's alias map)

Fix shape: Build a backfill tool that:
1. SELECT input_name, unapproved_form, attested_in, citation, reasoning
   FROM fantasy_morpheme WHERE bar_reason = 'attested_but_not_in_corpus'
   AND approach_version = current
2. For each row, INSERT into etymon (canonical_form=unapproved_form, language=attested_in, source=citation_or_'wyrd-ami-llm-backfill')
3. Re-run mine-fantasy-name --skip-resolved=false (or bump approach_version) over ALL the previously-attested_but_not_in_corpus inputs to rewrite their fantasy_morpheme rows as usable with etymon_id linked to the new etymon row.

Or alternatively: the descent-walking pre-filter can be taught to query the etymon table after the new rows are inserted — re-running with --skip-resolved=false on the previously-barred-as-attested-but-not-in-corpus subset is enough.

Effect: would convert roughly half the current barred entries to usable without any new language approvals. Empirical at the time of filing: 143 of 214 barred entries in the in-flight mine could potentially be rescued this way.

Caveats:
- LLM-identified forms have lower trust than wiktextract-attested ones. Probably worth tagging these etymon rows with source='wyrd-ami-llm-backfill' or similar so realistic-mode generation can filter them out.
- Need to handle the 'descent_walking_lookup' angle: a backfilled etymon with no descent edges into modern English might not be useful for town-name generation in modern register. Either accept and filter at generation time, or backfill descent edges via a second LLM pass.
- The LLM's citation is the audit trail; a future pass could verify against the actual cited source (Wiktionary, Monier-Williams, LSJ, etc.).

title: pfsrd2-data → wyrd-ami JSONL extractor for fantasy-name pipeline input
description:
Walks ~/521Studios/pfsrd2-data/monsters/ trees, extracts (name, description) tuples for the wyrd kenning lexicon mine-fantasy-name --batch input, dedupes by family root.

Extraction rules (verified via schema audit 2026-05-06):
- monster JSON shape: `name` (full creature name), `stat_block.creature_type.family` (optional, has .name + .text + nested .sections), `sections` (recursive tree, each node has .text).
- input_name: prefer family.name.split(',')[0] (strip subtype like 'Dragon, Red' → 'Dragon'); fallback to top-level name when no family AND name is single-word; skip multi-word no-family names ('Ancient Black Dragon' would be input ambiguity).
- description: concatenate family.text + all family.sections recursive .text + monster sections[] recursive .text. Family lore is often the richest source (Troll's per-variant section is empty; family.text has the full lore).
- Dedupe by lowercased input_name across the whole corpus before emitting JSONL.

CLI: `wyrd kenning lexicon extract-pfsrd2-monsters <root> [--output PATH] [--limit N]`. Stdout JSONL by default. Pipes into mine-fantasy-name --batch.

title: Etymonline scraper + ingester for Latin/OFr/ME etymological intermediates
description:
Second sub-ticket of wyrd-gpif. Etymonline's per-entry pages trace the Latin → OFr → ME → modE chain explicitly (e.g., 'harpy: late 14c., from Old French harpie (14c.), from Latin harpyia, from Greek Harpyia'). Wiktionary often skips these intermediates. Adding Etymonline as a parallel etymological-citation source would fill the gap.

Work: (a) scraper for etymonline.com per-entry HTML (respect robots.txt + rate limits), (b) parser for the 'from X (Yc.), from Y, from Z' chain shape, (c) ingester producing missing-intermediate etymon rows + descent edges + citation rows tagged source='etymonline', (d) re-run with a focus list (start with English-history words only, ~5K entries).

Output also gives the LLM-research step in wyrd-ami a 'cite Etymonline' option that's short and authoritative.

title: Ingest wiktextract `forms` arrays as etymon_variant rows
description:
First sub-ticket of wyrd-gpif. Wiktextract data already includes a `forms` array per lemma with semantic tags (`alternative`, `inflection`, `dative_or_pl`, `romanization`, etc.) — but our wiktextract_ingester.py drops it. Adding a new etymon_variant table and ingesting these would surface inflectional variants (Greek ἁρπυίᾱς) AND alternative spellings (ME 'harpe' alt 'harp') so pre-filters and LLM-research steps can resolve historical spellings against the canonical lemma.

Schema: etymon_variant(etymon_id, form, variant_class, tags JSON, romanization, attested_period UNIQUE (etymon_id, form, variant_class)).

Work: (a) extend wiktextract_ingester.py to walk `forms`, (b) add etymon_variant table + migration, (c) re-ingest the 28 wiktextract_*.jsonl files we already have on disk, (d) update lookup helpers (the descent-walking pre-filter, mining match heuristics) to join etymon_variant.

Should yield 200K-500K new variant rows on top of the existing ~500K etymon rows. No new corpus needed; data is already on disk.

title: Etymology corpus improvement epic: alt-forms, Etymonline, descent gaps
description:
Found during wyrd-ami Phase 1 spike (2026-05-05): our wiktionary-derived etymon corpus has two consistent gaps that hurt etymological lookups, especially for fantasy/literary morphemes.

GAP 1 — Wiktextract `forms` arrays not ingested. Every Wiktionary lemma's wiktextract record has a `forms` array with semantic tags ('alternative', 'inflection', 'dative_or_pl', 'romanization', 'archaic', etc.). The current ingester drops it. So we miss inflectional variants (Greek ἁρπυίᾱς genitive) AND alternative spellings (ME 'harpe' alt 'harp'). The data is on disk in sources/wiktextract_*.jsonl files; no new corpus needed.

Proposal: new table etymon_variant(etymon_id, form, variant_class, tags JSON, romanization, attested_period). Backfill all 50K+ existing wiktextract-derived etymon rows. Pre-filters and LLM-research steps would then resolve via etymon_variant.form OR etymon.canonical_form, surfacing historical spellings even when the modern lemma is the only first-class row.

GAP 2 — Etymonline isn't ingested at all. Etymonline traces the Latin → OFr → ME → modE chain explicitly (e.g., harpy: 'late 14c., from Old French harpie (14c.), from Latin harpyia, from Greek Harpyia'). Wiktionary often skips these intermediates: our DB has ancient-greek ἅρπυια → modern-english harpy with NO Latin/OFr/ME intermediates, even though Wiktionary's harpy entry mentions all of them in prose. Etymonline's per-entry HTML is structured enough to scrape into a parallel etymological-citation source.

Proposal: separate ingester reading scraped etymonline pages, producing both etymon rows for missing intermediates AND citation rows that the LLM-research step can echo back. (Note: respect their robots.txt + rate limits.)

GAP 3 — Wiktionary's coverage of Middle English is incomplete for borrowed words. ME 'harpie'/'harpye'/'arpie' isn't in wiktextract_middle_english.jsonl at all; OFr 'harpie' isn't in wiktextract_old_french.jsonl. This is a Wiktionary-data gap not solvable by re-ingesting. Etymonline (gap 2) is the partial-fix path.

Sub-tickets to file under this epic:
- Ingest wiktextract `forms` arrays into etymon_variant table + descent-aware pre-filter
- Etymonline scraper + ingester
- Re-thread the alt-form lookup into wyrd-ami fantasy pipeline (depends on #1)

Discovery context: this surfaced while building wyrd-ami Phase 1. Found that 'harpy' resolves to ancient-greek ἅρπυια via descent edges (good), but the Chaucer-era ME spelling 'harpie' isn't anywhere in our corpus (bad). User noted Etymonline traces the chain we're missing.

title: Refine empirical Wiktionary mining: filter noise + re-export to surface high-impact morphemes
description:
Discovered during PR #68 review (https://github.com/521-studios/wyrd/pull/68#issuecomment-4381510998): the committed bundle doesn't include several high-impact empirical morphemes (eglwys, betws, coch, cluain, demesne) despite their lexicon DB rows + reflex links existing. Reason: the committed bundle is the output of the FIRST empirical mining pass (pre-prefix/suffix expansion); the second-pass entries didn't get re-exported cleanly.

A naive re-export NOW produces 8596 subjects (vs 1879) and would push English to ~70% perfect-rate, but 7964 of those subjects are 3-4 char modern_usages from prefix-substring matches. Many are noise (-aac, -aba, -abc-, -abit-, -abla, etc.) and inflate the perfect-rate spuriously.

What needs to be done:

1. Add a min-length floor on empirical canonical_forms (length ≥ 5 most likely; tunable). This drops ~5000 noise entries while keeping eglwys (6), betws (5), coch (4 — borderline), demesne (7), cluain (6).
2. Add an attestation gate: only admit empirical entries that match ≥N place names in the relevant culture's corpus (proves the morpheme actually contributes to coverage). Without the attestation gate, every Wiktionary headword that's a substring of any place name gets in regardless of whether it materially helps.
3. Add a sense-quality filter: drop entries whose only sense is 'alternative form of X' (the redirect chain we deferred in wyrd-4hx7).
4. Re-export, re-rebuild-proportions, snapshot to COVERAGE.md.

Acceptance: post-refine bundle should have between 2000 and 4000 subjects (target middle ground), with eglwys/betws/coch/cluain/demesne all present, and the noise-floor short surfaces dropped. Net perfect-rate lift over current 35.1% English target: 5-10pp realistic, vs 35pp inflated by noise.

Closes the gap COVERAGE.md describes as 'didn't land in this pass'.

title: Anglicized-form mapping: lift Irish coverage by mapping corpus forms to native morphemes
description:
The Irish place-name corpus uses ANGLICIZED morphemes (cloon, bally, agh, aun, lagh, nag) — not the native Irish forms (cluain, baile, achadh, etc.) that Wiktionary indexes as headwords. Confirmed in the wyrd-4hx7 diagnostic: cloon=735 unaccounted hits, agh=2498, bally and others similar; none of these surface as Wiktionary headwords in the ga/sga/mga slices.

Two paths to lift:
(a) Explicit anglicization map: cloon→cluain, bally→baile, agh→achadh, aun→áin, lagh→lacha?, etc. Curated table — small (maybe 50-100 entries) but high impact.
(b) Mine Wiktionary's modern-English slice (not yet on disk) — has entries for 'cloon-' / 'bally-' as English place-name elements with cross-references to Irish etyma.

Either path lifts irish perfect-rate substantially (the 5805/34041 = 17.1% post-wyrd-4hx7 number is heavily bottlenecked by these specific anglicized morphemes — each high-frequency miss represents 100s-1000s of place names).

See the wyrd-4hx7 PR description + COVERAGE.md for the diagnostic numbers.

title: Joiner schema: top-level joiners field + matcher hook + audit 149 short subjects
description:
From the wyrd-4hx7 design discussion: the bundle currently has 149 subjects with 1-2 char modern_usage (-en-, -m-, -y-, -ar-, -bo-, etc.). Some are real grammatical morphemes (OE genitive -en-, ON -by); others are phonological joiners disguised as morphemes. Empirical evidence: removing all <3-char usages drops English perfect rate by 6.1pp — they're load-bearing but conflated.

Proposal: introduce a top-level 'joiners' field in meanings.json keyed by language family, carrying phonological connectors with attestation weights. Matcher consumes them during extract_meanings as 'matched-but-no-semantic' (drop unaccounted_chars to 0, but don't pollute structure patterns). Generator can optionally insert one between picked morphemes to graduate compound-formation.

Audit pass: triage the 149 short subjects — real morpheme stays as subject; pure joiner migrates to joiners field; spurious entry (e.g. 'um' with empty meaning) gets dropped. Manual triage required (gloss is the deciding evidence) — auto-classifying by length-only mis-categorizes real short morphemes.
notes: Phase 1 SHIPPED via PR #130 (squash-merged 2026-05-08). Schema (dict-or-list bundle), Joiner sentinel, load_joiners, matcher hook with anchor-gate (joiner consumption requires Meaning on both sides). 40 tests, 1834 full-suite passing. Real bug caught + fixed in review: unanchored joiner consumption (Phase 2 data alone could launder garbage), null per-lang defensive, Phase 2.5 limitation pinned by counter-fixture test. Phase 1.5 follow-up: wyrd-0l2g (compose-time joiner insertion). Phase 2 follow-up: wyrd-semi (audit 149 short subjects + populate joiners pool).

title: wyrd-k8e Phase 3: make trie matcher the default; remove legacy iterator
description: After wyrd-k8e Phase 2 wires the trie matcher behind a flag and the bundled-corpus equivalence regression passes, Phase 3 flips the default to trie and removes Word.extract_meanings. Also migrates KenningExplain (currently uses the legacy iterator) to canonical_decompositions(). Unblocks downstream cleanup of the matcher contracts.

title: wyrd-k8e Phase 2: wire trie matcher into Name.find_meaning behind a flag
description: wyrd-k8e Phase 1 (PR #64) shipped trie_matcher.py as a standalone module. Phase 2 wires it into Name.find_meaning so the matcher uses the trie-indexed segmentation DAG instead of (or alongside) the legacy O(M)-per-recursion-level iterator. Bundled-corpus equivalence regression vs the legacy iterator required (D29). May also reduce false partial-matches like the bogus '<-m->' middle-match that prevented wyrd-4hx7 from catching 'demesne'/'cluain' as candidates. Per the original wyrd-k8e closeout, ~200x speedup expected on routine corpus passes.

title: Empirical Wiktionary corpus miner: lift perfect-rate by filling miss-fragments
description: Mine the unaccounted-fragment misses surfaced by 'wyrd kenning unaccounted' against the existing wiktextract slices on disk. For each fragment that hits a Wiktionary headword in a culture-allowed language (e.g. english culture only looks at OE/ME/ON/OF/AN/Latin/Modern-English entries), write an etymon row tagged with a synthetic 'wiktionary-empirical' source — admitted to the bundle without the D4 ≥3-scholar gate, like rando-port. attested_year cells derived deterministically from language. Re-export meanings.json, rebuild proportions, snapshot to COVERAGE.md.
notes: Shipped via PR #68. Two follow-up tickets filed for agent-review concerns (complexity refactor, test-coverage gaps) plus a P2 ticket for refining the empirical mining filters. The committed bundle is from the first-pass mining only; second-pass entries (eglwys, betws, etc.) need refinement before re-export.

title: Re-emit meanings.json + per-culture proportions from current lexicon
description: Bundled meanings.json was last exported on 2026-05-03. Since then the lexicon has accumulated more attested_years data, more inflections, more variants, plus the wyrd-44a synset→cognate rename and wyrd-7tz meaning_synset Phase 1 schema. Re-emit the bundle and re-run rebuild-proportions for english/scottish/welsh/irish/breton so the runtime reflects the current corpus state. Compare before/after as part of the PR description.
notes: Re-ran export-meanings + rebuild-proportions for all 5 cultures against the current lexicon DB. The newly-exported meanings.json is bit-identical (canonical-JSON MD5 match) to the May 3 bundle. All 5 proportions JSONs are semantically identical (multiset-equal); the byte differences are list-ordering noise in 'structures' (non-determinism in _proportions_from). No-op refresh — the May 3 bundle (PR #58, commit 980041f) already reflects everything in the lexicon that flows through the current export. Substantive new data since May 3 (Wiktionary descent edges, meaning_synset Phase 1 schema) is gated behind wyrd-7tz Phase 2/3 + cluster-cognates and doesn't reach the bundle yet. May 5 mining was 1 acceptance from longnon_v2 — too small to move any morpheme over the witness threshold.

title: Rename etymon.synset_id → etymon.cognate_id (lexicon schema cleanup)
description:
Pre-existing concern flagged during PR #61 review (Claude M1): the etymon.synset_id column populated by cluster-cognates is misnamed. It represents a COGNATE-cluster ID (etymology-based: OE tūn / ON tún / Icelandic tún all share one cluster pointing at PGmc *tūnaz). The new wyrd-7tz Phase 1 introduced the meaning_synset table (semantic equivalence), creating a naming collision that's documented in lexicon.sql but is fragile.

The right rename:
- etymon.synset_id → etymon.cognate_id
- etymon.synset_method → etymon.cognate_method
- idx_etymon_synset → idx_etymon_cognate

Touchpoints (callsites in lexicon.py + cli.py):
- cluster_cognates() and its tests
- migrate_schema migration entries
- Any reports / stats command that reads synset_id

Should land before wyrd-7tz Phase 2 ships (LLM-assisted etymon_meaning_synset population) so future code only ever sees the disambiguated naming.

Out of scope for wyrd-7tz Phase 1 — kept as a separate cleanup to keep that PR's scope tight.

title: Generator.filter_for_tag: sort set iteration to lock cross-PYTHONHASHSEED bit-stability
description:
Pre-existing concern flagged during PR #59 review (Claude + seed-reproducibility-reviewer): wyrd/generators/kenning/proportions.py:filter_for_tag builds a dict by iterating a set comprehension over tag_db keys. The resulting dict's iteration order then feeds weighted_choice via Generator.select, where the cumulative-threshold construction is order-dependent.

Within one process the order is stable (PYTHONHASHSEED is fixed at startup). Across processes with different PYTHONHASHSEED, the dict iteration order can vary, which can flip weighted_choice picks at boundaries.

Same root cause as the wyrd-mj2 fix in _raw_class_score (PR #59); same fix shape applies — sort the iteration before building the dict.

Suggested change:
    keys_set = set(keys)
    return {key: self.elements[key] for key in sorted(keys_set) if key in self.elements}

Add a regression test analogous to test_raw_class_score_is_bit_stable_across_python_hash_seed: subprocess loop with varied PYTHONHASHSEED, assert weighted_choice returns the same key across runs.

Pre-existing — not introduced by PR #59. Was deliberately not bundled into PR #59 to keep scope tight.

title: kenning: bundle re-emit to populate attested_years (activates --era filter)
description:
The wyrd-lyp runtime --era filter shipped in PR #57 is a documented no-op end-to-end because today's bundled meanings.json carries no _attested_years data. The lexicon DB already has 2,667 attested-year rows (136 ETM + 2,531 toponym_etymology) populated by PR #56's mining. Running export-meanings against the current ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db will emit per-language _attested_years arrays into meanings.json, activating the --era filter on real morpheme data without further code changes.

Steps:
1. wyrd kenning lexicon export-meanings --output wyrd/generators/kenning/data/meanings.json
2. Diff to confirm attested_years fields appear; spot-check a few high-coverage entries
3. Run pytest to confirm bundle still parses cleanly via load_meanings
4. Verify Kenning().generate({'culture': 'english', 'era': 'oe-late'}) actually narrows the keep-set (per-call cost should drop from full-coverage no-op to genuine filter)
5. PR + merge

No code changes — pure data refresh.
notes:
Already-done. Verified origin/main:wyrd/generators/kenning/data/meanings.json carries 1215/3807 (31.9%) words with _attested_years fields — PR #58 (wyrd-j5v, commit 980041f, 'bundle refresh after 5/3 bridge work') re-emitted the bundle with the new fields when it merged. The --era filter is therefore active on real data today.

Confirmed via Kenning().generate({'culture': 'english', 'era': 'oe-early'}) narrowing the keep-set from 2901 usages to 2327 (and producing different names from 'me' / 'modern' on the same seeds).

The earlier 'zero attested_years in bundle' observation was from a stale pre-PR-#58 read.

title: kenning: move default lexicon DB location to ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db
description:
Currently _DEFAULT_LEXICON_PATH in cli.py is cwd-relative ('wyrd/generators/kenning/data/lexicon.db'). This is fragile in worktree workflows: a 'wyrd kenning lexicon build' run from a worktree's cwd silently creates a divergent DB in that worktree's data/ dir.

Move the default to '~/.wyrd/lexicon.db' (with WYRD_LEXICON_DB env override) so the location is independent of cwd / repo / worktree. One DB per user, survives 'rm -rf' of any checkout, fresh clones inherit the existing corpus.

Scope:

1. Add wyrd.generators.kenning.paths module (or similar) with default_lexicon_path() that returns Path.home() / '.wyrd' / 'lexicon.db', overridable via WYRD_LEXICON_DB env var.
2. Update _DEFAULT_LEXICON_PATH in cli.py to call this function.
3. Auto-migrate: on first command that needs the DB, if the new path doesn't exist AND a legacy path 'wyrd/generators/kenning/data/lexicon.db' exists relative to the git repo root, mv the file with a stderr warning. Don't auto-create ~/.wyrd unless we're committing to using it.
4. Add 'wyrd kenning lexicon path' CLI command that prints the resolved DB path (operator convenience).
5. Update OVERVIEW.md and INGESTION.md references to the new default location.
6. Drop the 'wyrd/generators/kenning/data/lexicon.db' line from .gitignore (no longer needed since the file won't exist there).
7. Tests: cover default-path resolution, env override, auto-migration of legacy DB.

Acceptance:
- _DEFAULT_LEXICON_PATH resolves cwd-independently
- 'wyrd kenning lexicon path' prints the right path
- Legacy DB at wyrd/generators/kenning/data/lexicon.db migrates to ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db on first command run with stderr warning
- WYRD_LEXICON_DB env var overrides everything
- Existing CliRunner tests pass (they all pass --db explicitly)

title: bridge_phonological_on: phonological bridge for Old Norse place-name forms (mirror of wyrd-ft3)
description:
Diagnostic on 2026-05-03 (post wyrd-083/ft3 merge): ON has 486 unbridged place-name etymons of ~600 total ON place-name forms. Same structural pattern as wyrd-ft3 but for Old Norse instead of Old English — never built.

ON place-name dictionaries write modernized forms (by, holm, byr, dal, gardr, thwaite, thveit, vik, tun, thorpe); Wiktionary uses scholarly orthography with þ/ð, macrons, and -r endings (býr, hólmr, dalr, garðr, þveit, vík, tūn, þorp, kirkja).

Top high-witness ON forms still unbridged (sources count):
  by (9), holm (6), byr (5), kirk (4), eski (3), dal (3), dale (3), skogr (3),
  gardr (3), thwaite (3), griss (3), tun (3), thorpe (3), vik (3), skjalf (2),
  dyr (2), vollr (2), buski (2), klakkr (2), slakki (2), ...

Verified Wiktionary canonicals exist for the top forms (e.g. þveit is in DB but tombstoned to thveit; bridge would redirect-follow once issue A from the OE ticket is fixed).

Implementation: copy bridge_phonological_oe / cli wrapper / tests, swap the language code and the curated mapping table. Apply chain-flatten OR-clause and lemma-reparent (round-1 critical fix from PR #46) — these are now load-bearing patterns for any same-language bridge.

Acceptance:
- New bridge_phonological_on() function in lexicon.py
- New _ON_PHONOLOGICAL_BRIDGES table with at least the top-30 high-witness pairs
- New CLI command 'lexicon bridge-phonological-on' (mirrors --apply, --dry-run, --db semantics)
- Tests covering: dry-run, apply, idempotency, chain-flatten, lemma-reparent, missing_target warning, CLI smoke
- Pre/post coverage measurement: cross-source bridge for ON place-name etymons rises substantially (target: 50%+ of ON bucket bridged)

title: bridge_phonological_oe: fix target-index to follow merged_into_id chains + expand bridge table
description:
Diagnostic on 2026-05-03 (post wyrd-083/ft3 merge): OE residue is 1510 unbridged of 1830 unmerged OE place-name etymons.

Two issues identified:

ISSUE A: bridge_phonological_oe target_index bug.
The target_index is built with 'WHERE merged_into_id IS NULL', so when the bridge map names a target that is itself a tombstone, the lookup fails silently.

Concrete failures from current DB state:
- 'dale' → 'dæl': dæl is merged into dael (id 1426). Lookup misses. (5 sources unbridged)
- 'ey' → 'īeg': īeg doesn't exist as canonical at all (only 'ieg' does, macron-stripped). Lookup misses. (5 sources unbridged)

Fix: when building target_index, follow merged_into_id chains so target lookup resolves through tombstones to the live canonical. Or alternatively, snap bridge values to the actual canonical-form spelling per current DB state — but the redirect-follow fix is more robust against future ingest re-shuffles.

ISSUE B: _OE_PHONOLOGICAL_BRIDGES is too narrow.
Top high-witness OE forms still unbridged after wyrd-ft3 (sources count in parens):
  ingas (7), wella (4), scelf (3), holegn (3), inga (3), hare (3), wlc (3),
  cippa (3), hang (3), pool (3), leofhere (3), lech (3), hasel (3), cylla (3),
  kirk (3), writol (2), hala (2), hīgna (2), kers (2), draeg (2), roth (2),
  ticce (2), hāran (2), hēg (2), cloppa (2), billing (2), ēg (2), hlyp (2)
... and ~50 more 2-source forms.

Add the high-witness pairs to _OE_PHONOLOGICAL_BRIDGES. Each has a known Wiktionary canonical (often macroned: ingas → ingas/-ingas, wella → welle/wiella, holegn → holen, hare → hara, pool → pōl, kirk → cirice, etc.). Cross-reference each addition against actual DB state via a quick SELECT.

Acceptance:
- Issue A: target_index includes tombstones reachable via merged_into_id chains
- Issue B: bridge table expanded by 30-50 high-witness pairs sourced from current DB
- Pre/post coverage measurement: cross-source bridge for OE place-name etymons rises substantially (target: ~50% of OE bucket bridged, from current 17.4%)
- Tests: regression test pinning the redirect-follow behavior + parametric tests pinning at least the top-15 new bridge pairs

title: D5-1 expansion: extend lookup-attested-years to also scan toponym_etymology rows
description:
Follow-up to wyrd-3ux (PR #47). The v1 lookup-attested-years scans etymon_text_match rows — those are reverse-search hits where canonical etymon forms appear in source bodies. Yield: 136 attestations on 5,298 rows (~2.6% density), well below the wyrd-3ux aspirational 1000+ target.

The reason for low density: reverse-search rows are MENTIONS of forms in scholarly prose, not necessarily citations. Real toponym citations with year-attestations live in toponym_etymology.notes — the LLM-extracted snippet that surrounded each toponym's body in the source dictionary.

Sample toponym_etymology notes: 'Kerorven, manoir en Guérande, 1476' or 'Tune, 1086 (DB); Tunes, 1242'. These have YEAR CITATIONS DIRECTLY in the captured snippet. Per a quick sample, ~40-60% of notes rows contain year citations.

Scope:

1. Schema: add attested_year column to toponym_etymology (or to toponym_etymology_element if attestations are per-element). Decide based on whether the LLM extracts per-element years or just one per toponym.
2. Function: lookup_attested_years_for_etymologies(db) — scans toponym_etymology.notes (no source bodies needed; the quote is in-DB). Apply the same form-attached pattern.
3. CLI: extend lookup-attested-years to also process toponym_etymology rows when present.
4. Tests: parametrize over both etymon_text_match and toponym_etymology shapes.

Estimated yield: corpus has ~5,238 toponym_etymology rows. At 30-40% density (year-citations are common in toponym dictionary entries), expected new attestations: 1,500-2,000.

Acceptance:
- Combined etymon_text_match + toponym_etymology yield >= 1,000 (per wyrd-3ux original target)
- FP rate stays <= 5% (form-attached pattern is the same)
- Reversible via clear-enrichment --stage=attested-years (works on both tables)

Pairs with D5-2 (era-cell sampling) which depends on attestation density.

title: cluster-cognates / lexicon: bridge generic 'celtic' language code to specific Welsh/Irish/Gaelic/Breton entries
description:
Discovered during 2026-05-03 wiktextract ingest: 441 place-name dictionary etymons with language='celtic' have no synset cluster despite their forms (ar, ach, dubh, ros, caer, fionn, cill, druim, ...) being well-attested in Wiktionary under specific Celtic language codes (cy=Welsh, ga=Irish, gd=Scottish Gaelic, br=Breton, gv=Manx, kw=Cornish, sga=Old Irish, cel-pro=Proto-Celtic).

Place-name dictionaries don't pin which specific Celtic language a morpheme is from — they write 'celtic' as a catch-all. Wiktionary entries are language-specific. The lookup mismatch leaves a real cross-source bridge unbuilt.

Fix options:

(A) New normalize-celtic CLI / lib pass: for each etymon with language='celtic', search for matching canonical_form in {welsh, irish, scottish-gaelic, breton, manx, cornish, proto-celtic} and merge via merged_into_id (D22 OCR-cluster style — non-destructive). The Celtic etymon becomes a tombstone pointing at whichever specific-language match exists. Cluster-cognates then rolls up via the merged_into_id chain (already redirect-aware per wyrd-223).

(B) Multi-language fuzzy search in cluster-cognates: when finding edges, treat 'celtic' as a wildcard that matches any of the specific Celtic language codes. More invasive; option A is cleaner.

Acceptance: post-implementation, the Celtic place-name etymons (ros, caer, dubh, fionn, etc.) appear in clusters with their Wiktionary specific-language counterparts. Coverage of place-name etymons with synset_id rises from 17.6%.

Out of scope: phonological-similarity matching (ton vs tūn vowel-weakening) — separate ticket.

title: wiktextract descendants section: parse nested tree shape (not flat-with-depth)
description:
Discovered during PR #41 live ingest 2026-05-03: wiktextract's actual descendants shape is a NESTED tree, not the flat-with-depth-markers list my parser assumed. Each descendant entry has {lang_code, word, optional descendants (recursive)} — there is NO 'templates' field on descendant entries and NO 'depth' field.

Concrete real entry from sources/wiktextract_proto_celtic.jsonl:
  {'lang': 'Proto-Brythonic', 'lang_code': 'cel-bry-pro', 'word': '*ɨn', 'descendants': [{'lang': 'Middle Breton', 'lang_code': 'xbm', 'word': 'en', 'descendants': [...]}]}

Result: the OE slice ingest yielded 0 downward edges across 66179 entries because the parser walked a non-existent 'templates' field. All useful descent edges came from the etymology UPWARD direction instead. That's still ~10K edges but loses the downward tree (parents whose descendants we don't have entries for).

Fix: rewrite _walk_descendants in wyrd/generators/kenning/wiktextract_ingester.py to:
- Read lang_code + word directly from each descendants entry (not via templates)
- Recurse into the nested 'descendants' field on each entry (true tree walk)
- Drop the depth-markers logic entirely (replaced by recursion depth)
- Handle borrow flag if present in the new shape (need to investigate — may be on 'tags' or 'roman' fields)

Tests: need a fresh fixture matching the real nested shape. The existing tests use the wrong (flat-with-depth) shape and would need to be either deleted or kept as 'historical-fixture-style' tests with a comment.

Synthetic test data should be built from a small slice of real wiktextract output (e.g. 5-10 lines from sources/wiktextract_proto_celtic.jsonl) committed as a test fixture under tests/fixtures/.

Acceptance criteria:
- _walk_descendants reads {lang_code, word, descendants?} directly
- Recursive descent through nested 'descendants' arrays
- Test fixture from real wiktextract output (small, deterministic)
- Live ingest of sources/wiktextract_proto_celtic.jsonl (1608 entries, dense descendants) yields significant downward_edges count (currently 0)

title: cluster-cognates: walk through merged_into_id redirects to land synset_id on canonical winners
description:
Discovered during the wyrd-hun (PR #41) live ingest 2026-05-03: the cluster-cognates pass operates on RAW etymon_descent edges and assigns synset_id to whichever endpoint the edge points at — including OCR-merged tombstones.

Concrete case: wiktextract has OE 'tun' (ASCII), place-name dictionaries have OE 'tūn' (macron). normalize-ocr correctly merges them ('tun' becomes a tombstone with merged_into_id pointing at 'tūn'). But the wiktextract descent edge (gmw-pro:*tūn → ang:tun) still points at the tombstoned 'tun' (id=2274), not the canonical 'tūn' (id=716). cluster-cognates then assigns synset_id on the tombstone, leaving canonical 'tūn' with synset_id=NULL.

Result: queries like 'cognates of OE tūn' return empty because they look up synset_id on the canonical row. The rollup-aware query exists but is gnarly (walk merged_into_id chain to find loser, get synset_id from loser, find other rows with same synset_id, roll those through merged_into_id again).

Fix options:

(A) cluster-cognates walks etymon_canonical (the view that filters out merged_into_id IS NOT NULL) and resolves edges through merged_into_id → canonical. Writes synset_id on canonicals only. Tombstones rolled up at query time.

(B) After OCR merge, rewrite etymon_descent.parent_id and child_id to point at canonical winners. Mining-evidence-preserving since the edge metadata stays. But mutating the descent table feels like a D21 violation (mining evidence is sacred).

Option A is correct per D22 ('enrichment passes operate on canonical view; tombstones are queried-through, not mutated').

Acceptance criteria:
- cluster-cognates resolves parent_id and child_id through merged_into_id when finding roots and walking children
- After PR #41's OE ingest + normalize-ocr, query for synset_id of canonical OE 'tūn' (id=716) returns the *tūn cluster's id
- existing wyrd-81n tests still pass (the merged_into_id paths weren't exercised; new tests add coverage)
- regression test: insert raw edges A→B, then merge B into B' via OCR, then run cluster-cognates → synset_id lands on B' not on B (the tombstone)

title: wyrd-4rt.1: wiktextract → etymon_descent ingester (Claude 1 implementation)
description:
Per user 2026-05-03: Wiktionary mining moves to Claude 1's lane (claude 2 stays on place-name etymology mining). Wiktextract is a pure structured-data ingester — no LLM, no form-in-body validation — so it doesn't fit claude 2's mine-llm pipeline shape.

Scope (this ticket):

(1) Library: parse wiktextract JSONL (one entry per line), extract:
    - word + lang_code → upsert etymon
    - etymology_templates: {{inh|...}} → inheritance edge upward, {{bor|...}} → borrowing, {{der|...}} → derivation, {{cal|...}} → calque
    - descendants section: each {{desc|<lang>|<word>}} → inheritance edge downward (Wiktionary defaults Descendants to inheritance unless explicitly flagged)
    - skip: {{cog|...}} (peer relation, no parent direction → optional 'cognate' edge if both in DB), {{m|...}} (mention only), pronunciation/qualifier/sense templates
    - depth field in descendants tracks nesting; sub-descendants chain off their nearest preceding entry at depth-1

(2) Lang code mapping: wiktextract uses Wiktionary lang codes (ang, gem-pro, non, is, en, de, ...) which differ from wyrd's existing language strings (old-english, proto-germanic, old-norse, icelandic, modern-english, german, ...). Build a lookup table for the ~30 codes we'll encounter most often; unmapped codes pass through raw with a counter.

(3) CLI: wyrd kenning lexicon ingest-wiktionary <path> with --apply / --db / --limit <N> / --since-line <N> for resumability.

(4) Source attribution: one synthetic source row 'wiktionary' (per D27).

(5) Idempotency: edge insertion is INSERT OR IGNORE on the (parent_id, child_id, edge_type, source_id) UNIQUE constraint; etymon upsert handles duplicates. Re-running on the same JSONL is a no-op.

(6) Tests: synthetic JSONL fixtures covering canonical entry shape, each edge-type template, descendants nesting, lang-code mapping, idempotency, malformed-entry skipping.

(7) Documentation: INGESTION.md gets a new 'Wiktionary mining (wyrd-4rt)' section with the kaikki.org dump URLs, slice strategies (per-language vs full corpus), and the ingest CLI.

Out of scope:
- Actually downloading the multi-GB wiktextract dump in a session — defer; user runs the dump pull manually and points the CLI at it.
- Compound/affix template handling (defer; the bulk of useful data is in inh/bor/der/cal/desc templates).
- Per-edit Wiktionary attribution (single 'wiktionary' source for v1 per D27).
- Cluster-cognates run after ingestion (already shipped wyrd-81n; user runs 'wyrd kenning lexicon cluster-cognates --apply' as a follow-up).

Acceptance criteria:
- New module wyrd/generators/kenning/wiktextract_ingester.py
- CLI 'wyrd kenning lexicon ingest-wiktionary' with --apply default-False (dry-run) flag
- Synthetic fixture tests covering each documented edge-type template and the descendants-depth chaining
- INGESTION.md procedure section with kaikki.org URLs
- 'wyrd kenning lexicon ingest-wiktionary --help' surfaces the flags cleanly

title: cluster-cognates enrichment pass: walk etymon_descent to populate synset_id
description:
Why this exists:

Once etymon_descent (filed as a sibling design ticket) lands and Wiktionary ingestion (wyrd-4rt) populates edges, we need a pass that walks the descent graph and assigns synset_id to every etymon reachable from a common root. Same shape as link-lemmas (D8): conservative, reversible, method-stamped.

Without this, queries like 'all cognates of Modern English town across languages' require an unbounded recursive CTE on every call. The materialized synset_id column makes it a single JOIN.

What needs to be done:

(1) New CLI: 'wyrd kenning lexicon cluster-cognates --apply'
    - Walks etymon_descent edges of edge_type IN ('inheritance', 'borrowing') from the most-ancestral etymons (those with no incoming descent edges of these types)
    - Assigns synset_id = id of the root to every descendant
    - Skips the 'cognate' edge_type (that's a 'compare with' relationship, not a chain)
    - Method/version stamp: etymon.synset_method = 'cluster-cognates-v1'

(2) Reversibility: 'wyrd kenning lexicon clear-enrichment --stage=cognates --apply' clears synset_id and synset_method. Reuses the existing clear-enrichment shape from D22.

(3) Tests:
    - A → B → C inheritance chain: all three get the same synset_id (= A.id)
    - Multi-root case: separate roots produce separate synset_ids
    - Cognate edges (edge_type='cognate') do NOT bridge synsets — cognate is a peer relationship, not a chain
    - Clear + re-run is a no-op (idempotent)
    - Borrowing edges DO bridge (we treat borrowed words as part of the cognate set; refine if this turns out to be too permissive)

Acceptance criteria:
- CLI command exists and is documented in INGESTION.md
- Tests as above
- Clear-enrichment knows about --stage=cognates
- Performance: cluster pass on the full corpus completes in seconds (it's a graph walk, not LLM)

Out of scope:
- Actual Wiktionary ingestion (wyrd-4rt)
- Generator-side use of synset_id for cross-language register rendering (separate ticket)
- Edge-confidence-weighted clustering (synset assignment is currently binary; could later weight by edge confidence)

title: Design etymon_descent schema + cognate-cluster query layer for cross-language reflex graph
description:
Why this exists:

Wiktionary etymology + Descendants sections produce a directed graph that doesn't fit the current schema. A Proto-Germanic root like *tūnaz has children in OE (tūn), ON (tún), modern Icelandic (tún), Faroese (tún), modern English (town), German (Zaun), Dutch (tuin). The current etymon table has merged_into_id (OCR-cluster losers, D22) and lemma_id (inflected variants of the same form, D8) — neither represents 'this OE form descends from this Proto-Germanic form' or 'this Icelandic word is a cognate of this English word.'

Without this schema, we can't:
- Mine Wiktermextract output (wyrd-4rt) without losing the chain information
- Surface 'modern descendants of OE tūn' as a query
- Render a place name in a different language register by swapping each etymon for its Welsh/Icelandic/Latin cognate (the cross-cultural rendering use case)
- Implement wyrd-7tz (synset / cross-language equivalence) — the Descendants tree IS the synset

Scope (this ticket):

Schema design + DECISIONS.md entry. NOT the actual ingestion (that's wyrd-4rt) and NOT the cognate-clustering enrichment pass (separate follow-on ticket). This ticket lands the tables and the query examples; wyrd-4rt populates them.

Key design decisions to record:

(1) Edge table shape — proposed:
    CREATE TABLE etymon_descent (
      id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
      parent_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etymon(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
      child_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etymon(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
      edge_type TEXT NOT NULL,  -- 'inheritance'|'borrowing'|'calque'|'compound'|'derivation'|'cognate'|'unknown'
      source_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES source(id),
      confidence TEXT CHECK (confidence IN ('high','medium','low')),
      notes TEXT,
      UNIQUE (parent_id, child_id, edge_type, source_id)
    );
    Plus indexes on parent_id, child_id.

(2) Edge types map to Wiktextract template kinds: {{inh}}=inheritance (high conf), {{bor}}=borrowing (high), {{cog}}=cognate-relation (medium), {{der}}=derivation (medium), free-text 'compare with X'=low. Document the mapping in INGESTION.md once wyrd-4rt lands.

(3) Should descent edges contribute to etymon_consensus.witnesses? PROPOSED: no. Descent ≠ extraction-attestation (D4 is about 'N scholars cite this morpheme as part of a toponym's breakdown'). Descent rolls up cross-language and would inflate consensus counts. Synset clustering is the right rollup for descent.

(4) Synset / cognate cluster layer — proposed: materialized via etymon.synset_id (nullable INTEGER), populated by a separate 'wyrd kenning lexicon cluster-cognates' pass that walks the descent graph from each Proto-* root and assigns synset_id to all reachable descendants. Same shape as link-lemmas (D8) — derivable, reversible, method-stamped via etymon.synset_method.
   Alternative considered: recursive CTE view. Rejected because cross-language synset queries would walk unbounded depth on every call; materialized column makes the query a single JOIN.

(5) Wiktionary as source: one synthetic 'wiktionary' source row for v1 (per-edit attribution lives in wiki history; per-language-section slicing is overkill until needed).

(6) Generality: the schema accepts descent edges from ANY source, not just Wiktionary. Existing dictionary mining that says 'from OE tūn' could populate descent rows too — just hasn't been the focus. Generalize the schema; let wyrd-4rt be the first big populator.

Acceptance criteria:
- New D-entry in DECISIONS.md (D27?) documenting (1)-(6) with rationale
- Schema changes in data/lexicon.sql + migration in lexicon.py
- Sample queries in INGESTION.md or a new section: 'modern descendants of <etymon>', 'cognates of <etymon>', 'languages with a reflex meaning <gloss>'
- Tests cover: schema migration is idempotent; insert/query round-trips; etymon_consensus does NOT roll up across descent edges
- wyrd-4rt updated to depend on this ticket
- New ticket filed for the cluster-cognates enrichment pass (synset_id populator), depending on this ticket

Out of scope:
- Actual Wiktionary ingestion (wyrd-4rt)
- Cluster-cognates enrichment pass (new follow-on ticket)
- Generator-side use of the descent/synset layer (e.g. cross-cultural rendering) — that's a third follow-on

title: Skeat-§ running-header parser: extend page resolution to Skeat-style books
description:
The Mawer-style parse_running_header_pages handles '<HEADWORD> <number>' (one-line ALL-CAPS toponym + trailing page). Skeat books use a different convention: '§ N. NAMES ENDING IN -X. <page>' as the running header at the top of each printed page. The current backfill skips Skeat books with no_headers=1.

Add parse_skeat_section_header_pages(text) returning the same [(offset, page), ...] shape, dispatch in backfill_citation_pages by trying Mawer first then Skeat (or pick the one with more headers), and update the parse-pages CLI audit to report which convention matched.

Beneficiaries: skeat_1901_cambridgeshire, skeat_1904_huntingdonshire (currently 36 quote misses, 184 before-first-page artefacts), skeat_1906_bedfordshire (50 cit but Mawer is spuriously matching TOC entries), skeat_1911_berkshire, skeat_1913_suffolk, skeat_1904_hertfordshire (currently fully skipped).

Pattern shape from sources/skeat_1901_cambridgeshire.txt body:
- '§   2.      NAMES   ENDING   IN   -TON.  9'
- '§8.      NAMES    ENDING    IX    -BRIDGE,   -HITHE.  33'  (OCR variant)
- '§  4.      NAMES   ENDING   IN   -HAM.  21'

Distinguish from non-running TOC + section openers ('§ 2. The suffix -ton.' — title case, no trailing page) by requiring ALL-CAPS title block + trailing digit.

Out of scope: any new mining; this is pure ingestion-time enrichment.

title: Backfill etymon_citation.page + toponym_etymology.page from parse-pages output
description:
Wire wyrd-9kh.5's parse_running_header_pages output into the page-number columns. Both etymon_citation and toponym_etymology have a nullable 'page' column populated by no writer today; mining always inserts with page=NULL. A retrospective backfill walks each source's running headers, locates each row's quoted excerpt in source text via str.find, and UPDATEs the page.

Scope:
- New CLI: 'wyrd kenning lexicon backfill-pages <sources_dir>' with --apply / --source / --db flags
- New library function: backfill_citation_pages(db, source_id, source_text, *, apply) returning per-source counts
- Updates both etymon_citation.page and toponym_etymology.page in one pass per source
- Idempotent (skips rows where page IS NOT NULL); rerunnable
- Skips sources with zero running headers (Skeat-§ books and ones without Mawer-style headers); reports them in the audit
- Dry-run by default
- Tests covering: header-found case, no-header case, quote-not-in-text case, idempotence

title: Chrestomathy/treatise-aware extractor: pull only etymology-commentary sections from non-dictionary sources
description:
Pattern surfaced from 4 mining attempts (Watson 1904, Quilgars 1906, Longnon 1920 vol 2, Loth 1890): the existing alphabetical-headword parser is mis-matched for treatises, chrestomathies, and methodological essays. Real etymology content is BURIED inside chapter prose or commentary sections, but the parser segments by capital-letter headwords and treats each as a candidate entry — so the LLM sees front-matter / TOC / text excerpts / numbered-list section-headers and correctly declines them.

Concrete failure shapes seen at mining time:
1. Longnon vol 2 saint-names: 2,775 parser entries, 2% accept on first 50 because front-matter dominates. The actual saint-name body is a numbered list ('1725. Euphrasia: Sainte-Euphrasie ...') that the headword parser can't break out into per-saint rows.
2. Loth 1890 Chrestomathie: 615 entries, mostly Middle Breton text excerpts (mystery plays, prose). The dense etymology commentary I sampled in research lives in dedicated 'Noms de Lieux et de Peuples' sections, but those aren't headword-shaped.
3. Longnon vol 1: 67 parser entries (only 24% accept), but the 470 pages contain ~3,500-4,200 named-place mentions in chapter prose. The headword parser misses 99% of those.

Proposal:
- New parser mode 'commentary' that finds etymology-commentary sections via heuristics (chapter heading patterns, dense Latin / 'cf.' / italic-form markers, year-citation density).
- For numbered-list shapes (saint-names, feudal-castles): segment by line-leading number ('1725.', '1726.') instead of by capital-letter headword.
- LLM-prompt variant that handles 'one-section, many-toponyms' shape (current schema is one-toponym-many-elements; would need a new 'extract-list-of-etymology-pairs' shape).

Estimated unlocked yield (rough projections):
- Longnon vol 1: 67 entries → potentially 600+ entries with section/numbered-list awareness, at 24% accept = 144+ rows (vs 16 today)
- Longnon vol 2: 2,775 → realistic ~1,500-2,000 numbered saint-name entries; even at 15% accept = 225+ rows
- Loth 1890: 615 → ~150-200 etymology-commentary entries; at 30% accept = 50+ rows
- d'Arbois 1890: ~700 entries possible, similar shape

Aggregate: easily 500+ new toponym etymology rows across these four sources.

Out of scope:
- The existing alphabetical-headword + skeat-section parsers stay unchanged for genuinely-dictionary-shaped books.
- Per-section / per-numbered-list LLM extraction is the real change; the parser is just a feeder.

OWNERSHIP NOTE: parser code is in dictionary_parser.py / skeat_parser.py / cli.py — out of the research/extractor agent's scope. Filing for the parser-side agent.
notes:
Partial completion: numbered-list sub-feature landed in PR #65 (commit 41af18e). Adds parse_numbered_list_text + --parser numbered-list + --min-entry/--max-entry CLI flags + 20 unit tests. Unblocks wyrd-ech (Longnon vol 2 saint-names mining).

Remaining sub-features still open:
- Chrestomathy commentary-section extractor (heuristic-based section detection for Loth 1890, Longnon vol 2 prose chapters, d'Arbois 1890)
- New LLM schema for 'extract list of etymology pairs from a single section' (one-section-many-toponyms shape)

These are larger scopes and will land as separate PRs.

2026-05-04 (after PR #65 numbered-list parser merge): Empirical confirmation that the 'one-section-many-toponyms' LLM schema is the actual blocker for Longnon vol 2 saint-names mining (wyrd-ech). 30-entry smoke with the new parser yielded 3.3% accept rate — the parser segments correctly (475 entries, 88% toponym) but the existing English-etymology-prose SYSTEM_PROMPT declines the terse 'Latin : Saint-X' derivation shape.

Concrete next step for the third sub-feature: a Longnon-style prompt variant that recognizes 'Latin source name : list of French derivatives' as a valid etymology shape, with attested_year defaulting to publication-era for the saint-name section.

title: Parse page numbers from Skeat-style OCR running headers
description:

Scope:

- Backfill: a CLI command 'wyrd kenning lexicon parse-pages --apply' that re-walks each source's body and updates etymon_citation.page for citations whose entry occurs in a known page span.
- Per-source heuristics: at minimum cover Skeat-1901, Skeat-1906, Skeat-1911, Skeat-1913, Mawer-1920 to start.

NOT in scope:
- Multi-line / footer-style page indicators (most of our corpus uses running headers; defer if a book breaks the pattern).

description:

title: D5-3: Era-aware bundle export + runtime cell selection
description:
Interface-layer of D5. Wires meanings.json + Meaning runtime to support era-cell selection at generation time.

Bundle shape (per D26 sibling-field pattern):
  Adds <lang>_era arrays carrying [{form, earliest, latest, cell}] entries per attested form.
  Example:
    'old_english_era': [
       {'form': 'tūn', 'earliest': 731, 'latest': 1066, 'cell': 'oe-late'},
       {'form': 'tun', 'earliest': 1086, 'latest': 1300, 'cell': 'me'},
       {'form': 'town', 'earliest': 1500, 'latest': null, 'cell': 'modern'}
    ]

Runtime:
- Meaning.pick_era_form(rng, era_cell) picks an attested form whose era cell matches; falls back to canonical (lang[0]) if no attestation in that cell
- NameGenerator.select(era=...) threads through and pre-renders surface substitutions at select time so __str__ stays pure
- 'load_meanings' strips _era suffix and routes into Meaning.eras

CLI:
  wyrd kenning generate english --era oe-late
  wyrd kenning generate english --era 1086        # year-as-era resolves to cell
  wyrd kenning generate english --era modern      # default-off preserves existing behavior

Update export-meanings to compute per-form era cells using D5-1's attested_year + D5-2's era_cell function.

Bundle-size budget: ~30-50 KB extra (negligible for importlib.resources path).

Determinism contract: --era=null (default) preserves bit-stable existing output. Picking --era N changes the pool; existing seeds will produce different names with --era set. This is the standard pattern (matches --novelty / --spelling-variety / --inflection-density).

Depends on D5-1 (data populated) + D5-2 (cell definitions).

See /tmp/wyrd-d5-era-axis-design-2026-05-02.md.
notes: Merged in PR #57 (squash). Code: strict era resolution + friendly error wrapper + full-coverage short-circuit. Tests: 8 new (CLI, culture mapping, error path, empty-string, _select_tag plumbing, full-coverage→None). 950 tests pass.

title: D5-2: Era-cell mapping + filtered sampling on (language × era) axis
description:
Sampling-layer of D5 era-aware register cells. Defines era cells per language family + adds '--era' CLI/JSON param that filters morpheme inventory to a chosen cell.

Era-cell definitions (proposed; see design doc):
- English: oe-early (-, 800), oe-late (800, 1100), me (1100, 1500), early-modern (1500, 1700), modern (1700, -)
- Norse: on-classical (-, 1100), on-late (1100, 1300), middle-scandinavian (1300, 1500), modern (1500, -)
- Brythonic: old (-, 1100), middle (1100, 1500), modern (1500, -)
- Goidelic: old-irish (-, 900), middle-irish (900, 1200), early-modern (1200, 1700), modern (1700, -)
- Latin: classical (-, 200), late-vulgar (200, 700), medieval (700, 1500), renaissance (1500, 1800)
- Norman-French: old-norman (-, 1300), anglo-norman (1066-1500 in England), modern (1500, -)

Implementation:
- ERA_CELLS constant in lexicon.py, keyed by family
- era_cell(language, year) -> str function
- Generator-side filter: morphemes whose attested_year falls in the chosen cell's range
- '--era' CLI argument accepts cell label OR a year (year resolves to cell)
- '--era=null' (default) preserves current bit-stable behavior

Approach for v1: era is a generation-time FILTER on the morpheme inventory; tag-co-occurrence stays per-culture (unchanged proportions JSONs). Output is 'morphemes attested in era cell, composed via culture's tag patterns.' Cheaper than a full per-(lang × era) tag-co-occurrence path; ships immediately on D5-1's data.

v2 (later): per-(lang × era) tag-co-occurrence, addressing 'tag patterns themselves shift across eras'.

Open question for the user (see design doc): is the proposed cell granularity right? Coarser (3 cells) would simplify; finer (10-year cohorts) gives more flexibility but undersamples.

See /tmp/wyrd-d5-era-axis-design-2026-05-02.md.
notes:
2026-05-02 update: User decision — era cells are PER-CULTURE, not per-language-family. Each culture defines its own ≤5 era cells, drawing era boundaries from whichever substrate languages apply. Updated proposed table:

- english: oe-early (-, 800), oe-late (800, 1100), me (1100, 1500), early-modern (1500, 1700), modern (1700, -)
- scottish: old-celtic (-, 900), middle-mixed (900, 1300), early-scots (1300, 1500), early-modern (1500, 1700), modern (1700, -)
- welsh: old-welsh (-, 1100), middle-welsh (1100, 1500), early-modern (1500, 1700), modern (1700, -) — 4 cells
- irish: old-irish (-, 900), middle-irish (900, 1200), early-modern-gaelic (1200, 1700), modern (1700, -) — 4 cells
- breton: old-breton (-, 1100), middle-breton (1100, 1700), modern (1700, -) — 3 cells (Ernault's wide moyen-breton)

ERA_CELLS dict lives in lexicon.py (or __init__.py) keyed by culture. era_cell(culture, year) -> str resolves a year inside the chosen culture's table.

Era cell labels are NOT globally unique — early-modern means 1500-1700 in english AND welsh but is absent from breton. The CLI flag '--era' is always interpreted in the context of '--culture', so 'wyrd kenning generate welsh --era middle-welsh' resolves inside welsh's table only.

User decision recap (other open questions from the design doc):
- Q1 cell granularity: 5 cells fine (some cultures use 3-4)
- Q2 axis vs enum-split: per-culture (closes the celtic-enum-split question — culture lens decides)
- Q3 default era on no-flag: keep current bit-stable behavior

See /tmp/wyrd-d5-era-axis-design-2026-05-02.md (updated 2026-05-02 with per-culture clarification).

title: D5-1: Mine attested years from source bodies via regex post-mining stage
description:
Foundation layer for D5 era-aware register cells. Adds an attested_year column to etymon_text_match and a 'lookup-attested-years' CLI step that scans source bodies for date citations near attested forms.

Approach: regex \b(\d{3,4})\b within the same sentence as a matched_form, with date-context filters (preceded by 'in'/'from'/'circa'/'DB'/'first recorded'). Idempotent / reversible (clear-enrichment --stage=attested-years).

Per D21/D22, this is enrichment-layer (LLM-free, rebuildable). No changes to mining evidence.

Schema delta:
  ALTER TABLE etymon_text_match ADD COLUMN attested_year INTEGER;
  CREATE INDEX idx_text_match_year ON etymon_text_match(attested_year);

Acceptance:
- regex extractor identifies year stamps in Mawer 1920, Ekwall 1922, Skeat county dicts (where 'X, 1086 (DB)' patterns are abundant)
- 1000+ etymon_text_match rows acquire non-null attested_year on first run
- false-positive rate <5% (validate against a 50-row sample by hand)
- idempotent re-run; clear-enrichment stage works

Foundation for D5-2 (era cell sampling) and D5-3 (era-aware bundle). Deferred year extraction during NEW mining (re-mining sources with prompt-side year capture) is a follow-up not in this ticket's scope.

See /tmp/wyrd-d5-era-axis-design-2026-05-02.md for the full architecture rationale and open questions.
notes: 2026-05-02 update: companion ticket wyrd-m70 will validate the new attested_forms SYSTEM_PROMPT via a Gemini Flash Tier-1 mining pass on Mawer 1920 (densest year-citation source per the corpus probe; 458 raw regex matches). The Tier-1 Gemini run is 'new' work per user's 2026-05-02 clarification (different model role on already-mined book, plus the new prompt). Expected to surface 200-400 (form, year) pairs in raw_response for the post-pass regex implementation to compare against.

title: Collapse --harsh + --grim into a unified --mood surface
description:
The two D6 knobs landed in PR #20 as separate CLI flags (--grim boolean, --harsh float). They actually skew different axes (--grim = semantic tags, --harsh = phonological weight) but the user wants them grouped under one user-facing surface — they're conceptually 'mood' presets that the GM picks rather than two unrelated dials.

Scope:
- Drop --grim and --harsh from CLI; add --mood (repeatable, choice-of-mood-names + optional :value suffix for graduation).
- Drop 'grim' boolean from JSON input_schema; KEEP 'harshness' number for graduated power-user control. Add 'mood' (array of strings).
- MOODS table in __init__.py: 'grim' -> tag-union, 'harsh' -> harshness float (default 1.0). Future moods (pastoral, noble, mortuary, etc) drop into the same table.
- 'harsh:0.5' colon syntax for graduated mood values.
- Update tests + DECISIONS D6 + README knob table.

Why this matters: the right shape for a GM-facing API. 'I want grim names' is one decision, not two. A unified mood vocabulary scales better as future moods land.

Why now: caught immediately after PR #20 landed; the user-facing surface hasn't shipped beyond the local repo, so clean-replace rather than soft-deprecate.
close_reason: landed in PR #25 (merged 2026-05-02). --grim and --harsh collapsed into --mood (repeatable, supports 'name' and 'name:value' syntax). MOODS recipe table in __init__.py. Power-user 'harshness' float param kept in JSON schema for non-colon graduated control. 332 tests passing.

title: Mine Loth 1890 Chrestomathie bretonne (Brythonic family) via Haiku
description:
Loth's Chrestomathie bretonne covers Breton + Welsh + Cornish in one source. Prior session called it 'essay-shaped, low parser yield' — that verdict was WRONG. Sample passages show 40-50 attested place-names per 20 pages with explicit etymological commentary (e.g. 'Abona [Itin. d'Ant., 486], l'Avon (Stratford-on-Avon), arm. aven dans Pont-aven').

Source: archive.org/details/chrestomathiebre00loth (548 pages, full DJVU TXT)

Tier-1 Haiku per D13.

Estimated yield: 1,100-1,370 place-name etymology pairs at Watson-1926 yield class.

Re-evaluation of prior call. Same risk-bucket as wyrd-efx (Longnon vol 1) — chrestomathy / treatise body, not alphabetical headword shape. The existing 'dictionary_parser.py' will yield fewer parsed entries than for Mawer/Skeat, but the LLM should handle the embedded named place + etymology pattern fine. Smoke-test 30 entries before full pass.

See /tmp/wyrd-corpus-research-2026-05-02.md.
notes:
2026-05-03: Parser yield smoke surfaced a content-shape issue. Loth's 'Chrestomathie bretonne' is — true to its name — an ANTHOLOGY OF MIDDLE BRETON TEXTS (mystery plays, prose excerpts, manuscript folios). The 615 parser entries are mostly text samples, not etymology entries. Sample headwords: 'Baly' (a play character), 'Fol. 2 r°' (folio reference), 'Allas/Assuret/Teuet' (Breton verse).

The earlier research-stage yield estimate ('40-50 attested place-names per 20 pages') was based on the EMBEDDED etymological commentary sections (sample passage 'Abona [Itin. d'Ant., 486], l'Avon (Stratford-on-Avon), arm. aven dans Pont-aven'), but those commentary passages are a small fraction of the 548 pages. Bulk content is the chrestomathy proper.

Pattern: this is the FOURTH instance of the trust-audit pattern (Watson 1904 stats, Quilgars 1906 shape, Longnon 1920 vol 2 front-matter, now Loth 1890 anthology). Research-stage yield projection from prose-density samples consistently diverges from parser-yield at mining time.

Recommended path forward (out of scope for me — flagging for the parser-side Claude or a follow-up ticket):
- A 'extract-only-the-etymology-commentary-sections' mode for chrestomathy/treatise sources (Loth 1890, Longnon vols, possibly d'Arbois 1890). Would need section-detection heuristics.
- For now: defer Loth 1890 mining until that pipeline exists.

title: Mine Troude 1876 (Léon Breton dictionary, 863 pages) via Haiku
description:
Largest single Breton dictionary in the PD-source survey, alphabetical Breton-French structure with explicit dialectal labels (V., T., C., Y., B., Ouess.) for Vannes / Tréguier / Cornouailles / Léon / etc. Sample-confirmed alphabetical headword + grammatical label + French gloss + dialectal-label entry shape.

Source: archive.org/details/nouveaudictionnairetroude (863 pages, full DJVU TXT downloadable)

Tier-1 Haiku per D13.

Expected accept rate similar to Watson 1926 (~50%) since it's a true alphabetical dictionary, not a chrestomathy / treatise. Provides multi-dialect annotations that flow into the D18 variant pool naturally if the Tier-1 prompt is told to record them.

This is the single biggest Breton-corpus uplift among PD sources — should expand the breton register from 20 subjects to several hundred when combined with the Le Gonidec/Villemarqué 1850 second-witness pass (separate ticket).

Solves the wyrd-fmg expansion problem that the prior session left stuck on Le Gonidec Gallica 403. See /tmp/wyrd-corpus-research-2026-05-02.md for the full Breton-source survey.
notes:
Pipeline mismatch identified — INGESTION.md (lines 200-209) explicitly groups Troude 1876 with Joret 1881, Le Gonidec, Châlons-Loth Vannetais as 'language dictionaries that fit the wyrd-4rt Wiktionary-style ingestion path, not the toponym extractor.' Existing lexicon mine-llm path validates against toponym shape (D3 form-in-body) which won't apply to Breton-French vocabulary entries.

Smoke-tested 2026-05-04: alphabetical parser yields only 103 entries from a 863-page text (paragraph-flow format with multiple ALL-CAPS headwords per body, format incompatible). The right path is wiktextract-style ingestion of the dictionary's Breton lemma + grammatical category + French gloss + dialectal labels into the etymon table with a French-Breton-aware prompt.

Reclassifying as blocked on wyrd-4rt.

title: Mine Longnon 1920 vol 2 (saint-names + feudal castle names) via Haiku
description:
Volume 2 of Longnon's 'Les noms de lieu de la France' — covers saint-derived toponyms (entries 1659-2138) and feudal castle/fortress names (entry 2139+). Saint-names section alone yields hundreds of Saint-X toponyms with explicit Latin saint etymologies.

Source: archive.org/details/lesnomsdelieudel02long (874 pages, full DJVU TXT downloadable)

Tier-1 Haiku per D13. Same shape as vol 1 (which is in wyrd-efx) — feedback from a vol 1 smoke-test should inform whether vol 2 needs its own smoke first.

Adds the ecclesiastical-Latin-onto-French overlay (saint-names + feudal castle names) that vol 1's substrate-focused chapters do not cover. Combined with vol 1, French as a register becomes seriously viable.

See /tmp/wyrd-corpus-research-2026-05-02.md.
notes:
2026-05-04: 30-entry Haiku smoke against the saint-names section [1659..2138] with the new numbered-list parser (PR #65). Result: 1 accepted / 26 declined / 3 rejected — 3.3% accept rate.

Root cause is prompt mismatch, NOT parser shape. The numbered-list parser correctly segments 475 entries with 88% toponym detection. But the SYSTEM_PROMPT in llm_extractor.py is calibrated for 19th/20th-c English place-name etymology PROSE (Skeat/Mawer-style 'the etymon X means Y in Old English'), and the Longnon saint-name format is terse Latin → French derivation:

  1659. Caradocus ; Saint-Caradu (Côtes-du-Nord, Morbihan), Saint-Cadreuc (...).

The LLM treats this as 'no etymology' (sets found=false / decline) because there's no narrative explanation of the derivation; it's a one-line cross-reference shape. Plus OCR mangling ('Saint-Garadu' for 'Saint-Caradu') makes the form-in-body validator (D3) reject the few extractions that do come through.

Path forward: blocked on the third sub-feature of wyrd-5af — a prompt variant for 'one-section-many-toponyms / Latin → French derivation' shape. Not productive to scale the mining run with the current prompt.

3 rejected breakdown: form_not_in_body (1), attested_form_not_in_body (1), attested_year_not_int (1) — the LLM did try to extract content but couldn't survive the validators on OCR-mangled text.

Status: still IN_PROGRESS but blocked. Re-evaluate after wyrd-5af third sub-feature lands.

description:
