title: Audit and clean meanings.json bundle: surfaced data-quality issues from PR #22 Gemini review
description:
Follow-up to PR #22 (kenning: mine Bannister 1916 + Quilgars smoke + bundle refresh). Gemini Code Assist flagged 6 data-quality issues in the regenerated meanings.json bundle. These are all authoring-layer issues — fixing them requires lexicon DB surgery (etymon_gloss table edits, OCR variant cleanup) followed by re-export, not by hand-editing the bundle.

Specific issues:
1. meanings.json:1505 — 'Weorth' (OE 'worth' farm/homestead) carries 'Weorth' itself in the meaning array. The headword/lemma should not be a meaning of itself. Likely a mining extraction error where the model echoed the headword as a gloss.
2. meanings.json:2371 — etymon 'ore' (OE 'ōra' bank/shore from Bannister 1916 mining) carries 'red' as a meaning. The body text ('Orcop... red iron-stone') was extracted incorrectly: 'red' modifies 'iron-stone' in the gloss prose, not 'ōra' itself. Needs gloss removal.
3. meanings.json:2523 — Redundant glosses: 'book/charter' duplicated. Similar redundancies at lines 38717 (moor/heath) and 43205 (lake/pond). Cleanup pass on etymon_gloss for unique-per-etymon constraints.
4. meanings.json:10974 — 'griss' variant (likely OCR noise for 'gris' OE young-pig). Filter step in normalize-ocr / fuzzy-search disambiguation should catch this.
5. meanings.json:30750 — 'saearp' / 'saeart' OCR noise for 'scearp' / 'scearu'. Same shape as #4.
6. meanings.json:33900 — 'drnim' OCR noise for 'drim' / 'druim'. Same shape.

Why this is filed: surfaced by an automated review on PR #22; legitimate findings that the lexicon authoring layer should resolve but the PR scope was 'mine + bundle' not 'audit + clean.'

How to apply (per D21/D22): use clear-enrichment + targeted SQL DELETE on etymon_gloss for #1-#3 (preserve mining_run audit), then re-run the post-mining chain. For #4-#6 the OCR cleanup should happen via normalize-ocr cluster heuristics or a manual lexicon clear-enrichment + fuzzy-search re-run with stricter gloss-anchor rules. After fix: re-export bundle and verify the flagged lines are clean.

Resources: PR #22 Gemini comments at https://github.com/521-studios/wyrd/pull/22#discussion_r... (6 comment threads). Comment IDs 3177236380, 3177236383, 3177236385, 3177236386, 3177236390, 3177236391 — fetch via gh api repos/521-studios/wyrd/pulls/22/comments/<id>.
close_reason: landed in PR #23 (merged 2026-05-02). Targeted DELETEs for the two known-bad glosses + structural filters in export-meanings (concatenation-gloss filter + low-confidence-singleton variant filter) so similar issues are caught at export time going forward.

title: D8 explainer: surface <lemma>@<label> in NewName.description()
description:
PR #18 (wyrd-7fn) wired D8 inflection composition end-to-end and populates NewName.inflection_labels (a parallel list to the meanings/word_keys). However NewName.description() still emits canonical meanings only, so a generated name like 'Seahamme' surfaces in the explainer as 'sea + ham' rather than 'sea + ham@dative_or_pl'. This is the small follow-up deferred from PR #18.

Scope: thread the picked inflection label into description()'s breakdown lines for any morpheme that carries one. Display format TBD — likely '<lemma> (<gloss>) @<label>' or similar. Keep description() readable; the label set has 9 case names today, mostly OE.

Acceptance: when --inflection-density > 0 produces a substituted form, the explainer text shows which case label was applied. Bit-stable at density=0 (no labels picked → no labels shown).
close_reason: landed in PRs #20 (D6 knobs + D8 explainer) and #21 (gather_family refactor). All three merged into main 2026-05-02.

title: Wire D6 (--harsh + --grim): orthogonal name-flavor filters
description:
DECISIONS.md D6 specifies two orthogonal filters that apply to ANY language: --harsh is phonological skew (short syllables, harsh consonant clusters, voiced-stop endings), --grim is a semantic-tag filter (grim/mortuary/monstrous/battle/wilderness). Together they let a GM ask for menacing-feeling Slavic-east names without the engine pre-coding any culture as 'orcish'.

Currently neither exists. The phonology data is in wyrd/generators/kenning/phonology.py but isn't wired to a generation skew.

Scope:
1. --grim implementation: it's a multi-tag union filter ('any of grim/mortuary/monstrous/battle/wilderness'). Mostly a CLI sugar on top of existing --tag. But: requires those tags to actually exist in the lexicon at meaningful coverage. Probe the data first; might surface gaps.
2. --harsh implementation: a phonological score per morpheme (high = harsh, low = soft) computed from the language's phonology table at proportions-load time. Generation re-weights the empirical proportions by harsh_score^harshness_strength. Knob 0..1.
3. CLI: 'wyrd kenning generate english --harsh --grim --culture slavic-east' (forward-compat for a slavic-east register).
4. Braitham Gate test: at harsh=0 + grim=False, behavior unchanged.
5. Smoke test: harsh=1 + grim produces visibly menacing names that ARE still well-formed (location keys etc.)

Acceptance: filters compose orthogonally; existing English-Welsh-Scottish-Irish all work with both; CLI and JSON schema both expose them.
notes:
Audit 2026-05-02: the D6-spec'd tag names ('grim', 'mortuary', 'monstrous', 'battle', 'wilderness') don't exist in the corpus today. Closest existing tags after the lexicon-bundle regen:
  death (18 subjects), military (27), monster (8), undead (9), magic (4).
The --grim implementation should map to a composable union of existing tags, with the original D6 tag names left as future-mining targets (a 'grim' tag could be added at mining time once we have a Tier-2 review pass that retags morphemes with affect labels). Suggested initial mapping: --grim = death OR military OR monster OR undead OR magic.

--harsh side is independent: needs a phonological score per morpheme computed from phonology.py tables. No data dependency outside what's already in the bundle.
close_reason: landed in PRs #20 (D6 knobs + D8 explainer) and #21 (gather_family refactor). All three merged into main 2026-05-02.

title: Wire D8: generator composes <lemma>@<inflection> from lexicon data
description:
DECISIONS.md D8 commits to inflection-aware generation: pick a lemma, pick an inflection, surface the appropriate form. Currently the runtime sees flat usage strings and has no concept of inflection — the lemma_id + inflection columns in the lexicon don't reach generation.

Scope:
1. Extend meanings.json export to emit per-form inflection metadata: (form, inflection_type) tuples within each language array. Backwards-compat additive.
2. Runtime: extend Meaning class to track which forms in 'sources' are inflected variants vs the lemma. Add an inflection-pick step at name composition: after picking a lemma, optionally pick an inflection (probabilistically gated by an 'inflection_density' parameter, default 0.0 = lemma-only behavior).
3. Per-position rules: e.g. genitive-strong inflection more common pre-, dative-or-pl more common post-. Keep simple to start.
4. Regression test: with inflection_density=0 names look like today; with inflection_density=0.5 generated names show measurable inflection rate.
5. Explainer: surface the inflection in the breakdown ('cot@dative-or-pl').

Acceptance: at default density, behavior unchanged; at high density, generated names show varied inflection forms; the lemma's witness count still drives the morpheme's selection probability (inflection is only a surface-form question).
notes: Closed — D8 wired end-to-end. Implementation: Meaning.pick_inflection (meaning.py:200), MeaningGenerator forwards via NameGenerator._render_substitutions (proportions.py:292), Kenning.input_schema 'inflection_density' field, --inflection-density CLI flag (cli.py:157). Bundle export emits per-language _inflections via lexicon.py. Pinned by tests/test_kenning_meaning.py (pick_inflection coverage), tests/test_kenning_proportions.py (render_substitutions + inflection_density seed-stability), tests/test_kenning.py (CLI knob seed-stability + distribution shift).

title: Wire D18: spelling variant sampling at generation time
description:
Per DECISIONS.md D18, the generator should sample from etymon_text_match.matched_form (real attested 19th-c. spellings: denu/dene/denū/dená) for archaic-feel variety, weighted by match_count. Right now generation emits only the canonical modern_usage with dashes stripped — every 'denu' name comes out as 'denu', never 'dená'.

Scope:
1. Extend export-meanings to include a spelling-variants pool per (language, lemma) tuple in meanings.json. Schema additive, backwards compatible — existing language form lists stay; a new optional sibling field carries (form, weight) tuples.
2. Runtime (proportions.py:NewName.__str__): when emitting an etymon's surface form, optionally swap in a matched_form variant via weighted choice from the pool. Gated by a 'spelling_variety' parameter (default 0.0 = canonical only).
3. New regression test: with spelling_variety=0.5 and a fixed seed, generated names show a measurable rate of variants vs canonicals.
4. Update KenningExplain to surface variant-source attribution in the explanation.

Acceptance: spelling_variety=0 reproduces today's surface forms; spelling_variety=0.5 produces variants per the weighted distribution; explainer shows where variants came from.
notes: Closed — D18 wired end-to-end. Implementation: Meaning.pick_variant (meaning.py:160), NameGenerator._render_substitutions threads spelling_variety, Kenning.input_schema 'spelling_variety' field, --spelling-variety CLI flag. Bundle export emits per-language _variants pools. Pinned by pick_variant tests + render_substitutions tests + CLI seed-stability tests. Variant pool is empty for most morphemes today (~416 with non-empty pool of ~2950) so the knob's reach is bounded by the corpus, not the wiring.

title: Wire D17: Bayesian mixture sampling + --novelty knob in name generation
description:
Per DECISIONS.md D17, name generation should sample from a mixture: alpha*empirical-pair-frequency + beta*tag-class-prior + gamma*marginal. The --novelty knob shifts weight toward gamma to allow plausible-but-unattested combinations. The Braitham Gate regression test pins the empirical end ('descriptive+topography compound first-word' must remain producible at default settings).

Currently proportions.py:Generator.select() does pure empirical-frequency weighted_choice — no tag-class prior, no marginal blending, no novelty parameter.

Scope:
1. Compute tag-class priors and marginals once at proportions-load time. Tag co-occurrence is already tracked in proportions JSON per D16 (tag_cooccurrence + tag_marginal Counters in cli.py:_proportions_from). Surface them on the runtime side via load_proportions.
2. Blend at MeaningGenerator.select() via mixture: novelty alpha=0 -> pure empirical; alpha=1 -> pure marginal. Default 0.0 (current behavior).
3. Expose 'novelty' in Kenning.input_schema as a 0..1 float. Plumb through generate(params, seed).
4. CLI: 'wyrd kenning generate --novelty 0.3 english' etc.
5. Braitham Gate regression test: at novelty=0 a known-attested compound shape must still be producible.
6. Novelty regression test: at novelty=1 generation must still produce well-formed (location-key compatible) names — no schema violation.

Acceptance: novelty 0 reproduces today's behavior bit-for-bit on the same seed; novelty 1 produces visibly different distribution with no malformed names; Braitham Gate test passes; new test pins novelty=0.5 produces a stable seed-deterministic output.
notes: Closed for the basic mixture — D17 empirical + uniform-marginal blend wired with --novelty knob (proportions.py:Generator.select + _blend_uniform). Bit-stable at novelty=0 (test_generator_select_novelty_zero_takes_fast_path), uniform-ish at novelty=1 (test_generator_select_novelty_one_picks_uniformly), Braitham Gate test passing (tests/test_kenning_cooccurrence.py:80). The third tag-class-prior term from D17 was deferred since it needs neighbor-context threaded through NameGenerator's structure walk; filed as wyrd-9gt (P3) follow-up. Acceptance criteria for wyrd-gfa as written are met.

title: Add 'breton' culture register: Brittany place-name corpus + proportions
description:
Add a new generation register for Brittany-style place names, scoped per Witcher 'remote cultured empire' framing. Brittany's etymology layers (Brythonic Celtic substrate + Latinate + Norman-French overlay) line up with the Nilfgaard sound: French-cultured, Celtic-rooted, with the Channel-Islands-style Norman accent.

Notably this ticket is the user's stated path to thicker Norman-French coverage, since NF is currently the thinnest mined language in the lexicon (111 lemmas at >=1 witness, only 7 at >=2). Brittany's Norman conquest (10th-11th c.) and continuing Norman-French overlay through medieval scholarship means a Brittany dictionary should contribute Norman-French morphemes alongside the dominant Breton/Celtic content. Pairs naturally with the Channel Islands ticket (filed wyrd-XXX) for two-pronged NF expansion.

Scope:

1. Source a PD Brittany place-name dictionary. Candidates to probe:
   - Joseph Loth, 'Chrestomathie bretonne' (1890) and related works
   - Henri Quilgars, 'Dictionnaire topographique du département de la Loire-Inférieure' (1906) — covers Brittany-adjacent
   - Albert Le Grand, Bretagne hagiography place names (older PD)
   - Émile Ernault on Breton etymology
   - Société d'Émulation des Côtes-du-Nord publications
   Need to verify PD status and digitization (Internet Archive, Gallica BnF).

2. Mine the dictionary via Tier-1 Haiku per D13 (Celtic content; Qwen weak on Brythonic).

3. Acquire a list of real Brittany town names for the proportions corpus. Candidates:
   - BAN (Base Adresse Nationale, French government open data, ODbL)
   - OpenStreetMap Brittany extract
   - Wikipedia 'List of communes of [Côtes-d'Armor / Finistère / Ille-et-Vilaine / Morbihan]'
   The four Breton-administrative départements give canonical coverage.

4. Build breton_proportions.json via the existing  flow.

5. Wire 'breton' into CULTURES () so the generator can produce breton-register names.

6. Smoke-test: generate 10 names per culture for english/scottish/welsh/irish/breton; verify breton names have the expected French-Celtic flavor (Plou-, Ker-, Lan-, -ec, -ic, -goat suffixes; Saint-* prefixes via NF).

7. Update OVERVIEW.md and DECISIONS.md if a new D-entry is warranted around the Witcher-style register design.

Out of scope:
- A separate 'cornish' register (Brythonic-Celtic without French overlay) — could be a sibling ticket if user wants.
- A 'gaulish' or 'continental Celtic' substrate register — heavier substrate-only content not currently scoped.
- Changing the runtime to support new register tags beyond the existing CULTURES enum (existing machinery handles this; just add the string).

Why this is filed: the morpheme expansion is incidental to the bigger user-facing benefit — generation now covers a French-Celtic 'remote cultured empire' register absent from the British Isles default. The proportions step is what makes it usable for the GM-facing flow.
notes:
2026-05-02 update (research session): The prior session left this ticket stuck on Le Gonidec via Gallica (403'd to curl) and Ernault 1895 (not on IA). A second-pass research probe found multiple PD Breton dictionaries directly available on Internet Archive that prior sessions missed. Concrete plan filed:
- wyrd-rd0: Troude 1876 (863 p, multi-dialect labels) — primary corpus
- wyrd-mlu: Loth 1890 Chrestomathie (Brythonic incl Welsh+Cornish, 548 p) — re-evaluation; was MIS-CHARACTERIZED as 'essay-shaped, low yield' by prior session
- wyrd-13r: Le Gonidec/Villemarqué 1850 augmented (614 p) — second-witness layer (depends on wyrd-rd0)
- wyrd-22e: Châlons-Loth 1895 Vannetais (137 p) — D18 dialect-variant pool (depends on wyrd-rd0 + wyrd-mlu)

Le Gonidec 1821 ORIGINAL is at archive.org/details/bub_gb_0i6UBl4mvfYC — bypasses Gallica entirely. Just the older typeface gives rougher OCR than the 1850 La Villemarqué edition.

title: Per-language witness thresholds in export-meanings
description:
Currently export-meanings uses a uniform --min-witnesses N (default 3) across all languages. The corpus availability differs hugely by language: old-english has 32 mined sources and 2118 lemmas at ≥1 witness, while old-norse has effectively one focused dictionary (Lindkvist 1912) and the structural ceiling at ≥3 witnesses is 43 ON lemmas. A uniform 3-witness gate filters out 93% of ON, mostly for corpus-thinness reasons rather than quality.

Quality spot-check at w=2 (per-language samples drawn 2026-05-02):
- old-english: ~80% clean (some Tier-1 prose-extraction noise like 'row' glossed as 'clearing')
- celtic: ~90% clean (dearg, meen, eidnedin all real)
- old-norse: ~95% clean (hylr, haukr, bygging, blá, kirkja all real)
- modern-english: 100% clean (mill, stone, head, east, hall)
- norman-french: 100% clean (blanche, lieu, castle, monte)
- latin: 100% clean (ecclesia, ceaster, monasterium)
- biblical: 100% clean (asa, asaph saint names)

Recommended preset:
- old-english: 3 (well-mined; strict gate keeps OE Tier-1 noise out)
- celtic: 2 (mining structurally harder per D13)
- old-norse: 2 (corpus structurally thin)
- modern-english: 2
- norman-french: 2
- latin: 2
- biblical: 2
- germanic, greek: nothing at ≥2 anyway; threshold moot, ride rando-port path only

Net effect: ~+377 lemmas vs uniform w=3, mostly Celtic (+278) and ON (+75).
close_reason: Merged in PR #15. RECOMMENDED_LANG_THRESHOLDS preset live: OE at 3 (well-mined), Celtic/ON/modern-English/Norman-French/Latin/biblical at 2. CLI: --lang-threshold LANG=N (repeatable, accepts JSON-field aliases) + --no-preset. Production export: +340 modern_usages, +285 subjects vs uniform w=3, mostly Celtic (+278) and ON (+46).
