title: Build alphabetical-dictionary parser for non-Skeat books
description: Mawer, Ekwall, Johnston, Joyce, Watson — all in alphabetical-entry format rather than Skeat's TOC+suffix-section format. Current parser returns 0 entries on these. Need a generic alphabetical parser: detect headword (capitalized at paragraph start), extract entry body up to next headword. Then feed to the same LLM extractor. Covers the remaining 27 books in sources/.
notes:
Starting work — pilot on Mawer Northumberland-Durham 1920 first, then test against Ekwall and Johnston for format coverage.
Phase 1 done: pilot on Mawer Northumberland-Durham succeeded. Parser handles Skeat-format AND alphabetical-dictionary format with auto-detection. Working well on: Mawer NorthDur (838 entries), Ekwall Lancs (499), Duignan Staffs (337), Harrison Liverpool (215), Watson Ross (652), Watson Celtic (474), Joyce vol 3 (606), Morgans (~830), Macbain (178), Gillies Argyll (155).

Still problematic (deferred):
- Taylor 1893: parser grabs back-of-book index entries (toponym + page number, no etymology body). Needs back-matter / index detection.
- Joyce vol 1: thematic chapters not alphabetical — wrong shape entirely. Skip; vol 3 is the dictionary.
- Lindkvist, Wyld/Hirst, Mawer 1922/1924/Stenton: small/methodological volumes with mixed content — low yield expected.
- Watson 1926 has some 3-letter false-positive headwords leaking through (Ady, Ann, Arch, Bede).

title: Sonnet/Haiku second pass for low-confidence LLM extractions
description: Qwen 9B leaks modern forms ('king' instead of 'cyning', 'mill' instead of 'myln', 'town' instead of 'tun') on some entries, and misreads attestation fragments as etymons (Croxton: 'estone'). Add a review CLI that picks toponym_etymology rows with confidence in (medium, low) and notes containing 'extracted_by:llm:qwen', re-runs them via the Anthropic API (Haiku first, Sonnet for residue), and inserts new rows from the better extractor. Old rows stay; consensus view shows where they agree/disagree.
notes:
Pivot to Gemini for second-pass review — user has GEMINI_API_KEY configured but no Anthropic key. Less bureaucratic: free-tier covers expected volume, paid pricing for 2.5-flash is very cheap (~$0.075/M input). Will build as a parallel client to OllamaClient with the same extract_one signature, then add --provider {ollama|gemini} flag on mine-llm.
Implemented as 'wyrd kenning lexicon review <source_dir>' command. Dry-runs by default; --apply to insert new toponym_etymology rows tagged with extracted_by:gemini:<model>. Idempotent — skips toponyms that already have a Gemini row. Filters by --book / --confidence / --limit. Tested end-to-end against the in-progress DB (3 Cambridgeshire entries, ~36s for 3 calls). Ready to run for real after the current Ollama mining job finishes.
close_reason: Implemented as 'wyrd kenning lexicon review'. 128 Gemini-reviewed Mawer rows written this session. Bug fixed mid-run: bare TimeoutError now caught in both extractors.

title: Populate reflex.productivity counts
description: reflex.productivity is currently always 0. Should be the count of distinct toponyms that use this (surface_form, position) reflex, derived from toponym_etymology_element joins. Drives generator weighting later.

title: Capture word-level positional bias for modifier words
description: Single-word modifiers like 'Great', 'Long', 'Old', 'Little' are pre-only ('Great Bevvy' yes, 'Bevvy Great' no). Cardinal-direction words like 'North', 'South' are flexible (both 'North Stoke' and 'Stoke North' attested). Current schema captures intra-word morpheme position (pre/inner/post within a compound) but NOT inter-word position (which word slot in a multi-word name). Need either: (a) new name_modifier table with per-word-position counts derived from observed toponyms; (b) an inter_word_position field on something. The generator currently treats single-word modifiers as positionally free, which produces unnatural names.

title: Move confidence from toponym_etymology to per-element
description: Scholars hedge per-element ('the prefix is clearly X; the suffix may be Y'). Currently we record one confidence per breakdown. Move confidence to toponym_etymology_element; keep an aggregate on the parent for back-compat queries.

title: OCR ligature normalization for etymon canonical_form
description: Skeat OCR consistently mangles æ→cs, æ→ce, ð→§. Etymons end up as 'hcsdan' (should be 'hædan') or 'hy§' (should be 'hyð'). Add a normalize_ocr_form() pass that maps these back, applied at upsert_etymon() time. Pairs with the lemma work (variants under one lemma).
notes:
Implemented normalize_ocr_form() and cluster_ocr_variants() with dry-run/apply modes. Tested. Will run as a post-mining pass.
Lexicon README + arch note added at wyrd/generators/kenning/README.md covering data model, authoring flow, key invariants, module map, and CLI cheatsheet. Helps future-us stay oriented.
close_reason: OCR ligature normalization applied: 43 variant-pairs merged. Sat upstream of the lemma pass and let it work on cleaned forms.

title: Add lemma_id self-FK on etymon for variant collapse
description: Inflected forms (Hæda/Hædan) and OCR/macron variants (hām/hamm/ham) currently become separate etymon rows, breaking consensus counts. Add etymon.lemma_id (nullable self-FK) so variants point at a canonical lemma. Update etymon_consensus view to roll up to lemma. Backfill via clustering pass over canonical_form within each language.
close_reason: Schema migrated, inflection-strip linker shipped. 50 lemma links applied; cross-witnessed etymons rose from 113 to 133. Known false-positive class (OE adj↔noun) tolerable for now.

title: Bundle export: <lang>_english_shaped + _transliteration siblings absent (wyrd-vsrn Phase 2c regression?)
description:
Discovered during wyrd-j43l bundle re-export:

The bundle has 0 word-level <lang>_english_shaped and <lang>_transliteration sibling fields, despite:
- 48,070 etymon rows carrying english_shaped values in the live DB
- Emission code present at lexicon.py:6997 (_emit_english_shaped_list)
- wyrd-vsrn Phase 2c being listed as a completed milestone

The bucket.english_shaped map in the family-collector path is apparently empty for every family. _absorb_member_english_shaped (lexicon.py:6828) populates it from member_english_shaped_by_id but somehow not getting through.

Reproduction:
1. wyrd kenning lexicon export-meanings --output /tmp/test-bundle.json
2. python3 -c "import json; b=json.load(open('/tmp/test-bundle.json')); n=sum(1 for s in b['subjects'] for w in s.get('words',[]) for k in w if k.endswith('_english_shaped')); print(n)"
3. Returns 0; expected non-zero.

Not a blocker for wyrd-j43l deploy — the bundle is otherwise healthy and the bundle SPA consumers gracefully degrade on missing siblings. But it means the user-visible multi-script rendering feature (etymological-provenance panel) won't have english_shaped data to display.

Should investigate the family-collector → bucket-absorb chain. Could be:
- collect_family_members not joining english_shaped column
- _absorb_member_english_shaped not appending to bucket
- bucket-to-word emission code skipping the field on a None/empty check

title: Add toponym_attestation to DIFF_REBUILD_TABLES + extend _l2_state_snapshot
description:
pr-test-analyzer on PR #204 flagged that DIFF_REBUILD_TABLES (wyrd/generators/kenning/jsonl_build.py:45) doesn't include toponym_attestation. The diff-rebuild operator workflow (lexicon rebuild-from-jsonl --diff) is the human-facing guard against round-trip regressions; without attestation in the monitored set, a future regression that silently drops all attestations would produce a zero-delta diff and go undetected.

PR #204 closes the dump-side gap. Now that attestation round-trips, it's safe (and necessary) to add it to the diff guard.

Changes needed:
1. Add 'toponym_attestation' to DIFF_REBUILD_TABLES
2. Extend _l2_state_snapshot in tests/test_kenning_jsonl_build.py to include attestation rows
3. Verify the format_diff_rebuild output reads sensibly when attestation count drops/rises
4. Bundle pre-existing similar gaps if any (check toponym_etymology coverage)

This is pre-existing — was out of scope for PR #204.

title: Add dump-side orphan-attestation telemetry (counter + warn)
description:
silent-failure-hunter on PR #204 flagged that dump_all_sources silently drops attestation rows whose source_doc routes nowhere (no direct source_id match, no registered prefix). The build side has attestation_orphans telemetry; the dump side has nothing.

Risk: a new ingester or a typo introduces source_docs that don't match any pattern, and the rows disappear from JSONL dumps. Six months later, a lexicon rebuild-from-jsonl produces a smaller DB with no explanation.

Implementation sketch:
- One-shot query at the end of dump_all_sources counting toponym_attestation rows whose source_doc neither equals any source.id nor starts with any registered prefix
- click.echo a warning with the count when non-zero
- Optionally surface as a return value for programmatic callers

Out of scope on PR #204 (Phase A — code skeleton); filing here for Phase B.

title: Refactor _insert_etymon — extract _merge_etymon_conflict helper
description:
Per complexity-reviewer on PR #203: _insert_etymon grew from ~22 lines to 68 lines after the wyrd-pcsj upsert fix. The else: branch (lines 172-204 — SELECT existing id + defensive None-check + UPDATE non-key scalars) is a self-contained unit that could be extracted to a module-level _merge_etymon_conflict(conn, payload, cols) -> int helper. That would bring _insert_etymon back to ~25 lines.

Also bundle (per silent-failure-hunter same PR):
* Document _NON_SCHOLAR_SOURCES + the _ETYMON_INSERT_COLUMNS allowlist explicitly so the L2/L3 boundary intent is clearer at the call site.
* Pre-existing concern: jsonl_build.table_counts catches sqlite3.OperationalError silently with no logging — a 'database is locked' or schema mismatch makes has_any_delta return True and fail CI with no diagnosis. Add logger.warning.
* Pre-existing concern: jsonl_build._insert_toponym uses plain INSERT — currently safe (toponym table has no UNIQUE constraint), but document the asymmetry with _insert_etymon's upsert so a future schema change adding a UNIQUE to toponym doesn't silently regress.

Tests added in PR #203 cover the merge contract; the refactor should be regression-safe.

title: Refactor: extract helpers in diff-bundle command + bundle_diff module
description:
complexity-reviewer + import-reviewer flagged three deferrable refactors in PR #201 (wyrd-w3x0). All were explicitly marked as 'beads ticket / deferral acceptable' by the reviewers; bundling them into one follow-up:

1. **format_bundle_diff is too long** (bundle_diff.py, ~93 lines). The 'emit capped list with ... and N more' pattern repeats identically for added/removed/changed subjects. Extract a module-level _emit_capped_list helper, plus a _format_subjects_section and _format_other_fields_section.

2. **lang-threshold parser duplication** (cli.py). The 16-line lang-threshold parsing block in lexicon_diff_bundle is a verbatim copy of the same block in lexicon_export_meanings (around cli.py:1311-1330). Extract a module-level _parse_lang_thresholds(specs, use_preset) helper and call it from both commands so they can't drift.

3. **lexicon_diff_bundle body is too long** (cli.py, ~90 lines across 6 phases: validate flags, load joiners, L1 bulk ingest, L2 replay, L3 enrichment, export+assemble+diff). Identified two natural split points: _rebuild_lexicon_db(rebuilt_path, jsonl_dir, fetch_bulk, skip_bulk) and _assemble_bundle_dict(db, ...). Note the tmpdir lifetime needs to outlive the rebuild → bundle flow, so the helpers may need to accept the open tmpdir path rather than create their own.

4. **Undocumented deferred imports across cli.py** (import-reviewer flagged this as a pre-existing pattern). Bulk-add 'why is this deferred' comments to the function-local imports in lexicon commands (diff-rebuild, rebuild-from-jsonl, fetch-bulk-sources, etc.) so future readers know whether the deferral is for help-snappiness, circular-import avoidance, or just historical accident. Could also collapse the redundant init_schema re-imports across all those functions in one pass.

Scope each as a separate commit so reviewers can land them independently. Tests already cover the surface: the round-trip test (wyrd-xrnw / test_kenning_hidb_phase3_round_trip.py) + the bundle-diff tests (test_kenning_bundle_diff.py + test_kenning_diff_bundle_cli.py) catch any behavioral regression from the extractions.

title: Refactor format_enrichment_run into per-section helpers
description:
complexity-reviewer on PR #199 flagged format_enrichment_run for repetition: 5 new per-pass sections all follow the same 'if result.get(key) is not None: lines.extend([heading, *fields])' pattern. Table-driven extraction (a (key, heading, render_fn) tuple per section) keeps the function declarative and makes adding the 9th pass — or rendering the same data to a different format — a one-line change.

Defer-acceptable now: the repetition is only mildly annoying at 5 sections. If Phase 3 adds more sections (per-pass timing breakdowns, etc.) the refactor pays off then.

title: Unit tests for decompose_all / derive_english_shaped_all / classify_stratum_all
description:
PR #199 (wyrd-hidb Phase 2) added three new L3 wrappers but did NOT add direct unit tests for each — only an empty-DB smoke that proves the chain composes. Test-coverage-reviewer flagged:

* decompose_all: no test for rule-firing distribution (scholar / scholar-disagreement / unique-zero / tiebreaker / no-canonical) against a synthetic toponym + etymon fixture.
* derive_english_shaped_all: no test for language-filter behavior, reshape flag, or the english_shaped IS NULL gate.
* classify_stratum_all: no test for the stratum IS NULL idempotency gate (re-run skips already-stratum'd rows), no test for the per-language by_stratum counter shape.

Acceptance:
* Each wrapper has 3-5 focused unit tests over a small synthetic DB built inside the test (per the fixture-data-reviewer rules).
* format_enrichment_run gets per-section tests (currently zero direct coverage).

Defer-acceptable: round-trip integration test in wyrd-hidb Phase 3 will exercise these end-to-end. But unit tests catch regressions cheaper than the round-trip.

Linked to wyrd-hidb.

title: Etymology-alignment audit: reason categorization + non-OE stop-morphemes + shared audit-base
description:
Three deferred items from PR #191 reviewer (wyrd-8upf):

1. **Categorize MisalignmentFinding by reason**: the heuristic flags both 'genuine hallucination' (element doesn't appear in prose) and 'incomplete reconstruction' (historical_form has fewer morphemes than the element list). Operator workflow would benefit from a flag-reason field (e.g., 'reason': 'hallucinated' | 'incomplete' | 'empty_form') so triage can focus on one class at a time.

2. **Extend _STOP_MORPHEMES for non-OE corpora**: the current set ({a,e,i,o,u,es,ing,an,en,s,n,r}) is OE-biased. Old French / Irish / Norse / Welsh have their own elision-prone inflections. Examples worth investigating:
   - OE -um, -on (dative/accusative plural)
   - ON -ar, -ir (nom/acc plural)
   - OF -e, -es (silent endings)
   - Irish gen sing -a, -e
   The over-flag pattern likely concentrates in the Joyce / arbois / lindkvist sources where these inflections appear.

3. **Shared audit-base abstraction (third audit triggers extraction)**: wyrd-bd68 (short_quote) and wyrd-8upf (etymology alignment) are now two near-identical audit modules. Same skeleton: SourceAuditResult dataclass, AuditReport, audit_jsonl_file/audit_jsonl_dir with underscore-prefix skip and _op=remove skip, format_audit_report top-N markdown. Per the wyrd-rbms playbook (defer DRY until 4th instance triggers extraction), do NOT extract yet — but file the tracking ticket so the abstraction has a home when audit #3 arrives.

Linked to wyrd-eni4 epic.

title: Re-mine top-5 short_quote-truncation offenders with larger LLM context window
description:
The wyrd-bd68 audit (docs/audits/2026-05-13_short_quote_truncation.md, committed in PR #190) identified 2,038 probably-truncated short_quote citations across 51 sources. Top-5 sources account for ~37% of the total flagged:

  mawer_1920_northumberland_durham      283 / 1165 (24.3%)
  joyce_1898_irish_names_vol3           151 /  429 (35.2%)
  ekwall_1922_lancashire                134 /  609 (22.0%)
  joyce_1913_irish_names_of_places      121 /  332 (36.4%)
  watson_1926_celtic_place_names...     117 /  272 (43.0%)

Approach options:
1. Re-mine with larger context window (qwen3.5:35b-a3b or anthropic claude-sonnet-4-5) — recovers the cut-off citation context at the cost of LLM compute.
2. Context-snippet refill: pull missing context from sources/<book>.txt via the citation page number (wyrd-9kh.4/.5 infrastructure exists for this).

Acceptance: post-pass re-run of `lexicon audit-short-quotes` shows the top-5 offenders' truncated counts cut by ≥75%. Append the new snapshot to docs/audits/.

Why now: audit snapshot is the evidence; the connection between audit and re-mining work fades if not filed contemporaneously. Per PR #190 reviewer recommendation.

Linked to wyrd-eni4 epic (Phase-2-ish curation pass).

title: Extract shared operator-CSV ingester base after 4th instance
description:
Three operator-CSV-templated ingesters now exist:
- wyrd/generators/kenning/hundred_rolls_ingester.py (wyrd-3atv)
- wyrd/generators/kenning/speed_1611_ingester.py (wyrd-myh1)
- wyrd/generators/kenning/hearth_tax_ingester.py (wyrd-myh1)

All three share the same skeleton: iter_csv_rows() → build_events() → ingest(), with _normalize_row producing a (toponym, attestation) pair, plus a CsvSchemaError class, _toponym_ref helper, and a _SOURCE_ROW constant.

Per the 'three similar lines is better than premature abstraction' rule and PR #188 reviewer recommendation, extraction is deferred until a 4th instance arrives. Each ingester also has source-specific bits (column names, default year semantics, source_doc format, OutOfRangeYearWarning for Hearth Tax) that complicate a shared base.

When the 4th ingester is needed, extract a shared CsvIngester base or similar abstraction in wyrd/generators/kenning/_operator_csv_ingester.py:
- Generic iter_csv_rows with required-columns parameter
- Generic build_events with seen_toponym_refs dedup
- Generic ingest with counts dict
- Subclass-specific _normalize_row, _SOURCE_ROW, source_doc formatter

Don't extract before then — the source-specific divergence is real and each ingester is small (~150 LoC) and self-contained.

title: CLI integration tests for lexicon prune-toponym + curate-etymon
description:
Per test-coverage-reviewer on PR #180 (wyrd-lene): the lexicon_prune_toponym CLI command and its UsageError ref-validation guard are untested. Same gap likely applies to lexicon_curate_etymon from wyrd-2jhs.

Add click.testing.CliRunner integration tests covering:
- prune-toponym: append-on-success, file-not-found error, ref-not-in-file error (the new ref-validation guard), reason field captured, --jsonl-dir override
- curate-etymon: --lemma-ref / --merged-into-ref happy paths, mutual-exclusivity rejection, --reason captured

Adjacent existing test pattern: tests/test_kenning_lexicon.py uses CliRunner for other CLI commands; follow that shape.

Deferred from wyrd-lene PR since the inner logic (replay_file resolution, payload assembly, file append) is covered indirectly via the apply_curation_overrides tests and the wyrd-lene end-to-end smoke.

title: Refactor build_from_jsonl Pass 3 into per-row-type helper functions
description:
Per complexity-reviewer on PR #180 (wyrd-lene): build_from_jsonl Pass 3 is ~70 lines with four similarly-shaped fact-row loops (citation / etymon_descent / mining_run / etymology_element). Each loop is extractable to a module-level _insert_*_rows helper.

Suggested signatures:
  _insert_citation_rows(conn, source_id, citations, etymon_id_by_ref, counts)
  _insert_descent_rows(conn, source_id, edges, etymon_id_by_ref, counts)
  _insert_mining_run_rows(conn, source_id, runs)
  _insert_etymology_element_rows(conn, source_id, rows, toponym_id_by_ref, etymon_id_by_ref, counts)

Reduces build_from_jsonl body length, keeps each helper testable in isolation, and makes the orphan-skip pattern centralized so future row types follow the same shape.

Deferred from wyrd-lene PR since the complexity comes from incremental additions (wyrd-f295 baseline + wyrd-tzf2 dedup + wyrd-lene orphan-skip), not from this PR specifically.

title: Dedupe exact-duplicate toponym_etymology rows from re-run LLM mining
description:
Per Gemini review of PR #175 round 2: data/mining/bannister_1916_herefordshire.jsonl has exact-duplicate etymology_element rows (e.g., 'Cart@Herefordshire' / 'ac-tun' appears twice on lines 309-310; 'Dom@Herefordshire' / 'Ceabba-bank' twice on lines 320-321).

Root cause: toponym_etymology table has no UNIQUE constraint on (toponym_id, source_id, historical_form, element-list-shape). When mining is re-run with the same model+prompt against the same source, the writer inserts a second identical row.

Two fix paths (not mutually exclusive):
1. Add UNIQUE constraint to toponym_etymology preventing exact dupes (probably (toponym_id, source_id, COALESCE(historical_form,''), provenance)).
2. Dedupe at dump time — content-equal etymology_element rows fold to one canonical-state row.

Currently the dump faithfully preserves what's in the DB (round-trip claim intact), so dedup is a separate data-quality pass. Adjacent to wyrd-lene (hallucinated toponyms) but operates on duplicate rows, not on wrong rows.

title: Audit toponym/etymology cross-misalignment in scholar mining
description:
Per Gemini review of PR #175: some toponym_etymology rows link a toponym to etymons that don't match the citation's actual breakdown.

Concrete example:
- mawer_stenton_1930_sussex.jsonl:143 — 'DownLanp Woop' (likely 'Downland Wood') is linked to old-english:hoh + historical form 'Hooe', but the associated citation (line 51) clearly says 'William ater Dune' (suggesting dun + land elements).

This is a structural LLM extraction error — element list doesn't match the citation prose. Fix requires audit + emit 'remove' or 'set' events on the affected toponym_etymology rows.

Scope: probably more than the one Gemini caught. Sample 100 random toponym_etymology rows and check element-list↔citation-prose alignment; extrapolate.

title: Re-mine entries with truncated short_quote citations
description:
Per Gemini review of PR #175: many short_quote fields in scholar-mined L2 files end mid-sentence ('| Ab', 'of the ') — the LLM extraction truncated context.

The truncation makes citations less verifiable for the SPA's etymological-provenance panel (wyrd-9kh.6). The fix is a re-mining pass with a longer context window OR a post-process pass that pulls full quotes from sources/<book>.txt via the citation page number (wyrd-9kh.4 + .5 infrastructure already exists for that).

Concrete examples surfaced by Gemini:
- bannister_1916_herefordshire.jsonl:101 (many rows)

Scope: full audit across all 51 sources to find every truncated row, then operator chooses re-mine vs context-snippet refill. Curation event log (Phase 2b / wyrd-2jhs) is the application mechanism.

title: Data quality: hallucinated toponyms from LLM extraction
description:
Per Gemini review of PR #175 (wyrd-f295 foundation): multiple toponym rows in the L2 backfill are LLM extraction errors where bibliography strings / abbreviations / publication titles were misidentified as toponyms.

Concrete examples:
- bannister_1916_herefordshire.jsonl: 'Cart', 'Dom', 'Eccles', 'Reg', 'Survey', 'Surveys' (Cart. → Cartulary, etc.)
- harrison_1898_liverpool.jsonl: 'Proceedings Archeol' (journal title)
- johnston_1892_place_names_of_scotland.jsonl: 'Arg' (extraction error for 'Leven', confirmed by notes field on line 178)
- longnon_1920_noms_de_lieu_france_v1.jsonl: 'Aculiacac' (modern name should be 'Aguilcourt', region 'Aisne')

Fix approach (post-wyrd-f295):
1. Audit toponyms with suspicious patterns (very short, all-caps abbreviations, journal/publication words, no real-world referent)
2. Emit 'remove' events on the affected toponym + toponym_etymology rows to the appropriate source JSONL files
3. Compact when batch is reviewed

Adjacent to wyrd-8wgr (dead-rando prune for etymons) but operates on TOPONYMS, not morphemes. Same workflow shape.

title: Source row metadata cleanup (author=unknown, stale notes)
description:
Per Gemini review of PR #175: several backfilled source rows carry incomplete metadata that's fixable from the bibliography:

- mawer_stenton_1925_buckinghamshire — author missing; should be 'A. Mawer and F.M. Stenton'; title should be 'The Place-Names of Buckinghamshire' (English Place-Name Society Vol 2)
- goodall_1914_sw_yorkshire — notes field still says 'book may not have been mined yet' even though the file contains extensive mining results

Probable full sweep value: many other sources likely have similar stale notes or incomplete author/year/region fields from the early reverse-search-creates-stub workflow.

Fix: append 'patch' events to the affected source rows on the per-source JSONL files. Lightweight; can be a single PR once the bibliography is gathered.

title: Phase 4a: Cross-era surfacing in dashboard (per-toponym era timeline)
description:
Per user 2026-05-12: once we have Domesday (1086) + Hundred Rolls (1279) + Speed (1611) + Hearth Tax (1660s) + modern (Wikipedia/OS), the dashboard should surface PER-TOPONYM era timelines:

  Acton:

title: Expose public phonology_chain_for() API; stop importing _PHONOLOGY_* privates from lexicon.py
description:
During wyrd-pmne review, the generator-contract reviewer flagged that wyrd/generators/kenning/language_quality.py imports three module-private symbols across the lexicon.py boundary:

- _phonology_rule_form
- _PHONOLOGY_FAMILY_CHAINS
- _PHONOLOGY_LANGUAGE_ALIASES

These are leading-underscore private symbols (per Python convention) and the cross-module import freezes their names as a de-facto public API. Any future refactor (consolidating chain registration, moving rules into phonology_rules.py) will have to update the reporting code as a side effect.

Recommendation: expose a public API in phonology_rules.py (or a new wyrd/generators/kenning/phonology.py module):

- phonology_chain_for(language: str) -> tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]] | None
- phonology_rule_form(canonical_form, from_language, to_language) -> str | None

Then have language_quality.py consume those public functions, and gradually migrate the lexicon.py call sites too.

Not blocking — wyrd-pmne shipped with the function-local-import pattern, which keeps the blast radius small. But the convention violation is real and worth cleaning up before another consumer (KenningEraMap explainer? Tier-4 mining tool?) adopts the same pattern.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #171. phonology_rules.py now exposes FAMILY_CHAINS, LANGUAGE_ALIASES, chain_for(), resolve_language(), rule_form() as the public API. language_quality.py + lexicon.py consume the public API; no more privately-named cross-module imports. 757 affected tests pass.

Tier 4 isn't persisted to the DB — it's synthesized on-demand by etymon_era_reflexes() at bundle-export time via _phonology_rule_form().

2. Persist Tier 4 outputs as a synthetic etymon_era_reflex row during bundle export so the metric has data to count. Mirrors wyrd-jbcu's source-tagged design.
3. Add a separate 'Tier 4 (synthesized)' line to the F breakdown that calls the live function for bundle-shipped etymons only (denominator-friendly).

Acceptance:

- Tests for the count

Dashboard F detail now shows Tier 4 phonology count with full-population walk; modern-english reads 1,346,968/1,376,099 (97.9%), middle-english 99.6%, OE 44.0%, welsh 41.8%, OW 20.4%; non-chain languages render n/a. title: Variant pool inheritance from cluster mates pollutes per-morpheme variants
description:
Surfaced during wyrd-r1ks (PR #166) review. The bundle's per-morpheme `_variants` pool inherits variants from CLUSTER MATES via the family rollup, so a toponymic suffix like OE `-ing-` gets variant entries from semantically-unrelated etymons that share the cluster.

Concrete example: OE `-ing-` (the patronymic / habitative suffix as in 'Readingas') ends up with variants:
  inēode  (past tense of ingān 'to go in')
  ingānne (gerund of ingān)
  ingum   (dative plural of ingang)

These are verb conjugations of the SEPARATE etymon `ingān` (a verb meaning 'to enter'). The family rollup joins `-ing-`, `ingān`, and other 'ing'-rooted etymons into one cluster, and the bundle export's `_absorb_member_variants` then attaches every member's variants to every other member's bundle slot.

This means `--spelling-variety > 0` can substitute a toponymic suffix with a verb conjugation, generating nonsensical names.

Fix paths to consider:
1. Filter variants by surface-similarity to the canonical form at export time (Levenshtein distance, edit-ratio, or shared-prefix heuristic)
2. Be more conservative at family rollup time — don't union variants across cluster mates of DIFFERENT modifier_type or different first-letter
3. Accept the noise — spelling_variety is opt-in; users dialing it up are signing up for some level of variation. Add a docstring warning.
4. Track variant provenance (which member of the cluster contributed it) and prefer same-canonical-form variants at sample time

Acceptance:
- Sample 10+ bundle morphemes with non-empty variants
- Verify that for at least 80%, the variant surface is morphologically related to the morpheme's canonical form
- If filtering by similarity, ensure morphological variants (plural / dative / mutated initial) STAY in the pool

Lower priority than other cluster work because:
- spelling_variety is opt-in
- the wrong variants don't break decomposition, just generation-time spelling-rendering
- the variants ARE valid OE/ON forms, just semantically off

Tracked as wyrd-r1ks follow-up.

title: Ingest modern-english wiktextract slice for true modern-english IPA
description:
Follow-up to wyrd-69s5. The corpus-miner code fix landed in PR #158, and PR #159 backfilled the existing etymons via re-mining. Resulting bundle IPA coverage:

  celtic_mix       40.1%
  old_english      39.8%
  modern_english   19.7%   <-- INHERITED, see below
  old_french       15.0%
  old_scandinavian  1.7%
  latin             0.0%

The modern_english figure is misleading — it's NOT real modern-english pronunciation. The DB has 0/21,175 modern-english etymons with IPA because there's no wiktextract_modern_english.jsonl slice on disk; _LANG_TO_SLICE_BASENAME has modern-english: None.

What's actually happening: the bundle export's family rollup (_absorb_member_pronunciation in lexicon.py around line 6918) keys pronunciation by (lang, form) tuples. When a middle-english member has form='brede' and the modern_english bucket's forms list also contains 'brede', the export attaches the ME IPA under the modern_english slot for the matching form. So the 19.7% is cluster-mate IPA inheritance, mostly from middle-english.

Concrete example diagnosed: 'brede' shows IPA '/ˈbrɛ̝ːd(ə)/' in modern_english_pronunciation. DB:
  middle-english 'brede' → IPA '/ˈbrɛ̝ːd(ə)/'  (source)
  modern-english 'brede' → IPA None
  old-english 'brede'    → IPA '/ˈbre.de/'      (different)

Whether to KEEP the cluster-mate inheritance for modern_english is a separate UX call — for an etymological-provenance panel, showing 'inherited from ME' alongside the form might be informative. For a strict 'this is the modern English pronunciation' UI, it's misleading.

Two paths to get REAL modern-english IPA:

PATH 1: Download Kaikki's modern English wiktextract slice
- URL: https://kaikki.org/dictionary/English/kaikki.org-dictionary-English.jsonl (or similar)
- Size: ~1-2 GB compressed, possibly 5-10 GB uncompressed (~1M entries)
- Acquisition: wget / curl + place at sources/wiktextract_english.jsonl
- Code: register in _LANG_TO_SLICE_BASENAME with the path; add modern-english to per-culture _LANG_TO_SLICE_BASENAME if not already mapped via culture scope
- Mining run: re-run mine-wiktextract-corpus --apply --culture all
- Coverage estimate: every modern English place-name fragment that hits will get IPA from the slice
- Trade-off: heaviest path; covers all English etymons; same machinery as other slices

PATH 2: Lighter-weight modern English IPA dictionary
- Sources: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (American English IPA), or a focused Wiktionary IPA-only dump
- Size: ~10-100 MB
- New ingest path: not via wiktextract_corpus_miner; would need a CMU-dict-aware ingester
- Coverage estimate: CMU has ~134K entries, mostly common words
- Trade-off: smaller download but separate code path; less consistent with other slices' shape

Acceptance:
- A wiktextract_modern_english.jsonl (or wiktextract_english.jsonl) slice on disk under sources/
- _LANG_TO_SLICE_BASENAME mapping points to it
- mine-wiktextract-corpus --apply --culture english --slice modern-english (or via 'all') runs and writes IPA on modern-english etymons
- Bundle re-export shows modern_english_pronunciation with IPA from the actual modern-english entries (not just inherited from middle-english)
- Per-language IPA % in COVERAGE.md sees a meaningful jump for modern_english (target: 50%+)

Optional additional work (stretch):
- Decide whether the cluster-mate inheritance behaviour should be kept or stripped after real IPA fills in
- If kept, surface it explicitly in the SPA's etymological panel ('IPA from middle-english 'brede'') to avoid misleading the user
- Consider whether to also ingest the FULL English slice via wyrd kenning lexicon ingest-wiktionary (which would pick up etymology + descent edges too)

title: Audit + clean up rando-port grandfathered bundle entries with no scholar witnesses
description:
The export_meanings 'include_rando=True' path admits any etymon family containing a rando-port-cited entry, regardless of scholar witness threshold. This is documented intentional grandfathering ('legacy seed kept until corroborated') but it now ships morphemes that have ZERO scholar witnesses with no path to corroboration.

Concrete example surfaced 2026-05-09: 'Haver-' (Goat) with old-french root → bundle citation list shows just ekwall_1922_lancashire, but the underlying old-french 'chèvre' etymon has only the rando-port citation in etymon_citation. It's in the bundle solely because rando-port admitted it, not because any scholar attested 'Haver-' as Goat in old-french.

Investigation:
1. Query the lexicon DB for all etymons cited ONLY by rando-port (no other source). That's the grandfather list.
2. For each, check if any sibling etymon in the same family (lemma_id rollup) has scholar witnesses. If yes → already corroborated, can drop the rando-port-only sibling without losing bundle coverage. If no → the entire family rides on rando-port.
3. For families riding solely on rando-port, decide:
   - Keep (the morpheme might be real; rando-port was hand-curated, not random)
   - Investigate via wiktionary-forms / wiktionary-corpus mining to find independent attestation
   - Drop (if the gloss looks suspicious or the morpheme is rare)

Expected scope: the original rando-port bundle was ~747 subjects. Many overlap with later mining. The pure-grandfather slice is probably 100-300 subjects.

Acceptance:
- A query returns: {language: count} of pure-rando-port-grandfathered families
- A spot-check of 20 randomly-sampled grandfather entries surfaces which look real (-ton, -ham, -mill kind) vs which look questionable (Haver-=Goat kind)
- Either a one-time cleanup pass that drops the questionable entries, or a doc that says 'we keep them all, here's why'

title: Audit kenning test suite for live-bundle dependencies, migrate to swap_bundle fixture
description:
The wyrd-b7fo deploy surfaced 10 tests that broke because the live meanings.json bundle changed shape and contents (4.5× growth post-wyrd-eni4). Those 10 are now migrated to the swap_bundle fixture pattern (tests/conftest.py: EXPLAIN_TEST_BUNDLE), but the rest of the suite hasn't been audited. The next mining session that re-emits the bundle will tip more tests off if any of them implicitly depend on the live bundle's specific contents.

Audit list candidates (anything reading meanings.json):

    rg -l 'meanings\.json|_load_meanings\(\)|_build_word_db|bundle_word_db' tests/

For each, decide:

* **Behavioural pin** (asserts on a specific decomposition,
  language pick, count, tag pair): MIGRATE to swap_bundle +
  EXPLAIN_TEST_BUNDLE. Add new fixture entries if the test needs
  morphemes the current fixture lacks.
* **Live-bundle smoke test** (broad-stroke regression guard with
  generous floor — like
  test_find_meaning_runs_full_bundled_corpus_without_crashing or
  test_sidecar_lifts_irish_corpus_perfect_rate): KEEP against the
  live bundle, but make the threshold generous enough that bundle
  churn doesn't trip it.
* **Bundle-shape contract** (asserts on schema, fields, etc.):
  KEEP against live bundle, but make sure dict-shape iteration is
  used (data['subjects'] if isinstance(data, dict) else data).

Acceptance:
- Inventory of live-bundle-dependent tests (file:test_name list).
- Each classified per the above (B / S / C).
- Behavioural pins migrated to swap_bundle.
- Suite passes against an artificially mutated live bundle (e.g.
  swap in a 100-subject sample bundle, run the suite, verify only
  the live-bundle smoke tests fail).

Why: bundle re-emit is now a routine event (every mining session
adds 100s-1000s of subjects). Tests that implicitly depend on the
live bundle become a tax on every re-emit — fix once, save 30
minutes per future deploy.

title: Re-add Llanfairpwllgwyngyllgogerychwyrndrobwyllllantysiliogogogoch to welsh_place_names.json after wyrd-p8ve
Variant mining for non-OE/ON: ingest Wiktionary 'forms' arrays
description:
Per wyrd-f6v4 investigation 2026-05-08: etymon_text_match (variant source) is empty for Welsh / Irish / Breton / Old French / Middle English / Modern English. Reverse-search / fuzzy-search find canonical_form occurrences in scholarly etymology dictionaries' prose bodies — the OE/ON sources (Mawer, Skeat, Ekwall, Watson) have prose; the Welsh/Irish wiktextract corpora are headword-only with no prose to scan.

Implementation path: extend wiktextract_corpus_miner to also ingest each Wiktionary entry's 'forms' array (which carries declined / mutated / alternative spellings as structured data). Write each form as an etymon_text_match row with matched_form != canonical. Source attribution: 'wiktionary-forms' — distinct from existing 'wiktionary-empirical' tag.

Acceptance: post-mine, dashboard E-metric (variant coverage) reports >0 for at least Welsh / Irish / Breton. wyrd-f6v4 follow-up 3 of 4. Highest expected lift among the four follow-ups since Wiktionary's 'forms' field is well-populated for Celtic-family entries.

title: Goidelic inflection: investigate non-suffix-strip approach (séimhiú / urú)
description:
Per wyrd-f6v4 investigation 2026-05-08: Irish (33616 etymons) / Old Irish (8126) / Scottish Gaelic (17189) / Middle Irish carry 0 inflection metadata. Initial-mutation morphology (séimhiú = lenition, urú = eclipsis, h-prefix) is NOT suffix-strippable — the inflection lives at the START of the word, not the end. The current INFLECTION_RULES architecture (suffix-strip with 3-char minimum stem) cannot capture Goidelic inflection.

Investigate approaches:
1. Pre-strip initial mutation via a regex-based rule layer (mh- → m- delenited; bp- → p- de-eclipsed; etc.) before suffix matching.
2. Hand-curated lemma_id linkages for the most-cited Goidelic inflected forms.
3. Defer Goidelic inflection entirely until a richer linguistic engine is in place — accept that Irish/Scottish Gaelic stays at 0 inflection coverage.

Decide between (1) and (3) based on impact: how many Goidelic etymons would actually link if (1) were implemented? Spike a 50-row prototype before committing.

wyrd-f6v4 follow-up 2 of 4.

title: INFLECTION_RULES: add Old French / Middle English / Norman French rules
description:
Per wyrd-f6v4 investigation 2026-05-08: lexicon.py:INFLECTION_RULES registers suffix rules for OE+ON only. Old French (10820 etymons, 0 inflected) / Middle English (53024 etymons, 0 inflected) / Norman French (70 etymons, 0 inflected) are all suffix-strippable in the same shape OE/ON were. Add rules for:
- Old French: oblique case -s, plural -s, accusative
- Middle English: plural -es / -en, genitive -es, weak -e endings
- Norman French: same Old French shape (Anglo-Norman = ON's Romance neighbor)

Acceptance: post-fix, dashboard D-metric (inflection coverage) reports >0 for old-french and middle-english. wyrd-f6v4 follow-up 1 of 4.

title: INFLECTION_RULES: add Welsh suffix-strip rules (subset only — initial mutation deferred)
description:

Add rules for the SUFFIX-STRIPPABLE subset of Welsh inflection (plural -au / -ion / -i, comparative -ach, superlative -af). Acknowledge that initial mutation (lenition / nasal / aspirate) is NOT suffix-strippable and is deferred to a separate ticket / approach.

Acceptance: post-fix, link-lemmas --apply on the live DB writes >0 (etymon.lemma_id IS NOT NULL) rows for language='welsh'. Spot-check via dashboard's metric D for welsh.

Implementation: add 'welsh' entry to INFLECTION_RULES with ~5-8 rules covering plural / comparative / superlative. Test via fixture exercising each rule.

title: Refactor etymon_era_reflexes into per-tier helpers
description:
Surfaced by complexity review on PR #146 (wyrd-98cs). After adding Tier 4, etymon_era_reflexes is ~135 LOC of straight-line cluster→descent→period-form→phonology dispatch. Each tier reads as 'cur = db.execute(...); tier_source = "..."; results.extend(...)'. Extract to _tier1_cluster / _tier2_descent / _tier3_period_form / _tier4_phonology helpers each returning list[EraReflex]. The dispatcher then becomes 'try each tier in order; first non-empty wins'. Pre-existing complexity from before this PR; Tier 4 made it worse. Pure refactor — no behavior change; covered by existing tier-isolation tests.

Audit context: wyrd-eni4 epic, surfaced by complexity reviewer 2026-05-08.

title: Discover candidate tag groups beyond the current top-15 (semantic-class expansion)
description:
Forward-looking feature (NOT part of cleanup epic). Today's runtime tag classes are the top-15 from English place-name proportions: architecture, topography, social, descriptive, plant, agriculture, water, animal, measurement, geology, religious, tree, geography, direction, mammal. These cover ~95% of tag mass in real toponyms but leave room for semantic distinctions the generator can't currently express.

Two angles to investigate, both deferrable:

1. **Data-driven discovery**: cluster the corpus's etymon glosses + descriptions to find semantic groups that ISN'T currently a tag class. Candidates plausibly surfacing:
   - water subtypes (lake / river / stream / marsh / spring / ford)
   - settlement subtypes (city / town / village / hamlet / fort / market)
   - geological subtypes (cliff / cave / peak / valley / ridge / hollow)
   - period / culture markers (Roman / Saxon / Viking / Norman provenance)
   - body-part topographic metaphors (head / mouth / neck / shoulder of a hill)
   - color / material modifiers (stone / wood / iron / clay)
   - directional / size already exist but underused
   Approach: top-N glosses that DON'T hit any current tag, cluster via embedding similarity, propose candidate tag classes with examples.

2. **Domain-curated discovery**: pull from a published place-name semantic taxonomy (Smith EPNS index headers, Cameron's classification, Mills's per-element categories) and propose tags that align with how scholars actually classify toponyms.

Acceptance for a Phase 1: ship a 'lexicon discover-tag-candidates' CLI that emits 5-15 candidate tag classes with worked examples and per-language coverage projections, so the user can pick which to adopt before any bundle export change.

Implementation should NOT modify the existing tag classes — that would change runtime behavior. New tag classes get added alongside existing ones, with downstream features (--mood presets, --cohesion tag_cooccurrence) opt-in.

Source: wyrd-wzwa Phase 1 dashboard (2026-05-08) showed even old-english only tags 1.2% of its etymons across the existing 15 classes — semantic tagging is a near-empty axis at the corpus level. Expanding tag classes won't fix that density problem (filed as wyrd-i1s1 + sibling tickets); this ticket is about increasing the EXPRESSIVE RANGE of tags so the generator has more semantic axes to filter on.

title: Audit follow-up: inflection + spelling-variant coverage gap on Welsh/Irish/Celtic/French
description:
2026-05-08 audit (wyrd-wl35) found that --inflection-density and --spelling-variety knobs work end-to-end but data coverage is heavily skewed: ~407 inflected words and ~308 variant words in the bundle, ~86% Old English / Old Norse, near-zero on Welsh / Irish / Celtic / French. Knobs are essentially OE/ON-only.

Investigate:
1. Mining: do extractors actually capture inflected forms in Welsh / Irish / French? Sample 20 mining_run rows per language and check etymon column patterns.
2. link-lemmas: does the post-mining pass write etymon.lemma_id + etymon.inflection for non-Germanic languages? If not, what's the language-specific gap?
3. etymon_text_match: does reverse-search / fuzzy-search populate matched_form rows for Welsh / Irish / French source corpora? If yes, why don't they propagate to bundle _variants pools?

Acceptance: identify whether the gap is mining-side, post-processing-side, or export-side. File specific phase tickets per language family if needed.

Audit context (wyrd-wl35).
notes:
Investigation complete 2026-05-08. Filed 4 follow-up tickets (all P3, all linked to epic wyrd-eni4):
- wyrd-r6bk Welsh suffix-strip inflection rules (initial mutation deferred)
- wyrd-rc0b Old French / Middle English / Norman French inflection rules
- wyrd-jott Goidelic inflection investigation (séimhiú / urú; needs different architecture)
- wyrd-vx09 Variant mining for non-OE/ON via Wiktionary 'forms' field

Smoking gun on inflection: lexicon.py:1730 INFLECTION_RULES has only old-english + old-norse entries. derive_lemma_candidate returns None for any other language. So 0 inflection coverage on Welsh / Irish / Celtic / French is a CODE gap (no rules registered), not a data gap. Highest-impact follow-up is wyrd-vx09 (variant mining via Wiktionary forms) since that requires no per-language linguistic work — just structured data ingestion.

title: wyrd-08m Phase 4b: witness-weighted + rare-morpheme tiebreaker refinements
description:
Phase 4b refinement to wyrd-08m's rule (c) tiebreaker. Phase 4a (PR #142) shipped the Occam-first + lex-order tiebreaker, which handles most multi-zero ambiguities. Phase 4b adds the parent ticket's deferred sub-criteria for cases where the Occam-only resolution mis-picks:

1. WITNESS-WEIGHTED preference: among zero-unaccounted candidates with the same morpheme count, prefer the breakdown using lemmas with HIGHER witness counts (D4 consensus signal). The witness count for a slot's lemma is in etymon_consensus.witnesses; mapping a slot's modern_usage back to a specific etymon row requires walking the bundle's word_db -> meaning -> sources -> language form list, then querying lexicon for the matching etymon.

2. RARE-MORPHEME PENALTY: prefer breakdowns that AVOID very rare morphemes. A morpheme's rarity = inverse of its corpus reflex frequency (toponym_attestation count or rebuild-proportions usage count). High-frequency lemmas like 'tūn' / 'ford' / 'leah' get strong preference; one-off Tier-3 rarities get penalized.

Implementation:

- Add witness_count + rarity_score columns OR a per-slot lookup helper in decomposition.py.
- Extend _try_rule_tiebreaker to a multi-pass sort: morpheme_count ASC, sum(witness_count) DESC, sum(rarity_score) ASC, morpheme_ids ASC.
- A new canonical_source string is NOT needed — Phase 4b refinements stay under 'tiebreaker' source so consumers don't need to differentiate.
- Tests: synthesize toponyms where the Occam check ties but witness counts diverge (and similarly for rarity).

Acceptance: re-running 'lexicon decompose --apply' against the production lexicon shifts at most 5-10% of 'tiebreaker'-tagged canonical picks. Phase 4b is ONLY worth shipping if mining surfaces evidence that Occam-only mis-picks are common; otherwise this stays deferred indefinitely.

Lower priority. Self-contained but requires careful etymon-mapping work.

title: wyrd-70s0 follow-up: refactor rebuild-proportions/unaccounted with shared decompose-corpus helper
description:
Complexity reviewer flagged the rebuild-proportions and unaccounted CLI commands as one-screen-rule violators after the wyrd-70s0 (PR #136) --db wiring landed:

- unaccounted is now ~117 lines spanning DB context manager + decompose loop + fragment aggregation + source-evidence annotation + dual JSON/text output.
- rebuild-proportions is ~64 lines (closer to the line but still over).
- Both manually invoke db_cm.__enter__() / __exit__() in a try/finally — re-implements 'with' semantics by hand. The standard pattern is contextlib.nullcontext.

Refactor:
1. Extract a module-level _decompose_corpus(names, word_db, db) -> tuple[list[Name], Counter] helper that handles the canonical-or-heuristic decompose loop and returns (resolved_names, canonical_hits_counter). Both consumers call it.
2. Replace the manual __enter__/__exit__ with: with (LexiconDB(db_path) if db_path else nullcontext()) as db: ... — collapses 4 lines per call site, propagates exception info correctly.
3. For unaccounted: extract _format_unaccounted_text(...) for the print block.
4. Both CLI commands shrink to thin orchestrators (~30 lines each).

Tests: existing CLI smoke tests should pass unchanged (refactor preserves behaviour).

This is pure refactor — no behaviour change. Defer if/when the next feature touches these commands.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #137 (d3dc195) — _decompose_corpus + _aggregate_unaccounted_fragments helpers extracted from rebuild-proportions/unaccounted with nullcontext. Pure refactor, no behaviour change.

title: wyrd-70s0 follow-up: plumb region through CLI consumers
description:
Phase 3a (PR #136) added 'region' as an optional parameter to lookup_canonical_signature and decompose_with_canonical, but neither rebuild-proportions nor the unaccounted miner CLI passes it. Both flatten the place_names JSON's {country: {region: [name, ...]}} shape via load_names() before the per-name loop, so region context is dropped before reaching the canonical lookup.

This is fine when toponym modern_name values are unique across regions. When they collide (e.g. multiple 'Stratford' rows in the lexicon, one per region), the current consumer code uses the lowest-id canonical for ALL same-name corpus entries — which violates the wyrd-08m 'stable counts via canonical attribution' acceptance criterion in those edge cases.

Implementation:
1. Update load_names() (or add a parallel helper) to preserve (country, region, name) triples instead of flattening to a name list.
2. Pass region into decompose_with_canonical from both rebuild-proportions and unaccounted miner.
3. Tests: corpus with two toponyms sharing modern_name but distinct regions, each with its own canonical → consumer counts reflect the region-tightened canonical pick instead of leaking across regions.

Likely small (~50 lines + tests). Lower priority — collisions are rare in the British Isles toponymy corpus, but the determinism crack is real.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #139. Region context plumbed through CLI consumers; lookup falls back to NULL-region rows only (cross-region returns None to prevent misattribution).

title: Scholar-name FP refinement in toponym_attestation regex
description:
Deferred from PR #108 (wyrd-skm Phase 3.0a) Claude review. The toponym_attestation extractor's blacklist filters known scholar surnames + connectives (kemble/skeat/ekwall/the/from/etc.), but new scholar names slip through. Specifically:

extract('Author, 1086 (p. 59) cited; ...') → ('Author', 1086) was a confirmed FP class
extract('Source, 1234 mentions ...') → ('Source', 1234) similar shape

The (p. 59) lookahead added in PR #108's round-2 closes the dominant case (where the FP is in academic-citation parens). The remaining FP class is 'ScholarName, YEAR' followed by source-attribution parens like '(F.A.)' or '(D.B.)' rather than '(p. ...'.

Scope:
1. Empirical: scan production toponym_attestation rows where source_doc points at a scholar-author abbreviation (F.A., D.B., R.B., etc.) AND form looks like a scholar surname (capitalized non-place-name token).
2. If FP rate is meaningfully high (>1% of rows), add a structural look-ahead: when the year is followed by ' (' + 2-4 letter abbreviation + '.)', and the form's first letter doesn't match any known toponym in the parent etymology row's toponym, suppress.
3. Add tests pinning the FP class is suppressed.

Parent epic: wyrd-lm5m

Defer condition: if production data shows <0.5% of toponym_attestation rows are FP from this class, close as wontfix — the noise floor is acceptable.

title: Add _resolve_stratum_param validator + SPA culture gating for --stratum
description:
Phase 3 follow-up from PR #109 Claude review (medium-priority deferred items).

## Context

PR #109 wired the --stratum filter end-to-end but left two surface gaps:

1. No input validation. A typo (--stratum native-welch) silently no-ops because every Meaning has empty stratum data → keep_keys collapses to None → bit-stable with no-flag run. This is the failure mode 'user thinks the filter applied but it didn't', easy to miss in smoke runs.

2. No x-options-by-culture in the input_schema. The SPA renders --stratum as a free-form string today; a user picking 'native-welsh' against an English culture gets a silent no-op. The era pattern (wyrd-awo) handles this with x-options-by-culture metadata that filters the dropdown to applicable labels per culture.

## Plan

Mirror the era pattern:

1. wyrd/generators/kenning/strata.py exposes a per-culture allowed-strata map. Welsh culture → WELSH_STRATA tuple; English / Scottish / Irish / Breton → empty (no Phase 1 classifier yet, will populate as Phase 4 lands).

2. _resolve_stratum_param(stratum: str | None, culture: str) -> str | None:
   - empty/None → None (no filter)
   - stratum not in the culture's allowed-set → ValueError with a friendly 'unknown stratum X for culture Y; valid: [...]' message
   - cli.py catches ValueError and exits non-zero (already-existing pattern from _resolve_era_param)

3. input_schema 'stratum' entry gains 'x-options-by-culture' computed from the per-culture allowed-strata map (mirrors _era_options_by_culture). SPA shows a culture-filtered dropdown.

## Why deferred

Phase 4 lands the French / OE / ON classifiers and adds those families' allowed strata. Validating against WELSH_STRATA only would block users from passing Phase 4 strata until both PRs land in the same release. Easier to bundle validation with Phase 4 so the per-culture allowed-set is complete on first ship.

## Test plan

- _resolve_stratum_param: None / empty / valid / typo'd / valid-tag-wrong-culture
- input_schema: x-options-by-culture has expected shape, contains WELSH_STRATA for Welsh culture, empty for cultures without classifiers
- cli.py: --stratum native-welch on welsh culture → friendly ValueError + non-zero exit
- generate(): bit-stability with no-validation path preserved when stratum is None or empty

## References

- _resolve_era_param at wyrd/generators/kenning/__init__.py:316 (template)
- _era_options_by_culture at wyrd/generators/kenning/__init__.py (template)
- WELSH_STRATA at wyrd/generators/kenning/strata.py:55
- Phase 3 stratum coercion at wyrd/generators/kenning/__init__.py:582 (where the TODO comment links here)
notes:
2026-05-07: Phase 4 (4a-4d) all shipped. Per-family STRATA tuples + ALL_STRATA frozenset registry now live in strata.py. Phase 4d (PR #115) deferred 'family-aware stratum validation on set-stratum' to this ticket — bundling with the runtime --stratum filter validation it already scopes.

Concrete addition to the Plan above:

5. ``set-stratum`` (Phase 4d's hand-correction CLI) currently uses ALL_STRATA for value-only typo protection. Once this ticket lands the LANGUAGE_TO_FAMILY map, set-stratum should also reject family-disjoint values — e.g. '--language welsh --stratum east-norse' should fail loudly because east-norse is in OLD_NORSE_STRATA, not WELSH_STRATA. Cross-family overlap (latin-loan / english-loan) stays accepted since those are valid in multiple families.

This makes set-stratum's validation match the runtime --stratum filter's validation — same per-language allowed-strata table sourced from the same map.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #120. _resolve_stratum_param validator (mirrors _resolve_era_param), _stratum_options_by_culture for SPA dependent-select, and family-aware set-stratum (reverses Phase 4d's cross-family tolerance). LANGUAGE_TO_FAMILY now built programmatically from per-classifier _SELF_LANGUAGE_TO_STRATUM maps — drift-proof by construction. _CULTURE_TO_VALID_STRATA registry with INVARIANT comment naming the rule. 209 strata+proportions tests cover the surface; 1714 total kenning tests pass. CLI smoke confirms welsh+east-norse rejection and english+native-welsh acceptance. Closes the wyrd-lr4 follow-on chain.

title: Extend _seed_subject to spread members across multi-substrata languages
description:
Test helper followup from PR #107 (Claude review nice-to-have).

The wyrd-lr4 Phase 2 export tests for multi-substrata families (welsh + middle-welsh + old-welsh sharing a celtic_mix bucket) bypass _seed_subject and use raw INSERT INTO etymon to spread members across substrata languages, because the helper takes (canonical_form, language_field) pairs through seed_from_meanings which routes celtic_mix → 'celtic' uniformly.

Future absorb-helper tests for stratum, era ranges, etc. will keep needing this multi-substrata shape (welsh + old-welsh, French + Old French, OE West Saxon vs Mercian, ON East vs West). A small extension to _seed_subject — e.g. an optional 'language_overrides' dict mapping canonical_form to lexicon language code — would remove the raw-SQL noise from each new test and concentrate the 'how do we spread family members' logic in one place.

Low priority: only matters when Phase 4 classifiers (French/OE/ON) start landing. Phase 2's three raw-SQL UPDATE tests are clear enough as-is.

Out of scope for the wyrd-lr4 phases; this is test ergonomics.
close_reason: Phase 3 + helper extension shipped via PR #109. CLI --stratum flag wired through Kenning.generate, MeaningGenerator.keep_keys_for_stratum + _intersect_keep_keys compose with era. 21 new tests cover all branches (filter primitives, cache, era∩stratum intersection, empty keep-set, positive-tag path, schema round-trip). _seed_subject gained language_overrides kwarg with (form, language)-scoped UPDATE; refactored 4 Phase 2 tests. Bit-stable until bundle re-emit lands. wyrd-j3gy filed for the deferred validation + SPA culture-gating.

title: kenning: refactor classify_welsh / lexicon_classify_stratum + batch the UPDATE loop
description:
Deferred from PR #105 (wyrd-lr4 Phase 1) per AGENT-REVIEWERS.md complexity-reviewer rubric.

Two functions exceed the one-screen rule:

- `classify_welsh` (wyrd/generators/kenning/strata.py, ~65 body lines) — three distinct phases (self-language pass / chunked parent fetch / priority-order ancestor assignment). Suggested extractions: `_classify_by_self_language`, `_fetch_welsh_parent_languages`, `_assign_stratum_by_ancestors`.

- `lexicon_classify_stratum` (wyrd/generators/kenning/cli.py, ~75 body lines) — does classifier dispatch + summary print + write loop. Suggested extractions: `_summarize_stratum_proposals`, `_write_stratum_proposals`.

Forward-looking concern flagged in PR #105 review: the per-row UPDATE loop is fine at 31k Welsh rows but will need batching when French / Old English / Old Norse classifiers land at 100k+ rows. Approach: `UPDATE etymon SET stratum = CASE id WHEN ? THEN ? ... END WHERE id IN (...)` chunked at SQLite's 999-var limit, similar to the chunked SELECT in classify_welsh.

Should also add a periodic '[N/total]' progress line per CLAUDE.md's mining-progress convention — not strictly mining but the same operator-debuggability concern applies once row counts grow.

Acceptance: each function ≤ ~50 body lines; UPDATE path uses CASE-batched UPDATE chunks; behavior unchanged (existing test suite passes).
close_reason: Shipped via PR #121. lexicon_classify_stratum refactored: 75-line body → 17-line parent + 4 single-purpose helpers (_resolve_stratum_classifier, _summarize_stratum_proposals, _write_stratum_proposals, _build_case_update). Per-row UPDATE loop replaced with chunked CASE-batched UPDATE at _STRATUM_WRITE_BATCH_SIZE = 300 (SQLite 999-var ceiling / 3 placeholders per row). Periodic [N/total] progress line emits per batch per CLAUDE.md mining-progress convention. Load-bearing AND stratum IS NULL clause (Phase 4d idempotency contract) preserved on the batch path with rationale comment migrated to _build_case_update. 100 strata tests cover every branch including 350-row batched-write happy path, --force overwrite, progress per batch, empty proposals short-circuit, idempotent re-run, single-row chunk SQL well-formed. 1719 total kenning tests pass.

title: kenning: refactor agentic disambiguator orchestrator and CLI driver to one-screen helpers
description:
Round-1 + round-2 complexity reviews on PR #103 (wyrd-uct) flagged two functions over the one-screen rule:

- `disambiguate_one_agentic` (wyrd/generators/kenning/disambiguator.py, ~110 body lines) — fails the and/or test (per-round LLM dispatch / expansion-request validation / snippet widening + short-circuits all in one body). Reviewer-suggested extractions: module-level `_parse_expansion_request` and `_widen_snippet` helpers.

- `lexicon_disambiguate_fuzzy` (wyrd/generators/kenning/cli.py, ~95 body lines) — mixes invariant-checking, setup, agentic/non-agentic dispatch, dry-run row-action classification (which duplicates `apply_disambiguator_result`), and reporting. Reviewer-suggested extractions: `_classify_dry_run` and `_process_one_case` helpers.

Both are correct and well-commented. The refactor is reviewability-driven, not bug-driven, so deferred from PR #103 per AGENT-REVIEWERS.md complexity-reviewer rubric ("acceptable to acknowledge complexity and defer refactoring by creating a beads ticket").

Acceptance: each function ≤ ~50 body lines (excluding internal function definitions) without losing the existing test coverage or changing behavior.

title: kenning: Scottish anglicization sidecar — Loch, Inver, Auch, Strath, Ben, Tigh
description:
Parallel to wyrd-1cjg (Irish anglicization sidecar). The Scottish corpus uses anglicized Gaelic prefixes — most landed via the Irish sidecar (Glen-, Kil-, Knock-, Bally-, Tully- all share Goidelic roots), but Scottish-specific forms aren't covered:

- Loch- (34 names) → loch "lake"
- Inver- (26) → inbhir "river mouth"
- Auch- (24) / Ach- (14) → achadh "field" (Scottish-Gaelic form)
- Strath- (18) → srath "river valley"
- Ben- (4) → beinn "mountain"
- Tigh- (2) → tigh "house"

Total: ~98 Scottish corpus names that the bundle currently can't recognize. Plus the prefix slot is then attributed for downstream cohesion / proportions consumers.

Sidecar approach (new data/scottish_anglicizations.json) parallel to wyrd-1cjg's irish_anglicizations.json. _load_meanings already extends with sidecars; just add the new file to the union.

Acceptance:
- New scottish_anglicizations.json with 6-8 high-impact prefix entries
- _load_meanings extended
- 5+ tests parallel to wyrd-1cjg's structure
- COVERAGE.md snapshot showing Scottish lift
notes: Investigated 2026-05-07 — not actionable. Most Scottish anglicized prefixes (Loch-, Inver-, Auch-, Ach-, Strath-, Ben-, Ty-) are ALREADY in the bundle from prior Wiktionary mining; only Tigh- would be new and that's ~2 corpus names. The 25.29% Scottish perfect rate is already what the mining achieves. A sidecar would be redundant. Future Scottish coverage gains need either deeper morpheme mining or a different angle (e.g. compound-component analysis for names like 'Benbecula' where the suffix is unaccounted).

title: wyrd-ami Phase 2 follow-up: extend etymon canonical-rollup views to include Phase 2a new columns
description:
Follow-up flagged by Claude review of PR #99. The etymon table grew 5 new columns in Phase 2a (pronunciation_ipa, pronunciation_dialect, original_script, transliteration, english_shaped) but the canonical-rollup views (etymon_canonical, etymon_consensus, the wyrd-7lo per-child rollups) weren't extended to surface them.

Practical consequence: when cluster_ocr_variants merges a richer row into a canonical that lacks the new columns, the canonical view shows NULL for those columns even though the loser had values. Town-name generation that reads from the canonical view (Phase 2c) would miss the loser's pronunciation/script data.

Fix:
1. Audit which views select from etymon — etymon_canonical, etymon_consensus, etymon_gloss_canonical, etymon_tag_canonical, etymon_text_match_canonical.
2. For each view that should propagate the new columns, add them with a COALESCE(canonical.X, loser.X) rollup pattern.
3. Migration: drop and recreate the views (SQLite has no CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW).

Not urgent — only matters once cluster_ocr_variants is re-run on rows that have the new columns populated, which won't happen until Phase 2c. File now so it's tracked.
notes:
Closed wontfix 2026-05-07: investigated during PR #99 review-loop closing. The premise (cluster_ocr_variants merging a row with pronunciation_ipa into a canonical that lacks it) doesn't apply to wave-2 non-Latin rows.

Reason: cluster_ocr_variants targets OCR-noisy etymons from scholarly toponym dictionaries (mostly old-english / old-norse / celtic forms transcribed from Joyce / Mawer / Ekwall books). It does NOT run against wiktextract-sourced wave-2 rows (he/ar/fa/sa/akk/egy/arc/pal) — those are clean structured-data ingests, not OCR. Live DB confirmed: 0 cluster merges affecting any of the 5 Phase 2a columns.

The 'fix' would rewrite etymon_canonical from 'SELECT *' to an explicit column list with COALESCE-from-merged-losers logic, ~60-90 min of work for a hazard that doesn't exist on real data. If cluster_ocr_variants is ever pointed at wave-2 rows in the future, file a fresh ticket then.

title: wyrd-ami Phase 2 follow-up: LLM-backfill english_shaped for the ~85k rows with no transliteration / IPA
description:
Follow-up from PR #99 (wyrd-ha9q Phase 2b). The rule-based derive_english_shaped only populates rows that have transliteration or pronunciation_ipa data from wiktextract. ~85k of the 133k wave-2 non-Latin rows have neither — derive returns None for them and the column stays NULL.

For rows with a non-Latin canonical_form (Hebrew niqqud, Arabic harakat, Sanskrit Devanagari, Egyptian hieroglyphs) but no transliteration / IPA, the only path to an english_shaped is an LLM. Each row is a small Gemini Flash call: 'Given the canonical form X in language Y, what's the conventional English-shaped rendering?'

Cost estimate: 85k Gemini Flash calls × ~$0.0001/call = ~$8.50. Plausibly cheap enough.

Implementation:
- Add a CLI flag --llm-fill that processes only rows where derive returned None (transliteration + ipa both NULL).
- The LLM prompt cites well-known forms (rakshasa, jinn, golem) for calibration.
- Confidence-low responses get a separate stamp (low_confidence_english_shaped column?) so the SPA can flag them.

Defer until Phase 2c+2d ship and we see how often town-name generation hits an english_shaped=NULL row in practice. May not be worth the cost if the rule-coverage is sufficient.
notes:
Closed wontfix 2026-05-07: PR #99's empirical pass populated 48k of 133k rows via rule-based derivation. The 85k skipped rows have NULL transliteration AND NULL IPA in wiktextract — they're not data the corpus actually carries.

Reason for closing rather than keeping queued: the LLM backfill is speculative (~$8.50 in API spend, ~85k Gemini Flash calls) AND it's unclear whether town-name generation would actually hit a NULL english_shaped row in practice. Phase 2c (wyrd-vsrn) will tell us empirically: if the generator never picks rows with NULL english_shaped, this work is unnecessary; if it does and the canonical_form fallback is ugly, file a fresh ticket then with concrete usage data.

The design consideration (LLM-fill via canonical_form prompt) is captured in PR #99's body for future reference. No code change needed today.

title: kenning: _load_culture lru_cache not cleared in tests that mutate _load_meanings
description:
Surfaced by test-coverage agent on PR #100 (wyrd-8s71).

_load_meanings and _load_culture in wyrd/generators/kenning/__init__.py are independently @lru_cache'd. Tests that need a fresh meaning_db call _load_meanings.cache_clear() — but _load_culture caches a MeaningGenerator built over the prior meaning_db, so subsequent generate-using tests can read a stale view through _load_culture even after _load_meanings is cleared.

In practice this PR's tests are read-only on _load_meanings so no observable bug — but it's a latent footgun for any future test that mutates the bundle and then exercises the generator via culture-loaded generators.

Fix options:
1. Always clear _load_culture alongside _load_meanings in any test that touches the meaning_db.
2. Wire a pytest fixture (_clear_kenning_caches) that clears both as a single autouse hook.
3. Have _load_culture re-derive the meaning_db on each access (drop the cache).

Option 2 is probably cleanest. The cache primarily helps repeated runs in long-lived processes (the API server) and the test-suite hit isn't the steady state.

Code pointers:
- wyrd/generators/kenning/__init__.py:_load_meanings (line ~149)
- wyrd/generators/kenning/__init__.py:_load_culture (line ~196)

title: kenning: KenningExplain doesn't recognize manorial-affix names on round-trip
description:
Surfaced by Claude review on PR #98 (wyrd-obu).

Kenning.generate with manorial_affix>0 produces names like 'Stoke Mandeville'. KenningExplain (the decompose-an-input-name pipeline) calls Name.find_meaning on the input string against the meaning_db, which doesn't contain Norman-family-surname entries. So 'Stoke Mandeville' decomposes as 'Stoke' (with morphemes) + 'Mandeville' (entirely unaccounted).

The user-visible asymmetry: a name the SPA just generated (with explanation citing "Mandeville (Norman family)") becomes only-partially-decomposable when copy-pasted into the explainer.

Fix options:

1. Sidecar approach (parallel to wyrd-1cjg's Irish anglicizations): inject the Norman families into meaning_db at runtime as Meaning entries with usage='Mandeville' / 'Lacy' / etc., language='old_french', tag=['manorial', 'norman']. The explainer would then decompose 'Stoke Mandeville' correctly.

2. Special-case in KenningExplain: load the manorial-families list and post-process the explainer's output, recognizing the trailing space-separated word as a possible manorial affix and emitting a synthetic component for it.

3. Document the asymmetry as out-of-scope (KenningExplain is for morpheme-decomposition, not the manorial pattern).

Option 1 is consistent with wyrd-1cjg's pattern and gives explainer parity with generation. Option 2 is special-case logic. Option 3 punts.

Code pointers:
- wyrd/generators/kenning/__init__.py:KenningExplain.generate_all
- wyrd/generators/kenning/__init__.py:_load_norman_manorial_families
- wyrd/generators/kenning/data/norman_manorial_families.json

title: wyrd-ami: dedicated dictionary parsers for Klein's Hebrew, Lane's Arabic, Faulkner's Egyptian
description:
Part of EPIC wyrd-ialp (wave-2 language etymon corpus expansion). SECOND to implement per user 2026-05-06 — after wyrd-3wt's wiktextract re-ingest establishes the baseline.

Most authoritative etymological dictionaries for the wave-2 languages aren't well-indexed in Wiktionary. Specialist references:

- **Klein's Hebrew Etymological Dictionary** (Ernest Klein, 'A Comprehensive Etymological Dictionary of the Hebrew Language for Readers of English', 1987) — the standard for Hebrew etymology including loanwords from Aramaic/Akkadian.
- **Lane's Arabic-English Lexicon** (Edward William Lane, 1863-93) — definitive classical Arabic dictionary, far deeper than Wiktionary's Arabic coverage. The LLM keeps citing Lane's so we should ingest it.
- **Faulkner's Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian** (Raymond Faulkner, 1962) — standard Middle Egyptian. The LLM cited Faulkner's for Rekhep / Anpw etc. during the 2026-05-06 mine.
- **Hans Wehr Dictionary of Modern Written Arabic** — for modern Arabic register if we need it.
- **Monier-Williams Sanskrit-English Dictionary** — already cited frequently by the LLM for Sanskrit. Might be worth ingesting even though our 'sa' coverage is OK (12k entries) — would catch the gaps.
- **Tropper's Akkadian Handwörterbuch** or **CAD (Chicago Assyrian Dictionary)** — Akkadian.
- **MacKenzie's Concise Pahlavi Dictionary** — Middle Persian.

What to do:

1. Pick a dictionary, find a digitized or scrapable form (PDF OCR, public-domain scans, structured online versions like Sefaria for Klein's, perseus.tufts.edu for some).
2. Build a parser per dictionary (similar shape to skeat_parser.py and the etymonline ingester from PR #80). Each yields ParsedEntry-style rows.
3. Wire to a 'lexicon ingest-<dictname>' subcommand that walks parsed entries and upserts into etymon + citation tables.
4. Tag each etymon with source='<dictionary-name>' so realistic-mode generation can filter by trust level.

Per-dictionary effort: probably ~1 PR each, 1-3 days of work. Klein's (well-structured, modern, English) is probably easiest; Faulkner's (transliteration conventions, hieroglyphic alongside Latin script) probably hardest.

Trust level: HIGHEST — these are the authoritative dictionaries the LLM cites when it knows the answer.

Dependencies: should be done after wyrd-3wt to avoid duplicate work for entries Wiktionary already covers.

title: kenning: extract _create_canonical_rollup_view helper to shrink _rebuild_etymon_views
description:
After PR #88 added three new CREATE VIEW statements (etymon_gloss_canonical, etymon_tag_canonical, etymon_text_match_canonical), _rebuild_etymon_views in lexicon.py grew past the one-screen rule (~95 lines).

The new view DDLs share a uniform DROP/CREATE/applied[...] = True boilerplate. Extract a small helper:

    def _create_canonical_rollup_view(db, applied, name, sql):
        db.conn.execute(f"DROP VIEW IF EXISTS {name}")
        db.conn.execute(sql)
        applied[f"{name}_view"] = True

This collapses the three new view-creation blocks to single helper calls, brings the function back under one screen, and centralises the recreate-on-migration pattern.

Surfaced by complexity-reviewer agent on PR #88; deferred since the view bodies themselves are the substance and they remain readable in linear form. Worth doing as a small standalone refactor.

Code pointer: wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon.py _rebuild_etymon_views

title: wyrd-7tz Phase 2: LLM-classify production etymons into meaning_synsets
description:
wyrd-7tz Phase 1 (PR #61) shipped the meaning_synset schema + 53 seed synsets. Phase 2 runs an LLM-assisted classification pass over the production lexicon's etymons, populating etymon_meaning_synset rows.

**Provider: Gemini 2.5 Flash** (consistent with D25 — the existing `disambiguate-fuzzy` LLM step, which is the closest task analog to synset classification: take a small structured input, produce a categorical verdict against a fixed candidate set). Per D19 Sonnet doesn't lift over Flash for this task class; per D2 Anthropic budget is reserved for runtime user features. Override via `WYRD_GEMINI_MODEL`.

Input per call: etymon's canonical_form + language + glosses + tags. Output: synset id(s) the etymon belongs to, with a confidence label and one-sentence reason (mirrors the disambiguator's verdict shape so the audit trail is consistent across LLM-decision tables).

Cost gate: classify only etymons that (a) are bundle-eligible (passed export_meanings promotion) and (b) don't already have an etymon_meaning_synset row. Idempotent on (etymon_id, meaning_synset_id) UNIQUE.

Estimate: ~few-thousand classifications at ~$0.0001 each — order of $1-5 total for the full bundle. Defer until Phase 3 transforms (wyrd-llq0) are queued — the data is wasted without the consumers.

title: kenning: skeat_1904_huntingdonshire source file is wrong (Cambridge Antiquarian Soc Proceedings index, not Skeat dict)
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-05 during a low-yield audit. The source file at sources/skeat_1904_huntingdonshire.txt is a Google-Books OCR of:

  PROCEEDINGS OF THE Cambridge Antiquarian Society
  14 October 1902 to 18 May 1903
  Volume X, No. 44

The actual content the parser consumed is INDEX BACK-MATTER (list of place-names with page references like 'Shelford (Notts). 326 Sheppey 366 Sherborne 79...'). The alphabetical parser yielded 108 'entries' that are all index-list shape; LLM accepted 0 of them because the bodies are page-number lists, not etymology prose.

Skeat 1904 Huntingdonshire (his actual paper 'The Place-Names of Huntingdonshire') is presumably PUBLISHED IN that proceedings volume, but the OCR file as currently shipped is the proceedings INDEX section, not the paper body. Fix options:

1. Find a clean OCR of Skeat's Huntingdonshire paper specifically (archive.org has the Cambridge proceedings vol X — needs to be sliced to just Skeat's contribution).
2. Mine the proceedings vol X as a whole, accepting that other Cambridge papers will get extracted alongside Skeat's.
3. Skip Skeat 1904 Huntingdonshire entirely and rely on the Mawer-Stenton Huntingdonshire EPNS volume if/when one is available pre-1929 (probably not).

The 108-parsed/0-accepted mining_run row in the DB is misleading — should be tagged or discarded. wyrd-bgr's 'Tier-2 never sees Tier-1 declines' is unrelated; this is a content-mismatch issue at the source-file layer.

title: kenning: --include-sonnet flag for lexicon review (or generalize to --include-anthropic)

title: Add COVERAGE.md tracking place-name decomposition rate over time
description: Record initial-commit (2026-04-29 ceadce6) baseline and current (2026-05-05 9cfa477) decomposition coverage as a rolling log. Initial: english 28.3%, scottish 18.3%, welsh 15.1%, irish 10.0%. Current: english 32.6%, scottish 21.4%, welsh 19.0%, irish 12.4%, breton 1.6%.
