title: kenning: tighten or warn on high --concurrency for paid providers
description:
Per Claude review on PR #62 (Medium #2): the --concurrency IntRange of 1-64 is permissive enough that a user copying examples could hit `--concurrency 64` against Anthropic, blow past their org-wide RPM cap, and watch ~64 entries fail simultaneously with transport_error_result (since wyrd-cfa retry/backoff is also deferred). The parallel path doesn't propagate transport errors as exceptions — they become rejections — so the user gets a corrupt-looking mining run rather than a loud failure.

Two reasonable options:
1. Tighten the IntRange to 1-16 (covers the paid-provider sweet spot).
2. Leave 1-64 but emit a warning when concurrency > 16 and provider in {anthropic, gemini}.

Either also pairs naturally with wyrd-cfa (429 retry/backoff): once retry exists, high concurrency can be self-rate-limiting via the backoff feedback, and the ceiling can be widened back out.

title: kenning: 429 retry-with-backoff for paid-provider mining (Anthropic, Gemini)
description:
wyrd-l0r shipped the parallelized mining loop with bounded ThreadPoolExecutor concurrency. The original ticket called out a separate concern that wasn't bundled in: paid providers (Anthropic, Gemini) have requests-per-minute caps, and a high --concurrency value can blow past them, returning 429 errors that currently propagate as transport failures.

Scope:
- Add a retry-with-backoff layer to anthropic_extractor.extract_one and gemini_extractor.extract_one (NOT llm_extractor / Ollama — local Ollama doesn't rate-limit).
- Exponential backoff with jitter on 429 / quota-exceeded responses.
- Cap retries at ~3 attempts with a max total wait of ~60s; after that, surface as transport_error_result so the existing failure-handling path captures the count.
- Optionally: a token-bucket semaphore at the mining loop level so the user can specify --rpm 50 alongside --concurrency 8 to enforce a global rate cap.

Out of scope for wyrd-l0r itself; deferred so the parallelization landed without scope creep.

title: kenning: D17 third term — tag-class-prior in Generator.select
description:
Wyrd-gfa shipped the empirical + uniform-marginal blend (the basic --novelty knob). The full D17 design specifies a three-term mixture: alpha*empirical + beta*tag-class-prior + gamma*marginal. The middle term — biasing each pick by the tag-co-occurrence prior given the neighbor morpheme's tags — was deferred because it requires threading neighbor-context through the structure walk in NameGenerator.

Documented in proportions.py:Generator.select docstring: 'The full D17 design layers a third tag-class-prior term, deferred to a follow-up since it requires threading neighbor-context through the structure walk.'

Data is already in the bundle (tag_cooccurrence + tag_marginal Counters per culture proportions, populated by cli.py:_proportions_from). Just needs the runtime side: surface them via load_proportions, thread the previously-picked morpheme's tags down to subsequent picks, and blend tag-class-prior into the mixture via a new beta knob.

DECISIONS.md D16 / D17 are the design references.

title: kenning: structured SPA control for --era field (enum or culture-keyed select)

The --era input is a free-form string accepting three shapes (year '1086', cell label 'oe-late', or 'family/label'). The SPA renders this as a plain text input today (the manifest has no enum). For better UX, render a structured control — either a flat enum of all defined era cells (era_cells_for_family across all 6 families) or a dependent select that filters to the chosen culture's family.

title: Bridge expansion: Welsh/Breton stub-rerouting + ON/OE long-tail forms
description:
Follow-up to wyrd-9ig (OE), wyrd-fkg (ON), wyrd-7k4 (celtic). The bridge-grinding session of 2026-05-03 closed the major buckets (37.65% rollup coverage from a 31.4% start) but a stub-rerouting and long-tail residue remains.

Diagnostic snapshot post-2026-05-03 bridge work:

- celtic: 1879 etymons, 37.1% clustered. wyrd-7k4 closed 66 forms (mostly Goidelic). The remaining ~1180 unbridged celtic etymons are dominated by:
  - Welsh forms (cyfeiliog, cynfarch, blaen, ddewi, etc.) — wyrd-7k4's table is Goidelic-focused
  - Breton forms (kerque-prefixes, plou-/lan- compounds, less-common -et/-ic suffixes)
  - 1-source long-tail (~600 forms, 1 source each) — high curation cost
  - The 245 wyrd-083 stub-bridges that wyrd-7k4 didn't catch (Welsh/Breton lemmas with no clustered alt anywhere)

- old-english: 2452 etymons, 38.5% clustered. wyrd-9ig closed 20 forms. The remaining ~1500 unbridged include:
  - ~50 high-witness 2-source forms (most are Anglo-Saxon personal names — leofhere, baldhere, brihthelm — not in Wiktionary)
  - Many 2-source common nouns NOT in the wyrd-9ig table (cylla, holegn, hang, wlc, kers, hēg, draeg, ticce variants, hala variants)
  - Long tail of 1-source forms

- old-norse: 708 etymons, 35.9% clustered. wyrd-fkg closed 36 forms. The remaining ~450 unbridged include:
  - ~30 2-source forms not in wyrd-fkg's _ON_PHONOLOGICAL_BRIDGES table
  - Frankish/personal names overlap with Norse names

Scope:
1. Welsh/Breton inflection/lenition table extension to wyrd-7k4 (~30-50 entries) — biggest remaining single-bucket gain
2. OE 2-source common-noun additions to wyrd-9ig (~20-30 entries)
3. ON 2-source additions to wyrd-fkg (~15-25 entries)
4. Decision: whether to attempt the personal-name layer (separate ticket scope — Wiktionary doesn't catalog OE/ON personal names as common-noun entries)

Estimated yield: +1-2 pts global coverage (bringing total to ~39-40%). Diminishing returns past this point — long-tail 1-source forms have curation/yield ratio that doesn't justify investment.

Acceptance: ≥30 new bridge entries across the three tables, all verified against live DB state via the audit pattern from wyrd-9ig/fkg/7k4. Apply against ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db + re-run cluster-cognates. Coverage measurement before/after.

title: kenning: bundle per_lang_* accumulators in export_meanings into a dataclass
description:
Surfaced by complexity-reviewer on PR #56. _emit_word_languages now takes 6 positional args; both callers (_word_for_reflex + _synthesize_word_for_family) declare/absorb/pass an identical 4-variable group:

  per_lang: dict[str, list[str]]
  per_lang_variants: dict[str, dict[str, int]]
  per_lang_inflections: dict[str, dict[str, str]]
  per_lang_citations: dict[str, set[str]]
  per_lang_attested_years: dict[str, dict[str, int]]

These four dicts always travel together. Suggested refactor: a small _PerLangAccumulators dataclass that bundles them. Callers create one instance, the absorb_member_X functions take it, and _emit_word_languages takes one ParameterObject argument plus the word dict. Signature drops from 6 args → 3, future per-language fields add one attribute and one absorb call instead of threading through every signature.

Acceptance:
- New _PerLangAccumulators dataclass with the 5 fields above.
- _absorb_member_* helpers updated to accept the dataclass and mutate one field on it.
- _emit_word_languages takes (word, accumulators) instead of 6 separate dicts.
- Both callers updated.
- All existing tests still pass; no behaviour change.
- Bonus: easier to add new per-language metadata in PR-3 (--era resolution metadata, etc.).

Out of scope: changing the bundle output shape.

title: kenning: optimize normalize_ocr_form for large source bodies
description:
Surfaced by Gemini round-5 review on PR #53. The current normalize_ocr_form implementation calls s.replace() repeatedly to apply each ligature mapping. For a typical OCR'd source body (~10-100 MB) with ~30 OE-ligature mappings, this allocates 30 copies of the string per scan — hundreds of MB to several GB of allocation on a single source.

The hot path is:
- _scan_etymon_text_match_for_years (the existing wyrd-3ux scanner): one normalize_ocr_form call per source file (5298 etymon_text_match rows ÷ ~50 sources = ~100 calls per ingest, but each one scans a multi-MB body).
- reverse_search_attestations: same pattern.
- fuzzy_search_attestations: same pattern.

Optimization options (pick one):

1. Build a single str.translate table from the single-char mappings (æ→ae, ð→d, etc.) and a precompiled regex for multi-char ones. One pass over the body, no intermediate copies.
2. Move normalization off the hot path: normalize at indexing time (when the source is first read into memory) and cache, OR normalize only the relevant ±N-char window around each form match instead of the whole body.
3. Add a benchmark target so the perf claim is concrete before making the change. On the canonical corpus today, ingest-side normalize_ocr_form is the only normalize site that matters; benchmark it directly.

Acceptance:
- Function output is bit-identical to current behaviour on a corpus of test inputs (existing tests cover this).
- Benchmark shows >=2x speedup on a 50 MB OCR body.
- Memory peak during ingest of a 100 MB source drops measurably (RSS or tracemalloc snapshot).

Out of scope for this ticket: refactoring the call sites that consume normalized output.

title: bridge_inflected_celtic: handle Irish inflected forms (genitive/dative/eclipsis) in place-name etymons
description:
Diagnostic on 2026-05-03 (post wyrd-083 merge): 936 'celtic' place-name etymons remain unbridged after wyrd-083 normalized the lemma forms. Top high-witness misses are dominated by INFLECTED Irish forms — wyrd-083 only matched canonical-form lemmas, so genitive/dative/eclipsed forms are passed over.

Top high-witness celtic unbridged (sources count):
  choill (5) — gen of coill 'wood'
  drum (4) — Anglicized of druim 'ridge'
  kin (4) — Anglicized of cinn (gen of ceann 'head')
  fearna (3) — gen of fearn 'alder'
  gcorr (3) — eclipsis of corr 'crane' (negation/dative trigger)
  cluana (3) — gen of cluain 'meadow'
  gamh (3), eudan (3), clar (3), lough (3), gag (3), monach (3), tulaigh (3),
  ath (3), thairbh (2 — gen of tarbh 'bull'), tigh (2 — gen of teach 'house'),
  raithne (2), līn (2), duin (2), turlach (2), maigh (2 — gen of magh 'plain'), ...

This is HARDER than wyrd-083/ft3:
- Same-form lookup doesn't work — need to compute the lemma form from the inflected form
- Irish inflection rules are complex (eclipsis, lenition, vowel mutation, syncope)
- Anglicization adds another layer (Anglicized 'kin' for Irish 'cinn')

Implementation options:
A) Hand-curated inflection table: ~150-300 high-witness pairs derived from the unbridged set + scholar references. Like wyrd-ft3 but bigger because Irish inflection is more productive.
B) LLM-disambiguated: for each unbridged celtic form, ask an LLM to identify the lemma + Wiktionary canonical (similar pattern to wyrd-uct / wyrd-6z7 fuzzy disambiguator).
C) Sound-change rules library (wyrd-4i6) — proper inverse-phonological transforms. Most general but most expensive to build.

Probably best: start with option A on the top-50 high-witness, evaluate yield, then escalate to B or C if there's a long tail worth chasing.

Defer until wyrd-fkg (ON bridge) and the OE bridge expansion ship — those are mechanical applications of the proven wyrd-ft3 pattern. The celtic case needs a new design.

Acceptance:
- Either implementation A delivers ≥75% bridge-rate on the top-100 high-witness inflected forms, OR a design doc explains why option B/C is the better path forward
- Tests + CLI in line with wyrd-ft3 / wyrd-fkg patterns

title: Wiktionary corpus expansion: ingest more language slices toward full-corpus coverage
description:
Current Wiktionary corpus state (post-wyrd-c9t/223/prv overnight ingest, 2026-05-03):
- 30 language slices ingested across all major IE branches (Germanic, Celtic, Romance, Iranian, Indic, Tocharian, Slavic, Armenian, Greek)
- 731K etymons total, 424K in cognate clusters across 57K cluster roots
- 794K descent edges
- 1130 distinct languages (mostly leaves grown via UPSERT side-effect from descendants)
- Cross-source bridge to place-name dictionaries: 18.2% (limited by structural gaps in wyrd-083/wyrd-ft3, NOT slice count)

Full corpus stats (per kaikki.org):
- raw-wiktextract-data.jsonl.gz: 2.6 GB compressed (22 GB uncompressed)
- ~10M entries total (vs ~270K we've ingested)
- 4000+ distinct languages (vs ~1130 in current DB)
- Estimated DB growth: 190 MB → 7-8 GB (well within 597 GB free)
- Estimated ingest time: ~3 hours wall clock + minutes for cluster pass

Reasons NOT to do full corpus yet (deferred until after wyrd-083 + wyrd-ft3):
1. Diminishing returns for British place-name etymology — Tagalog/Kazakh/Mandarin/Swahili expand graph laterally without strengthening the IE chains we care about
2. Coverage gap is structural (celtic generic-language + OE phonological), not slice-count
3. Cluster-pollution risk at 4000+ languages: more weird-borrowing edges (Hawaiian kaona → English town already snuck in)
4. Etymology quality varies wildly across Wiktionary — long-tail languages have stub entries with no etymology_templates
5. OCR-normalize at 8M etymons with form-only normalization could produce false-positive merges across unrelated languages
6. Source attribution: all wiktextract under single 'wiktionary' source; at 8M entries this becomes useless attribution — need per-language source rows first
7. Maintenance burden: Wiktionary updates continuously, periodic re-ingest is real ops cost

Reasons TO do full corpus eventually:
1. wyrd-7tz cross-cultural rendering ('render this name in <any-language> register') wants the whole graph
2. wyrd-jxr MCP exposure — more complete graph = more useful 'cognates of X across all families' query
3. One-and-done > incremental slice management
4. Validation completeness for the parser

When ready (post wyrd-083 + wyrd-ft3 implementation):

Phase A: Pull slices for missing major branches (haven't done yet):
- Modern English (2.9 GB — needs careful disk planning)
- Modern French (510 MB)
- Modern German (992 MB)
- Modern Italian (668 MB)
- Spanish (919 MB)
- Catalan (215 MB)
Total ~5.3 GB additional sources. Each ingests cleanly with current parser.

Phase B (optional): Full raw-wiktextract-data.jsonl.gz pull + ingest. Pre-work needed:
- Per-language source rows (replace single 'wiktionary' attribution)
- Verify OCR-normalize pass scales without false positives at 8M etymons
- Consider cluster-pollution mitigations (confidence scoring on borrowing edges from low-edited languages)

Acceptance criteria (for this ticket as written):
- Phase A complete: all major modern IE languages ingested
- Cross-source coverage measured pre/post wyrd-083 + wyrd-ft3 land
- Decision recorded (DECISIONS.md update?) on whether to proceed to Phase B

title: OE place-name forms vs Wiktionary canonicals: phonological-similarity bridge (ton vs tūn)
description:
Discovered during 2026-05-03 wiktextract ingest: 130 place-name OE etymons (ton, lea, cote, burgh, dale, ey, ingas, ...) have no synset cluster despite their Wiktionary equivalents being present (tūn, lēah, cot, burh, dæl, īeg, -ingas).

The mismatch is NOT macron-strip OCR (normalize-ocr correctly handles macrons). It's vowel-weakening over time: scholars writing 'ton' in place-name etymologies reference the same morpheme as OE *tūnaz, but the modern (Middle English-influenced) reflex is 'ton', not 'tūn'.

Examples of the unbridged pairs:
  ton ↔ tūn      (vowel weakening ū → o)
  lea ↔ lēah     (æ-loss + macron strip)
  cote ↔ cot     (silent-e ME modernization)
  burgh ↔ burh   (Anglo-Norman gh spelling)
  dale ↔ dæl     (æ → a + silent-e)
  ey ↔ īeg       (palatalisation collapse)
  ingas ↔ -ingas (hyphen-prefix difference)

Fix: phonological-similarity matcher specific to OE → ME → modern English vowel/consonant shifts. Could be:
- Hand-mapped suffix table (-ge → -ey, -gh → -h, -e suffix drop, etc.)
- LLM-disambiguated for ambiguous cases (similar to wyrd-uct / wyrd-6z7 fuzzy disambiguator)
- Just a hand-curated bridge file for the 100ish high-witness OE place-name forms

Probably best: hand-mapped table for the 100-200 most common pairs, since the corpus of OE place-name elements is bounded.

Acceptance: post-implementation, OE place-name forms like 'ton'/'lea'/'cote' appear in clusters with their wiktionary canonical counterparts. Coverage of OE place-name etymons with synset_id rises substantially.

Out of scope: similar issue in Norman-French / Latin (smaller corpus, fewer hits).

title: wiktextract ingester: extend template kind support (compound, prefix, suffix, af, root, etymon, dercat)
description:
During PR #41 live ingest 2026-05-03, OE slice (66K entries) reported 12,299 unsupported_templates. Top kinds in the unsupported set:

- compound (1431) — compound formation, should map to edge_type='compound' in etymon_descent
- af (2573) — affix formation
- prefix (1212) + suffix (881) — affix formation, should also map to 'compound' or 'derivation'
- com (936) — abbreviation of compound
- pre (317) + suf (570) — abbreviations of prefix/suffix
- dercat (822) — derivation category, has args like {1: this_lang, 2: parent_lang, 3: cousin_lang, 'inh': '1'} — when 'inh' flag is set, treat like {{inh}}
- root (500) — PIE root reference, similar shape to {{inh}} with {1: this_lang, 2: 'ine-pro', 3: '*root'}
- etymon (421) — generic etymon ref
- glossary (376) — formatting only, skip
- m+ (73) — variant of mention, skip
- noncog (51) — explicit non-cognate, skip
- unk (76) — unknown origin marker, skip

Recommended:
- compound, com, prefix, pre, suffix, suf, af → edge_type='compound' (D27 has this as a valid type but it's not in the bridging set, so won't bridge synsets — appropriate)
- root → edge_type='inheritance' (PIE root is a real ancestor)
- dercat with inh=1 → edge_type='inheritance'
- etymon → edge_type='derivation' (weakest signal)
- glossary, m+, noncog, unk → add to _SKIPPED_TEMPLATE_NAMES

Estimated additional edges: ~6,000 from the OE slice alone (compound + prefix + suffix + root + dercat). Across all language slices probably 50K+.

This is purely additive: extending the maps, no logic change. Adding the test fixture is the bulk of the work.

Acceptance criteria:
- _UPWARD_TEMPLATE_TO_EDGE extended for root, dercat (when inh flag present)
- New _COMPOUND_TEMPLATE_NAMES set or similar covering compound/prefix/suffix/af + abbreviations
- _SKIPPED_TEMPLATE_NAMES extended with glossary, m+, noncog, unk

title: Re-mine d'Arbois 1890 after attested_year range widens (wyrd-z56) — recover Roman-era rejections
description:

The first d'Arbois pass (wyrd-cmz, closed) rejected 71 entries on attested_year_out_of_range (39) and attested_year_not_int (32) because the validator's 800-floor cuts pre-Carolingian dates that d'Arbois cites routinely (Roman charters, Gaulish gentilice formations, Merovingian foundation dates).

title: etymon_citation: future re-mine could create duplicate (etymon, source, NULL) row alongside backfilled (etymon, source, page) row
description:
From PR #36 review: the unique index is etymon_citation(etymon_id, source_id, COALESCE(page, '')). After wyrd-azv backfills page='15' on an existing row, a future re-mine via add_citation() (which always passes page=None) would insert a NEW row at (etymon, source, NULL) without conflicting — splitting the same evidence into two citation rows.

Possible fixes (not blocking on v1):
1. Have add_citation() check for any existing (etymon, source) row first and skip if one exists.
2. Or have the mining writer pass a page=NULL with INSERT OR IGNORE that treats any existing row as the de-dup target (would need ON CONFLICT clause restructure).
3. Or document that re-mining should always run backfill-pages immediately after.

Affects: wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon.py add_citation; wyrd/generators/kenning/data/lexicon.sql idx_etymon_citation_unique.

title: Backfill: ambiguous_match counter when source_quote could match multiple body positions
description:
From PR #36 review: backfill_citation_pages uses str.find which always returns the leftmost match. If a stock phrase ('See Plate III.') happens to appear in multiple entries, the page silently resolves to the first occurrence — which may not be the entry the citation actually came from.

Acceptable for v1 because:
- Real source_quote excerpts are 200-500 chars and tend to be entry-unique
- Misattribution is to a NEARBY page (citations cluster by alphabet), not a random page
- Better to have an approximately-correct page than NULL

Future improvement: count matches up front, increment ambiguous_match when n>1, and either pick the first / log to a separate audit table / require disambiguation. Per D24 the count should land in a queryable column or audit row, not stdout-only.

Code pointer: wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon.py _resolve_page inner function.

title: Widen attested_year validator range to capture Roman/Gaulish-period citations (currently 800-1700)
description:
The D5-1 attested_year validator (in llm_extractor.py: _ATTESTED_YEAR_MIN=800, _ATTESTED_YEAR_MAX=1700) was sized for British/Continental Norman-era place-names (Domesday 1086 onward). On Roman/Gaulish-period sources like d'Arbois 1890 'Recherches sur l'origine de la propriété foncière (période celtique et période romaine)', the 800-floor blocks legitimate Roman-empire and Frankish-era citations.

Concrete: d'Arbois 1890 smoke (30 entries) yielded 12 accepted but 8 rejected, with rejection reason counts: attested_year_out_of_range=8, attested_year_not_int=10. Multiple rejections per entry. The 'out_of_range' rejections are losing legitimate Roman charters (e.g. 'une charte de l'année 786' would land < 800). The 'not_int' rejections are model emitting strings like '856 (?)' rather than integers — separate bug, see below.

Proposed:
1. Widen _ATTESTED_YEAR_MIN from 800 to 100 — covers Roman empire, Visigothic, early Merovingian. Below 100 is still too noisy (folio numbers and page numbers crash into legitimate range).
2. Tighten the SYSTEM_PROMPT 'attested_forms' section to emphasize INTEGER format — current prompt says 'integer 800-1700' in the schema example but apparently models still emit strings like '856 (?)' or '856 ca.'. Add an explicit example: WRONG: {form: 'X', year: '856 (?)'}. RIGHT: {form: 'X', year: 856}.
3. Update tests to cover the new range bounds (100 floor + 99 below boundary).
4. After the change merges, re-mine d'Arbois 1890 (idempotent, cheap) to recover the rejected Roman-period rows.

Ownership: extractor-layer (validator + prompt) is in the research-thread Claude's territory per the 2026-05-02 division. Companion tests in tests/test_kenning_llm_extractor.py.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- The cap stays at 1700 (post-Restoration sources are likely citing publication years, not attestation years).
- Per-source range overrides (would add complexity for a single use case).
close_reason: Merged in PR #42 (squash 3ca119b). Widened _ATTESTED_YEAR_MIN from 800 to 100 to capture Roman-era / early-Merovingian dated attestations on Romance-Celtic-substrate sources. SYSTEM_PROMPT tightened with explicit RIGHT/WRONG examples for JSON-integer-not-string year format. 466 tests pass; ruff clean; CI green; loop converged in 1 round (agents clean, Gemini rate-limited but no actionable feedback).

title: Tier-2 review candidate query: include Haiku-Tier-1 rows for non-Celtic books
description:
The 'wyrd kenning lexicon review --provider gemini' command filters its candidate query to provider='ollama' rows (per INGESTION.md Stage 5 'review path's candidate query specifically targets Ollama-tagged rows'). This was correct when D2/D13 framed the matrix as:
- English: Qwen Tier-1 -> Gemini Tier-2 review
- Celtic: Haiku Tier-1 (already strong); skip Tier-2

But the matrix has evolved: some non-Celtic books are now Haiku-Tier-1 because the content shape benefits from it (Bannister 1916 Welsh-Marches NF, Harrison 1898 Liverpool, etc.). Those books currently miss Tier-2 review entirely — Gemini's hedge-recognition advantage (D14) doesn't reach them.

Proposed scope:
1. Extend the candidate query to ALSO include Haiku-Tier-1 rows where the source's primary language is in (old-english, modern-english, norman-french, mixed). Identifying the source language could come from the source row metadata or a per-source policy table.
2. Default behavior on existing English-Qwen books unchanged.
3. Behavior on pure Celtic books (Joyce, Watson, Gillies, Macbain) unchanged — still skip Haiku rows.
4. Add a per-source override flag if the heuristic is wrong: 'wyrd kenning lexicon review --include-haiku --book <id>'.

Out of scope:
- A 'rerun-Haiku-with-different-prompt' loop. That's a separate refactor.

Why now: filed as part of the 2026-05-02 mining_run audit pass. Bannister 1916 (35% Haiku accept) and Harrison 1898 (37% Haiku accept) are both candidates to benefit. Filed alongside wyrd-??? (Bannister review) which can either run after this fix or before via a per-source override.

See /tmp/wyrd-corpus-research-2026-05-02.md for the audit summary.
notes: Closed 2026-05-05. The --include-haiku flag (PR #66) shipped and was empirically validated by 13 successful Tier-2 review runs in this session, adding +212 Gemini-tagged toponym_etymology rows across 8 non-Celtic + 7 Celtic + 1 Watson-haiku books. Per-book accept rates are now documented in INGESTION.md. Original goal (unblock wyrd-nl6 / wyrd-1ze) achieved.

title: Investigate Harrison 1898 Liverpool 33% rejection rate (Haiku Tier-1)
description:
Harrison 1898 Liverpool was mined Tier-1 Haiku and shows an anomalous rejection-rate profile: 56 rejected / 170 parsed = 33% reject. Normal band per INGESTION.md is 5-15%; >=25% means investigate.

For comparison, Skeat 1904 Hertfordshire (already noted in INGESTION.md as a format-anomaly outlier) is at 26% reject. Harrison is even worse.

Diagnostic order:
1. Check rejection_reasons distribution: SELECT by_failure_json FROM mining_run WHERE source_id='harrison_1898_liverpool';
2. Sample 10 rejected rows; check whether the rejected forms are (a) OCR-garbled but legitimate (book-side issue) or (b) hallucinated by the model (model-side issue).
3. If (a), the form-in-body validator is correctly rejecting OCR-garbled forms — no fix; the book is partial-loss and we accept the corpus contribution we already have.
4. If (b), investigate prompt regression on this content shape; possibly retry with stronger prompt + Gemini review.

NOT a candidate for blind re-pass: a different model on the same OCR'd body will likely produce the same rejection profile.

Re-pass would only help if the 33% reject is model-overreach rather than book-side OCR damage. Diagnose first.
notes: Closed 2026-05-05. Harrison 1898 Liverpool Tier-2 Gemini review ran via the wyrd-eca --include-haiku flag: 22 reviewed, 8 written, 12 declined, 2 rejected. 36% Gemini-on-Haiku accept rate. Net +8 Gemini-tagged rows. The original 33% rejection-rate diagnostic concern (Tier-1 Haiku) didn't propagate into Tier-2 — Gemini's hedge-recognition didn't flag a content-shape problem. Closing without a fix; the 33% Tier-1 reject rate is bounded by the 67% accept rate which already gave the corpus 56 toponym_etymology rows.

title: Run Gemini Tier-2 review on Bannister 1916 Herefordshire (Haiku Tier-1 single-pass)
description:
Bannister 1916 Herefordshire was mined Tier-1 Haiku (per D13, NF/Welsh-Marches content) and shipped in PR #22. Audit shows 35% accept rate (81/230), 22 medium-confidence rows, and 123 declines. No Tier 2 has run.

(a) Run review with a per-source override that includes Haiku-mined rows, OR
(b) Wait for the structural fix (separate ticket) and revisit.

Option (a) is the immediate path. Per D14 the Tier-2 review's value is recovering hedged-etymology rows that Tier 1 declined — Bannister has 123 declines, of which a chunk are likely hedge-shaped ('possibly from', 'perhaps a corruption of') that the Haiku prompt declined too eagerly.

Cost: ~15 minutes Gemini Flash, well under $1.

Acceptance: post-review witness counts on the Welsh-Marches NF morpheme set increase by N>=10. NF lemmas at >=2 witnesses (currently 7 pre-Bannister) hopefully tick up after the review pass adds Bannister's hedged-etymology rows as parallel witness rows.

title: Probe Joret 1881 Bessin etymological dictionary section (NF source candidate)
description:
Joret 1881 'Essai sur le patois Normand du Bessin; suivi d'un dictionnaire étymologique'. Title's 'suivi d'un dictionnaire étymologique' is real — preface + addenda confirm an alphabetical glossary section. Initial OCR fetch caught only the front phonological essay; the back-half dictionary structure is title-confirmed but not body-density-confirmed yet.

Source: archive.org/details/essaisurlepatois00joreuoft (222 pages, full DJVU TXT)

Smoke-test the DICTIONARY portion (find where the phonological essay ends and the alphabetical section begins) before committing to a full mining pass. If body density is acceptable, proceed Tier-1 Haiku per D13 (Romance content; Norman dialect).

Importance: Channel Islands NF probe was confirmed barren in PD window (Le Maistre 1966 not PD until ~2036+). Joret 1881 is the ONLY remaining direct Norman-French dialect dictionary candidate among PD sources. Combined with Bannister 1916 (Welsh-Marches NF, already shipped per PR #22), this would close out wyrd-hub's PD coverage.

See /tmp/wyrd-corpus-research-2026-05-02.md for the wyrd-hub status update.
notes:
2026-05-03 (research session): Probed sources/joret_1881_patois_normand_bessin.txt (fetched from IA: archive.org/details/essaisurlepatois00joreuoft, 222 pages). Parser found 79 entries from the alphabetical dictionary section.

CRITICAL finding: Joret 1881 is a NORMAN DIALECT word-dictionary, NOT a toponymic dictionary. Sample entries:
- 'Etande, v. a. : étendre. R, extendere.' (Norman 'étende' ← Latin extendere)
- 'Foche, fouache, s. f. : petit pain au beurre. R. focacia.' (Norman dialect word for a pastry)
- 'FoRTEUNE, s. f. : fortune, richesse. R. fortuna.' (Norman form of 'fortune')

The 'suivi d'un dictionnaire étymologique' from the title is etymology of DIALECT WORDS, not place-names. The original wyrd-hub framing assumed it was toponym-shaped because the book covers Bessin (a Norman region), but Joret was doing dialectology, not onomastics.

Pipeline mismatch identical to Troude 1876 / Le Gonidec / Châlons-Loth — language dictionaries fit the wyrd-4rt Wiktionary-style ingestion path (entry → standalone etymon row), not the existing mine-llm path (toponym → etymology breakdown).

For NF expansion (wyrd-hub) this means:
- The Joret 1881 candidate doesn't yield through the existing mining pipeline.
- Bessin-area NF is still likely the strongest geographic angle — needs a TOPONYMIC source. Possible alternatives to probe: a Bessin/Caen-area cartulaire, Beaurepaire's Normandy place-name studies (1830s-1850s, PD), or a département-toponymique like Joret might list separately.
- After wyrd-4rt's Wiktionary pipeline lands, Joret 1881's 79 dialect entries become directly mineable for Norman-French word morphemes (relevant to wyrd-fmg breton + norman expansion).

Closing as 'probe complete, defer mining until pipeline support'.
close_reason: Probe complete: Joret 1881 is a Norman DIALECT word-dictionary, not toponymic. Pipeline-mismatch — needs wyrd-4rt-style language-dictionary ingestion, not the existing mine-llm toponym path. Source fetched + characterized; 79 entries available for the Wiktionary-style pipeline when it lands. Bessin area still strongest NF angle; needs different source.

Source: archive.org/details/dictionnairebre00unkngoog (614 pages, full DJVU TXT)

title: Wire D5: (language × era) era-aware register cells
description:
DECISIONS.md D5 promises any (language × era) cell — Old English at ~900 AD = Hædan-tūn; Old English modernized = Hadenham; Latin at empire = Pons Aquae. Currently the runtime has only the (language) axis; era is implicit in the morpheme set, no cells.

This is the biggest scope of the chain. Probably wants a separate epic.

Scope (rough):
1. Era tagging on etymons in the lexicon (pre-1066, Domesday, late-medieval, early-modern, modern). Mining-time field from the source's date or the form's expected period.
2. Per-(language × era) sub-proportions: language alone today, language × era after.
3. Phonology: era-specific orthography rules (OE ƿ vs w, modern-English collapse rules).
4. Sound-change rules library (separate ticket wyrd-4i6) is the engine for converting between era cells.
5. CLI / API: 'wyrd kenning generate english --era 900' or '--era pre-1066'.

Acceptance: at default (modern era), behavior unchanged; user can request a specific era and get morphemes drawn from that period.

Caveat: substantial work. May want to split into (a) era tagging on etymons (data), (b) era-aware proportions (sampling), (c) era-aware orthography (surface form), (d) cross-era sound-change rules — separate tickets.
notes:
2026-05-02 update (research session): Architecture design + epic split filed. Per the prior handoff's 'probably wants splitting into 3-4 tickets' note, decomposed D5 into 4 layers:

- wyrd-3ux (D5-1): Mine attested years from source bodies via regex post-mining stage. Foundation. Adds attested_year column to etymon_text_match. LLM-free, idempotent, reversible.
- wyrd-38d (D5-2): Era-cell mapping + filtered sampling on (language × era) axis. Defines era cells per family + --era CLI/JSON param that filters morpheme inventory. Depends on D5-1.
- wyrd-lyp (D5-3): Era-aware bundle export + runtime cell selection. Adds <lang>_era arrays per D26; wires Meaning.pick_era_form. Depends on D5-2.
- wyrd-4i6 (D5-4 = pre-existing): Cross-era sound-change rules library. Independent of D5-1/2/3. Required only for 'Old English modernized'-style rule-based surface derivation; D5-1+2+3 ship era axis WITHOUT it (era-attested-only forms).

Approach choice for v1: Layer-2 path (c) — era is a generation-time FILTER on morpheme inventory; tag-co-occurrence stays per-culture (existing proportions JSONs unchanged). Cheaper than per-(lang × era) tag-co-occurrence; ships immediately on D5-1 data. Per-era tag-co-occurrence is v2.

Open questions (see design doc):
1. Era cell granularity (proposed 4-5 cells per family) — confirm
2. Era as separate axis vs language-enum split — confirmed separate axis (preserves D8 lemma identity)
3. Year-extraction prompt vs regex — regex (path C) for v1, prompt re-mining deferred
4. Default era on no '--era' flag — keep current bit-stable behavior
5. Bundle size — ~30-50KB extra, negligible
6. celtic enum sub-division (Brythonic vs Goidelic era cells differ) — open

Full design rationale, layer-by-layer trade-offs, PD source survey for D5-4 sound-change rules, and risk register in /tmp/wyrd-d5-era-axis-design-2026-05-02.md.

title: Norman-French corpus expansion: Channel Islands + EPNS Southern-county targeting
description:
Norman-French is the thinnest mined language (111 lemmas at >=1 witness, only 7 at >=2, 2 at >=3). The structural reason is corpus availability — most modern Norman-French scholarship is post-WW2 and still in copyright. Two PD-friendly directions:

(a) Channel Islands toponymy: Jersey, Guernsey, Sark were the closest English-controlled territory and retained Norman dialect into the 20th century. PD scholarship from the Société Jersiaise / Société Guernesiaise era (early 1900s) likely covers Channel Islands place names. Need to probe for what's been digitized (Internet Archive, archive.org/details/jersey, etc.).

(b) EPNS Southern-county volumes with heavier Norman strata: Sussex (already partial via mawer_stenton_1930_sussex + roberts_1914_sussex), plus Kent, Hampshire, and East Anglia. Norman conquest impact peaked in the South-East; OE-county dicts under-weight that layer.

Suggested first steps: (i) probe Channel Islands archive.org for PD place-name dictionaries (Yves Falla, J. Le Maistre, etc.), (ii) check which EPNS Sussex/Kent/Hampshire/East-Anglian volumes are PD (1928 cutoff plus author-death rules), (iii) mine via Tier-1 Haiku per D13 if Celtic-French boundary content, otherwise Qwen.

Surfaced when discussing PR #15 (per-language witness thresholds): NF gets only +4 words moving from uniform-3 to the recommended preset because the population at w>=2 is already exhausted at 7 lemmas. Threshold can't help; need more sources.
notes:
2026-05-02 update (research session): Channel Islands NF probe is structurally barren in PD window — ALREADY confirmed in prior wyrd-hub note (Carey 1904, Ansted 1893, Berry 1815, Société Jersiaise Bulletins were all essay/travelogue). Frank Le Maistre's foundational 1966 Dictionnaire Jersiais-Français is not PD until ~2036+ per UK life+70.

NEW finding (research probe): Joret 1881 'Essai sur le patois Normand du Bessin; suivi d'un dictionnaire étymologique' (archive.org/details/essaisurlepatois00joreuoft, 222 p) — has an etymological dictionary section per title + addenda. Filed as wyrd-8m9. Smoke-test the dictionary section (after the front phonological essay) before committing to a full mining pass.

Combined with Bannister 1916 (Welsh-Marches NF, already shipped per PR #22), Joret 1881 closes out wyrd-hub's PD source coverage. Channel Islands direction should be considered closed; Welsh-Marches + Bessin are the surviving PD angles for NF expansion.

Full context in /tmp/wyrd-corpus-research-2026-05-02.md.

title: export-meanings: narrow per-reflex language arrays via reflex_etymon links
description:
In wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon.py:_build_words_for_group, every reflex's word entry currently uses the subject-wide combined_forms across all families in the group. That's too wide: a reflex like '-don' should only carry the etymons it's actually linked to via reflex_etymon (here: 'dun'), not also celtic_mix forms from a sibling reflex like 'Bre-' that lives under the same Hill subject.

Per the original meanings.json shape (e.g. the 'Alder tree' subject), each word's language slots are reflex-specific — '-farne' has only celtic_mix; 'Alder-' has only old_english; 'Orle-' has both. seed_from_meanings preserves this via per-(reflex,etymon) links in reflex_etymon.

The right fix is per-reflex etymon lookup: for each reflex R seen in the subject, find R's directly-linked etymons via reflex_etymon, roll each to its family root, and emit only those families' forms grouped by language. Synthesized words (families without any reflex) keep their own forms_by_lang only.

Why deferred: this requires restructuring _gather_family or _build_words_for_group to thread reflex_links through. Functionally the runtime decomposer/generator works either way — the over-wide language arrays only affect explanation prose (a generated '-don' name's explanation might claim celtic origins it doesn't have). Cosmetic v1 issue; tracked here to fix when the lemma+variants weighting refactor lands.

Surfaced by Gemini in PR #14 review (comment 3176293576): https://github.com/521-studios/wyrd/pull/14#discussion_r2710906366
close_reason: Fixed in PR #14 round-2 (commit f07d23f). _gather_family collects per-reflex linked etymon ids + member descendants; _build_words_for_group walks each reflex's linked etymons + their D8/D22 descendants only. Verified: production export shows 'Sel-' explainer goes from (EN/CL Seal) to (EN Seal) — false Celtic attribution gone. Regression test test_export_meanings_narrows_word_language_to_linked_etymons. 0 coverage regressions vs bundled meanings.json.

title: LLM disambiguator: group ambiguous rows by (source_id, matched_form) to dedupe LLM calls
description:
Follow-up to wyrd-6z7. find_ambiguous_rows currently returns one AmbiguityCase per etymon_text_match row, so when multiple fuzzy rows share the same (source_id, matched_form) — same body word, different originally-matched etymons — the disambiguator asks the LLM the same question multiple times.

Fix: group fuzzy rows by (source_id, matched_form) before constructing AmbiguityCase. Each case holds a list of text_match_ids to be updated/deleted together. apply_disambiguator_result becomes apply_disambiguator_result_for_group and writes the verdict to all rows in the group.

Acceptance: a regression test with two fuzzy rows for the same body word in the same source (different originally-matched etymons) results in one LLM call and a consistent verdict applied to both rows.

title: LLM disambiguator: agentic expand_context tool-call loop
description:
Follow-up to wyrd-6z7. The disambiguator currently uses a fixed snippet window. Per the wyrd-6z7 NOTES section, the model should be able to request more context when the initial snippet isn't sufficient.

Architecture: tool-call style with two tools: expand_context(direction, chars) and commit_answer(choice, confidence, reason). Orchestrator runs the conversation loop, capping at 3 expansion rounds or 2000 chars total.

Acceptance: a test case where the first 200 chars is genuinely ambiguous but the next 300 chars resolves it; disambiguator should request expansion and arrive at the correct answer.

title: [bug] Tier-2 review 'written' summary includes silently-dropped low-conf rows
description:
cli.py:1118-1120 increments counts['written'] for every accepted Gemini result, but ingest_parsed_entries in lexicon.py:1394 silently drops entries with confidence='low' (returns without inserting). Result: summary line claims more rows persisted than actually exist in DB.

Concrete example (2026-05-02): Ekwall 1922 Tier-2 review summary said 'written: 149', actual gemini rows in toponym_etymology for that source: 53. Discrepancy: 96 low-conf Gemini extractions silently dropped.

Fix options: (a) have ingest_parsed_entries return per-entry persistence status so cli.py can count accurately; (b) raise the writer's skip-low to a click.echo so it's visible; (c) check entry.confidence in cli.py before calling ingest_parsed_entries.

Not urgent — the silent drop is a sensible quality gate. Bug is in the *reporting*, not the data integrity. mining_run audit table reflects the inflated 'accepted' count too (D23), so any downstream stats should be aware.

title: Canonical-group rollup views for etymon_gloss, etymon_tag, etymon_text_match
description:
Why this exists:

After D22's non-destructive OCR clustering landed (wyrd-et0), glosses, tags, and text-match evidence stay attached to their original (loser) etymons rather than being moved to the canonical winner. The etymon_consensus view rolls up citations correctly via merged_into_id chains, but there is no equivalent rollup view for the other three child tables.

A direct SELECT against etymon_gloss / etymon_tag / etymon_text_match scoped to a canonical etymon's id will miss data attached to its merged tombstones. Compared to the previous destructive model where data was moved to the winner, this is a regression in 'what does this canonical etymon know?' visibility.

Flagged by Gemini in PR #7 review (https://github.com/521-studios/wyrd/pull/7).

What needs to be done:

Three new views, each unioning rows on the canonical-group rollup chain (the same COALESCE(merged_into_id, lemma_id, id) that etymon_consensus uses):

- etymon_gloss_canonical(canonical_etymon_id, gloss) DISTINCT
- etymon_tag_canonical(canonical_etymon_id, tag) DISTINCT
- etymon_text_match_canonical(canonical_etymon_id, source_id, matched_form, total_match_count, ...) — note the SUM aggregation for match_count parallels D21's UPSERT semantics

Audit existing direct queries against the underlying tables (the diagnostic SQL in INGESTION.md, the fuzzy-search EXISTS check in lexicon.py, any future report builders) and migrate them to read through the canonical views where the consumer wants 'all data for this canonical etymon, including from its merged variants.'

Acceptance:
- Three views created via migrate_schema (idempotent, recreated like etymon_consensus).
- Tests verify rollup correctness when an etymon has merged variants with their own glosses/tags/text-match rows.
- INGESTION.md's diagnostic queries updated to use the new views.
- No production code reads the underlying tables in a way that misses data attached to merged variants.

Soft prereq: wyrd-et0 (this PR).

title: Refactor cluster_ocr_variants: extract per-table merge logic
description:
Why this exists:

cluster_ocr_variants in wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon.py is now ~120 lines after wyrd-go5's FK fix landed. The apply-phase loop (~76 lines) is a sequence of repetitive INSERT OR IGNORE / UPDATE / DELETE blocks, one per child table that references etymon. The repetition itself was the bug surface for wyrd-go5: when a new child table (etymon_text_match) was added, the merge loop wasn't updated and silently dropped rows.

Flagged by complexity-reviewer on PR #5 (https://github.com/521-studios/wyrd/pull/5).

What needs to be done:

Two viable shapes:
1. Extract a _merge_etymon_into(db, winner_id, loser_id) helper that owns the per-table merge sequence.
2. Build a declarative _ETYMON_CHILD_TABLES dispatch list — each entry names the child table, its UNIQUE-constraint columns, and any 'self-FK' column on etymon — and iterate it. Schema discoverability becomes auditable; future child tables get caught.

Acceptance:
- cluster_ocr_variants main body drops to fit one screen (~50 lines).
- All existing tests still pass; regression coverage from wyrd-go5 still exercises the new helper.
- Adding a hypothetical new child table requires updating one declarative list, not editing the merge loop body.

Likely supersedes interaction with wyrd-et0 — if non-destructive clustering lands, the merge loop becomes much shorter (mark-as-merged via merged_into_id), and this refactor is moot. Keep open as fallback if wyrd-et0 stalls.
close_reason: Obviated by wyrd-et0 (PR #7, commit 64a99c9). The non-destructive merge eliminates the per-table INSERT-OR-IGNORE/DELETE dispatch entirely — cluster_ocr_variants is now ~25 lines of merge logic with two UPDATEs (re-parent lemma children + mark merged_into_id with chain-flatten). No table-list refactor needed.

title: Batch SQL operations in cluster_ocr_variants
description:

Why deferred: cluster_ocr_variants runs occasionally during ingest, not in a hot path. Lexicon currently has ~few-hundred OCR variants tops; the chattiness hasn't caused observable slowdown. Worth doing as a focused optimization PR if/when it becomes a bottleneck.

Per Gemini review on PR #28: when an LLM extractor returns found=False, the assemble_extraction_result decline path stores body[:SOURCE_QUOTE_BUDGET] WITHOUT the notes_prefix attribution. The accepted path includes 'extracted_by:<provider>:<model>' as a prefix; the decline path doesn't. This makes it impossible to distinguish 'Gemini declined this entry' from 'Qwen declined' from 'baseline regex produced no body' when querying the lexicon later.

Current behavior (intentional per the existing test docstring):
  source_quote = body[:SOURCE_QUOTE_BUDGET]

Proposed:
  source_quote = (notes_prefix + ' | ' + body)[:SOURCE_QUOTE_BUDGET]

Trade-off:
- Pro: per-provider attribution on declines enables 'show me all toponyms Gemini Flash declined' queries; helps identify which model is over-declining a given content shape.
- Con: small loss of body context (~30-50 chars consumed by the prefix). The SPA citation view doesn't render decline rows in the same way as accepted rows anyway.
- Con: changes the documented contract on test_assemble_extraction_result_not_found_emits_low_confidence_entry. Update the test + docstring to match.

This is OUT OF SCOPE for PR #28 (which is about budget, not attribution). Filed separately so it's not lost.

See PR #28 comment 3177442609.

title: MCP server: expose wyrd APIs to GMs via Claude / other AI assistants
description:
Wrap the wyrd HTTP API (or core generation functions directly) as an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server so GMs can use Claude / Cursor / other AI assistants to call the generator with rich natural-language constraints.

Use case: GM says to Claude 'give me 10 names for villages in a Norse-influenced coastal region in the 12th century, all with water-related morphemes, presented as a markdown table with pronunciation guides.' Claude calls wyrd's MCP tools to actually generate, then formats as requested.

Tools to expose:
- generate(culture, era, register, tags, count, novelty, seed) → list of structured names with breakdowns
- explain(name) → morpheme decomposition with all matching readings
- convert(name, target_register) → cross-register rendering (when wyrd-4cd ships)
- pronounce(name, language) → respelling + IPA
- lexicon_search(form_or_gloss) → all etymons matching, with citations
- list_pantheons() / get_deity(pantheon, name) → for deity-based naming
- pin_name(name, target_register) → conjugate user-supplied name into register

Architecture options:
1. Python MCP server using the official Python SDK, calls into wyrd's existing generate/explain functions directly (no HTTP). Cleanest for a single-machine GM.
2. HTTP-fronting MCP server that calls the deployed lambda. Useful for multi-user setups.
3. Both (start with 1, add 2 if there's demand).

Distribution: package as 'wyrd-mcp' with an entry point in pyproject.toml, then a GM does:
  pip install wyrd-mcp
  # add to ~/.config/Claude/mcp_servers.json
  # restart Claude
  # GM types: 'generate me 5 elven villages in the Shire'

Killer feature: GM gets fluent natural-language access to a constrained, reproducible generator — Claude handles the parsing of intent, wyrd handles the constrained generation. Better than either alone.

When an agent (Explore, Task, etc.) summarizes mining stats, model performance, or any quantitative claim about the lexicon corpus — OR makes a content-shape verdict on a mining-source candidate (e.g. 'this is essay-shaped / low yield', 'this is a dictionary, will mine well') — ALWAYS verify against actual data before propagating to docs or decisions.

Five documented instances now (and counting):

1. 2026-05-01: a transcript-mining agent reported 'Watson 1904 Haiku 6× yield over Qwen' — actual mining_run data showed Haiku 3% vs Qwen 7% on Watson 1904 (both poor — Watson 1926 is the Haiku-earns-it case at 52%).

2. 2026-05-02: a probe agent verdict on Quilgars 1906 was based on raw OCR keyword counts (dense Plou-/Ker- prefix presence) rather than body content. Reality: 3% accept rate because Quilgars is a topographical (property-record) dictionary, not toponymic etymology.

3. 2026-05-02: prior session called Longnon 1920 and Loth 1890 'essay-shaped, low parser yield' from titles + surface signals. Re-probe found Longnon vol 1 yields 67 parser entries × 24% accept = 16 acc / 27 etymons; Loth 1890 is actually a Middle Breton text anthology where the etymology commentary is a small fraction of bulk. Both initial 'low yield' calls were wrong about the REASON; final yields ended up modest because of structural mismatches the original framing missed.

4. 2026-05-03: Joret 1881 Bessin smoke. Title 'Essai sur le patois Normand du Bessin; suivi d'un dictionnaire étymologique' suggested toponymic etymology but the dictionary section is NORMAN DIALECT WORDS + Latin etymons (Etande ← extendere, Foche ← focacia), not toponymic. Pipeline-mismatched.

5. 2026-05-03: d'Arbois 1890 yield projection. Initial smoke showed 40% accept on first 30 entries; full pass dropped to 10% as later chapters got more abstract. Lesson: smoke-the-FIRST-N is biased because front-matter / dense early chapters / sparse tail aren't uniformly distributed across a 700-page treatise. ALSO: the 800-floor on the attested_year validator (set conservatively for British Norman-period sources) cut 39 legitimate Roman-era citations on this source — fixed via wyrd-z56 widening to 100, recovered 27 rows on re-mine.

Why: agents synthesize from indirect sources; the DB / actual OCR body is the ground truth. Yield projections from prose-density samples consistently diverge from parser-yield at mining time. Validators' default ranges may be miscalibrated for source classes outside their original design context.

How to apply:
- For source-candidate probes: pull the IA *_djvu.txt URL; sample 3-5 contiguous ~500-word excerpts from spaced positions; count named places + explicit etymological links per passage; CONFIRM the parser yield (run _select_parser_and_run); only THEN smoke 30-50 entries via LLM. The parser-yield step is the one most often skipped and most-likely to surprise.
- For corpus-stats claims: run the equivalent SQL against mining_run / toponym_etymology and reconcile; flag and fix any divergence in the agent's prose before using it.
- For VALIDATOR rejection patterns: when rejection counts are dominated by a specific rule (e.g. attested_year_out_of_range), check whether the source class differs from the validator's design context; widening / per-source overrides may recover real data.

waiter-loop-self-reference-bug: When using `until ! pgrep -f "<pattern>"; do sleep 30; done; tail ...` as a background-task waiter, the pgrep itself matches the parent shell's argv (which contains the pattern literally as a string). The until loop then never exits. Three waiters in 2026-05-04/05 spun for 10-12 hours each before the user noticed in the UI. Fix: check by PID instead — capture the target PID first via `P=$(pgrep -f '<pattern>' | head -1)`, then `until ! kill -0 $P 2>/dev/null; do sleep 30; done`. Or just use `run_in_background: true` on the actual command and trust the task-notification system to fire when it exits — don't write waiter loops at all.
